Tested by `sc_questions_grill` and `sc_questions_keys` in `gates-test.sh`. — Rationale (recorded by the author, not stated by the user): a grill is an interview whose next question depends on the last answer, so it cannot be batched, and the user's replies in an interview are the point of it. — Alternatives rejected by the author (not stated by the user): batching the grill's questions and changing fixture EXPECTED P1/P9 (breaks dependency order, the user kept the fixtures); exempting by role (the task author's ordinary round must stay limited); raising the limit (hides the cause). — Limits: the exemption is enforced for the task author role only, through `submit` (architect, data_architect and designer may write under `design/`, so the role is part of the key, tested); rounds are unlimited, not capped, because the interview's length depends on the decision tree and the user's replies bound it; the task author writes `design/INTENT.md` and its `## Status` itself, so a task author that writes `in-progress` there for a non-interview purpose is exempt: a trust convention checked by shape (A75 stops the stub and the other roles, not a deliberate forgery), recorded as residual; a grill with more rounds than the harness reply limit is outside what C-14 counts for that fixture.
### Open technical points — how they were closed

- **User-invoked-only skills in role agents:** verified against the Claude Code docs: a skill with `disable-model-invocation: true` cannot be preloaded or invoked by a subagent, so role definitions point to the skill's SKILL.md path explicitly (A15). Codex reads `.agents/skills/` natively.
- **Platform formats:** verified on 2026-10-09 against code.claude.com docs (plugin, marketplace, subagents, skills, hooks, headless) and Codex 0.162 help output + docs (custom agents in `.codex/agents/*.toml`, skills in `.agents/skills`, hooks in `.codex/hooks.json`, `codex exec` flags). Verified live: PreToolUse input carries `agent_id`/`agent_type` for subagent calls and none for the main session; a PreToolUse deny blocks in `-p` with `bypassPermissions`; SubagentStop context goes to the subagent, so record outcomes are relayed to the lead by its next PostToolUse; Codex project hooks fire and deny. Details: `docs/concepts/enforcement-layers.md`.

- **A94. Review hardening of the skill validators: a check that cannot see the evidence must not pass, and a result the control plane accepts must not be rejected by the lead's parser.** What: an independent review of A78-A90 found validators that accepted a PASS on self-labelled or unverified input. Each fix keeps the evidence classes (measured, reproduced, traced, judged) and adds no role, gate or skill. (1) `skills/proofline-lead/scripts/check-result.mjs` mirrors `agent.sh record_validate`: the reviewer's risk focuses `contract|concurrency|performance|config|migration`, `FOCUS visual` for qa and `dependencies` for security_reviewer are valid, `UNSUPPORTED` is a gate result of a risk focus only (never `dependencies`, an `UNSUPPORTED_REASON` line required, no blocking rows), and the rules-gate focuses accept `REVIEW_RULES-n` or `REVIEW_SMALL-n` row ids because the tier is not known to the parser. (2) contract-proof: `--path` is added to the discovered changed set instead of replacing it; a named path that is not changed against the base, or does not exist, is an `unsupported` row (never `compared` with no changes); a tool in `tools.used` counts only when it is in `tools.detected` (the regenerated report's list when `--repo` is given), left a command naming it and non-empty output, and its `formats` cover the file's format; the plan-coverage negation lexicon gains `n/a`, `w/o`, `out-of-scope`, `as-is`, `impossible`, `later`, `unknown`, `=0`, `: no`; a `oneOf`/`anyOf` whose length changed is compared member by member (removed member `CP-B06` on any side, added member `CP-N03` on the request side and `CP-N04` otherwise) instead of `CP-U01`. (3) data-design: non-SQL migrations (python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, Go, XML, ...) are token scanned by the scanner `classify-migration.mjs` already had (`drop_table`, `drop_column`, `remove_column`, `DropTable`, `op.drop_*`, `schema.dropTable`, SQL string literals); a destructive or unknown action is `not_executable` (A52); a file with run-time built SQL or no recognised operation is listed under `unanalyzed` (and counts as destructive in `classify`), never skipped silently; `validate-migration.mjs` gains `--repo`, re-classifies each cited migration and refuses `destructive: no` on a destructive or unknown action (V16), an applied file the scanner cannot analyze or a cited file that does not exist (V17), and a `patterns: pass` while the scan traces a blocking hazard; with `down_migration: yes` the status can be PASS only when `rollback` is a measured pass (a `warn` or `judged` rollback derives UNSUPPORTED). (4) exploit-proof: unknown manifest names that decide what is installed or from where (`.npmrc`, `.yarnrc`, `packages.config`, `environment.yml`, `deno.json`, `pip.conf`, `nuget.config`, ...) are listed unparsed (confidence low); a lockfile entry with an unchanged version but another resolved host or integrity is a `replaced` change; a plan mention inside a negating clause ("do not add left-pad") no longer declares the dependency (the lexicon is duplicated from contract-proof, skills share no files); with no plan the validator prints `PLAN_CHECK: not_run` and the confidence is `low`, so the `PASS` is `pass_low` and cannot close the gate (the focus has no `UNSUPPORTED` result, A88), while a missing audit tool stays `medium` with the plan check run. `DEPENDENCIES.md` no longer says the audit step uses no network: the skill's scripts make none, the project's own audit tools may. The shipped risk mapping's `dependency_manifest.paths` now lists every manifest and lockfile name the manifest diff reads or lists unparsed (npm-shrinkwrap, requirements variants, `*.versions.toml`, setup.py/cfg, `.npmrc`, `packages.config`, `environment.yml`, `deno.json`, Package.swift, pubspec, Podfile, ...), with a risk-test scenario. (5) proof-review config: a new line is a line the diff added whose text the same diff did not also remove (position, not set membership in the base file), so a flag flipped to `enabled: true` next to an unchanged `enabled: true` is found; a flag is identified by its parent path plus leaf; `validate-config.mjs --repo --base [--plan]` re-runs the scan and rejects a document that dropped or added an item; `--gate REVIEW_RULES|REVIEW_SMALL` sets the row ids (the SKILL no longer hard-codes `REVIEW_RULES`). (6) evidence-map `impact`: `exports.X =`, `module.exports.X =` and `module.exports = { ... }` are declarations; `.vue` and `.svelte` files are code (script blocks lexed as TypeScript, template references count); readable files over 1 MiB are listed under `unknown` `skipped_large` instead of being dropped. (7) ui-design: a redesign approval needs a recorded answer (`questions/NNN.answer.md` or `INTENT.md#anchor`) or a `Q<n>` of the NEEDS_INPUT round that does not sit next to a meeting, review or planning word; "approved in the Q3 planning review" is refused. (8) benchmark: a `EXPECTED.md` with no id-keyed items but a `Traps`, `Planted facts`, `Must hold` or `known answers` heading is read structurally (table rows and bullets, positional ids `F<n>`/`T<n>`), so the contract-proof, impact-map, insights and migration-validation fixtures are measurable without editing their EXPECTED files; prose is still never an item. (9) The `visual_proof:` line is parsed by one rule in plan-contract's and verify-proof's validators (optional bullet plus space, optional backticks), pinned by tests in both. (10) Follow-up of the re-review: negation words inside hyphenated names (`no-case`, `is-not-empty`, `skip-list`) are not negations (the lexicons require the word not to touch `-_/.@`, and the element or package name is removed from the clause first); heredoc and triple-quoted SQL bodies are scanned, and a paren-less or computed `execute`/`raw` argument, or a string that is no SQL statement, makes the file `unanalyzed` even when other known operations are present; only the up path decides `destructive` (a drop on the down path is `down_destructive`, V18, never executed); an unparsed manifest has an exit: a `manual_review` row `{file, note, diff_sha256}` whose hash the validator recomputes with `--repo/--base` lets the result be `PASS` at `medium` (without the recomputation it stays `low`); a redesign approval `Q<n>` needs round wording (a bare quarter label is refused); `validate-migration.mjs` without `--repo` prints a self-attestation warning and `CONFIDENCE: medium`. — Alternatives rejected: **keeping `--path` as a restriction and requiring the validator to catch the omission** (the validator is not run by the control plane, so the differ itself must not hide changes); **running a discovered ORM migration on the throwaway database to "measure" it** (A52: destructive statements are never executed, and a framework we cannot see may do anything); **a numeric weight per hazard** (A91); **making the dependencies focus UNSUPPORTED without a plan** (A88 fixed that the manifest diff always exists, and `agent.sh` rejects it; `pass_low` has the same effect, the gate stays open); **editing the four EXPECTED files to fit the benchmark parser** (the fixture is the source of truth, the parser follows it); **one shared helper for the negation lexicon or the `visual_proof` rule** (skills are standalone, check-shared.sh pins copied sections only). — Limits: the non-SQL scan is a token and string scan, so a migration that builds names or statements from variables is `unanalyzed`, not understood; a vendored or generated migration framework with its own DSL is read only by the tokens above; negation detection is a word list, not parsing; the host and integrity comparison covers npm lockfiles and `yarn.lock`, not the other lockfile formats; `validate-migration.mjs --repo` needs the migration files in the working tree. — `skills/proofline-lead/scripts/check-result.mjs`, `skills/contract-proof/scripts/diff-contract.mjs`, `skills/contract-proof/scripts/validate-contract.mjs`, `skills/data-design/scripts/classify-migration.mjs`, `skills/data-design/scripts/migration-check.mjs`, `skills/data-design/scripts/validate-migration.mjs`, `skills/exploit-proof/scripts/diff-manifests.mjs`, `skills/exploit-proof/scripts/validate-dependencies.mjs`, `skills/proof-review/scripts/check-config.mjs`, `skills/proof-review/scripts/validate-config.mjs`, `skills/evidence-map/scripts/impact.mjs`, `skills/ui-design/scripts/validate-ui.mjs`, `skills/plan-contract/scripts/validate-plan.mjs`, `skills/verify-proof/scripts/validate-verify.mjs`, `tests/benchmark/benchmark.mjs`, `control-plane/agents/config.yaml`, `control-plane/agents/scripts/risk-test.sh`.

- **A97. C-18 and S-6 from the STANDARD round 1 evaluations: shell writes outside the copy are refused by the hook whatever their spelling, and GREEN/REFACTOR evidence needs an earlier RED and a changed implementation.** What: (1) *Hook.* Reading the runs again, the `/tmp/x` commands counted as C-18 breaches (`cat > /tmp/x`, `> /tmp/x`, `npm test > /tmp/x`) were already denied by the A56 guard ("never /tmp/x directly"); the files named in the evaluation (`qa-t1-*.mjs`, `t1-findings.txt`) are dated before A56, from earlier rounds. What the guard still let through was any absolute target that is neither under `/tmp`/`$TMPDIR` nor in the project: `> ~/x`, `> $HOME/x`, `cp f /Users/me/x`, `tee /opt/x` (the run-scoped path policy caught `~` and `$HOME` inside a run, with another message; nothing caught them before a run exists). `scratch_guard` now denies every shell write (redirection, `tee`, `cp`/`mv`/`install`/`rsync`/`ln` targets, `touch`/`rm`/`truncate`, `dd of=`) whose resolved absolute target is outside the project root and the registered worktrees, `/dev/*` excepted (`> /dev/null`, `2>&1`, `>&2`, `/dev/stderr` stay allowed); `~`, `$HOME` and `$TMPDIR` are expanded, `//` and a `/private` prefix normalised. Both stray-path messages now say "Scratch files go under `.agents/runs/<ID>/scratch/` (before a run exists: `.agents/local/scratch/`); only worktrees go under `$TMPDIR`" instead of the older "go under $TMPDIR". The Codex adapter runs the same hook script (`adapters/codex/hooks.json`). Residual (policy-only, in ENFORCEMENT.md): writes the tokenizer cannot see, computed paths, `cd` plus a relative path, a script writing a file by itself; the older raw-text `/tmp` check can still refuse a `/tmp` string inside quotes. GREEN and REFACTOR are refused for a non-exempt target path with no RED record of that path; GREEN is refused while no implementation path (a scope path that is not a test file by name or folder; any path if the scope holds only tests) differs from the snapshot of the latest RED for it; REFACTOR is refused before a GREEN or FIX record. A path with `tdd_exemption` is not held to RED; records without a snapshot (older runs) skip the change check. The evaluated run recorded GREEN-1 and REFACTOR-1 seven seconds before RED-1, so a green was recorded before the fix existed. Why: both findings were made from run records; the first was partly a mis-attribution (denied attempts are not writes) but exposed the real gap above. Because a freeze can no longer record an empty scope, a refreeze never repairs one, so no extra exception to the scope-approval rule is added. - **A98. An UNSUPPORTED check is unproven and reported, not blocking by default; an INCONCLUSIVE measurement still blocks (amends A78, A82, A83, A84, A86, A87).** What: a risk-focus result `UNSUPPORTED` with a non-empty reason and no blocking row is recorded with result `unsupported` (gate record field `unsupported: "<focus>"`, an `info` row `UNSUPPORTED <focus>: <reason>`), so `pipeline` prints `focus.<GATE>.<focus>=unsupported` (never `pass`) and `unsupported.<GATE>:<focus>=UNSUPPORTED (unproven, reported): ...`; the focus counts as satisfied for its gate, so the gate is `pass` when every other focus passes and CODE_DONE is reachable; `next` prints one `UNSUPPORTED (unproven, reported)` line per such focus before CODE_DONE and before the report; the completion report must carry `## Unsupported Checks` with, for every unsupported focus of every required gate, a line naming `<GATE>:<focus>` and `not proven: <what>` (`publish-completion-report` refuses an omission or a line without it; the template shows the line; verify-proof never cites such a focus as proof). Blocking stays where it means something: (1) config `risk.unsupported: block|report` (default `report`, accepted by `config-check`, inside the frozen `risk_sha256`) where `block` restores the A78 rule (blocking row, FAIL, only the user waives it); (2) a reason that starts `<focus> INCONCLUSIVE:` (performance-proof and visual-proof submit their INCONCLUSIVE that way) is blocking in both modes, because a measurement ran and was unreliable and the user must decide; (3) a defect found in the part that could be checked is a FAIL (`--result UNSUPPORTED` still refuses blocking rows; a FAIL that carries UNSUPPORTED rows, the contract-proof shape, keeps them blocking). The `dependencies` focus still refuses UNSUPPORTED. Visibility: `pipeline` adds `gate.<GATE>.unsupported=<focus,...>` under a gate that closes with one, `agent.sh summary` prints `<GATE>: pass (unsupported: <focus,...>)` (never a bare pass), and `next` tells the lead to surface the unsupported checks to the user in its reply. Anti-dodge: `record` refuses an UNSUPPORTED_REASON shorter than 12 characters or without an anchor (a path-like token, an `INCONCLUSIVE:` measurement, or a tool/capability word such as parser, tool, browser, benchmark, schema, snapshot, contract, installed, throwaway), so "n/a" is refused; the report's `not proven:` needs at least three words. performance-proof submits a report whose thresholds could not be verified as `performance INCONCLUSIVE: thresholds unverified ...` (a measurement exists but is not verifiable), so it blocks. Trade-off, stated plainly: an agent that wants to skip a check now pays one concrete-sounding line instead of a user waiver; the word list cannot prove the tool is absent (amended by A102: a reason alone no longer suffices; UNSUPPORTED cites the skill validator's own saved output and is cross-checked against the script's own signals, and the word list stays as a secondary sanity check). What limits that: the result is visible in `pipeline`, `next`, `summary` and the completion report, the user is told in the lead's reply, a project that wants the old guarantee sets `risk.unsupported: block`, verify-proof never cites an unsupported focus as proof, and the skill validators (contract-proof, visual-proof, performance-proof, data-design) decide UNSUPPORTED from what they detected, not from the agent's choice. Why: in the COMPLEX e2e round 2 run the plan declared `contract_change: yes` for an HTTP API documented only in markdown, and the migration had no test-owned throwaway database; both focuses honestly reported UNSUPPORTED after a manual trace found no defect, yet A78 made each a blocking finding, so REVIEW_RULES and REVIEW_DATA failed, CODE_DONE was unreachable and the run ended asking for two waivers. On any project without machine-readable contracts or a temporary test database every contract or migration change would dead-end the same way, which trains users to waive by reflex. The user's invariant is "capability missing -> UNSUPPORTED, never counted as PASS, listed explicitly in the completion report"; a distinct `unsupported` status plus a mandatory `not proven:` line keeps that invariant without a stop the user cannot act on except by waiving. Alternatives rejected: keep A78 and let the e2e expectation accept waivers (C-13 forbids waivers in the harness, and the dead end stays for users); record UNSUPPORTED as `pass` with a note (A78's objection holds: it reads as a pass; here the status, the pipeline line and the report line all say unproven); a new waiver kind or an auto-waiver (a waiver is a user decision, not a default); making INCONCLUSIVE non-blocking too (a failed measurement is evidence of instability, not an absent tool); a separate gate or role for unsupported checks (no new gate types or roles).
- **A99. The script's own questions are printed in the run's language; identifiers and approval words stay verbatim (amends A63).** What: `agent.sh run-language [ID]` returns `tr` or `en`: a `Language: tr|en` line of the run's TASK.md wins, else the newest captured user prompt (`.agents/local/prompts/history/`, at least three words) is Turkish when it holds two or more Turkish-only letters or Turkish function words, else English (also when there is no signal). `request-approval` (plan, destructive, single_step, scope, budget, commit, push, waive), the assumption question of `freeze` and the failover question of `dispatch.sh` print a Turkish block in a Turkish run: the question, the labels (`seçenekler`, `önerilen`, `neden`) and the reason are Turkish; `approve`, `reject`, `accept AS-n`, `yes`, `no`, the kind word the user must type (`approve commit`), ids, hashes and the `QUESTIONS:` / `ASSUMPTION:` keys are unchanged, so approval matching (A41) and `assumption_prompt_accepts` (A79) see the same words. English runs print the old text byte for byte. The lead skill and role text say: never leave an English-only `QUESTIONS:` block as the last words of a non-English message; a specialist's English block is shown with a translation, keeping identifiers. — STANDARD.tr round 3: the lead's final message ended with the English approval block copied from `request-approval` (TR-1); A63 left the script without a language input. — Limits: the signal is a heuristic (A67 limits: ASCII-only Turkish with fewer than two function words reads as English); only Turkish is localised; a specialist's NEEDS_INPUT block stays English as stored (D13). The Stop hook (A44/A68) does not additionally detect an English-only block: the language of free text cannot be decided in POSIX sh/awk without false positives on quoted identifiers. — Alternatives rejected: translating in the lead only (failed in round 3; A63 already tried), translating every stored question (breaks D13 verbatim relay of specialists), a config `language` key (a second source that can disagree with the user's actual messages).
- **A102. An UNSUPPORTED result is backed by the skill validator's own output and cross-checked against the script's own signals; a reason alone no longer closes a focus (amends A98).** What: `agent.sh submit --result UNSUPPORTED` takes `--evidence <file>`, a run-relative file in the focus's report folder or `reports/`, snapshotted to `reports/snapshots/<sha12>-<role>-<path>` exactly like the report (A43); the result carries `UNSUPPORTED_EVIDENCE: <path> <sha256>`. `record` refuses an UNSUPPORTED (1) without that line; (2) whose file is outside the run or those folders, or whose sha256 differs from the cited one; (3) whose file lacks the validator's `RESULT: UNSUPPORTED` line (case-insensitive, so performance-proof's `result: UNSUPPORTED` from `--rows` counts; for `visual` also `RESULT: INCONCLUSIVE`); (4) whose file prints `BASE: <commit>` that is not the run's base; (5) for `contract`: when a contract file the control plane's own `risk_compute` found in the diff (`signal.contract_file`, source diff, by path or content) is not listed in a `FILE: compared|unsupported <path>` line, or when every listed file is `compared`; (6) for `migration`: when the file is `validate-migration.mjs` output without `--repo` (its `WARN no --repo` line), or a changed `.sql` migration signal is not listed `FILE: unsupported <path>`. The `concurrency` and `config` focuses, like `dependencies`, always have a tool-free check (a traced interleaving; the static consistency scan), so UNSUPPORTED is refused for them. The skill scripts print what this needs: `validate-contract.mjs` adds one `FILE: <status> <path>` line per file and, with `--base`, `BASE: <commit>`; `validate-migration.mjs` adds `RESULT: <status>` and, for UNSUPPORTED, `FILE: unsupported <file>` per cited migration (no throwaway database is UNSUPPORTED, so the e2e COMPLEX migration path keeps its evidence). Visibility without a dead end: the gate record keeps `unsupported_evidence: "<path>@<sha12>"` and `unsupported_evidence_sha256` (`valid_gate_file` makes the record stale when the file changes), `pipeline` prints `unsupported.<GATE>:<focus>=... (evidence: <path>@<sha12>)`, and `next` names the same before CODE_DONE and the report. The A98 status model is unchanged: a truthful UNSUPPORTED still closes its gate as `unsupported`, is listed under `## Unsupported Checks` with `not proven:`, `risk.unsupported: block` stays available, and INCONCLUSIVE still blocks. The A98 reason checks (length and anchor word list) stay as a secondary sanity check. The lead's `check-result.mjs` mirrors the line and the two refused focuses. Why: the user saw that after A98 a check (contract, migration) could be skipped with one concrete-sounding line that no longer held the gate, and the independent review said the same; the A98 follow-up only added a word list, which proves nothing about the tool. The control plane already knows, without the agent, which contract and migration files the diff touched; requiring the skill's own deterministic output and checking it against those files turns the cheapest dodge (claiming UNSUPPORTED over an OpenAPI file or a SQL migration the skill can handle) into a refusal, while an honest UNSUPPORTED costs one redirect of output the skill already prints. Limits, stated plainly: the control plane checks the file's text, it does not re-run the skill (skills stay standalone and may not be installed beside the control plane), so an agent that fabricates a file naming every signalled path as unsupported still passes; that takes a deliberate false artifact, bound by sha256 in the record and visible in `pipeline`, `next` and the completion report, where the verifier and the user can open it. Alternatives rejected: refuse a contract UNSUPPORTED whenever a signalled file is listed `compared` (the literal reading of the request): a run whose OpenAPI file was compared without a breaking change but whose second file cannot be parsed is honestly UNSUPPORTED and would dead-end again, the A98 failure; letting the control plane run the skill validators itself (couples the control plane to skill installation paths and node, and a skill is standalone by rule); a free-text evidence field (the same one-line dodge); requiring evidence only under `risk.unsupported: report` (block mode already needs a waiver, but one rule is simpler and the evidence helps the user decide the waiver); a cross-check on every migration path (`**/migrations/**` also matches non-SQL helpers the scanner may not analyze; the `.sql` rule is the conservative one). Review round on A102 (same decision): (a) capability probes in the control plane, independent of the agent, that only ever refuse: a `visual` UNSUPPORTED is refused when a Chromium-family browser is on PATH or in the standard macOS application folders or a project browser-test dependency is installed (the lists of visual-proof's `measure.mjs --detect`, kept equal by a risk-test drift guard), a `performance` UNSUPPORTED when the project has a benchmark command (package.json script `bench`/`benchmark`/`perf*`, Makefile or justfile `bench`/`benchmark` target, cargo `benches/`, Go `func Benchmark` in a tracked `*_test.go`, asv or pytest-benchmark, JMH, BenchmarkDotNet); a probe never refuses an INCONCLUSIVE (a measurement ran), and a benchmark that exists but cannot reach the change is submitted BLOCKED for the user (the flag `performance_critical` is the plan's own claim, so the user decides); `PROOFLINE_PROBE_ROOT` replaces PATH and the application folders for the self-tests only, and counts only with the second marker `PROOFLINE_SELFTEST=1` outside a runtime session (no Claude Code or Codex session variable set); the PreToolUse hook (Claude and Codex share it) refuses any model command that names either variable; (b) the INCONCLUSIVE prefix follows the evidence in both directions: INCONCLUSIVE evidence (visual `RESULT: INCONCLUSIVE`, performance `reason: performance INCONCLUSIVE:`) needs a reason starting `<focus> INCONCLUSIVE:`, so a measured but unreliable result cannot be downgraded to a non-blocking UNSUPPORTED, and UNSUPPORTED evidence refuses an INCONCLUSIVE-prefixed reason; (c) the evidence must be the submitting role's own file (its focus folder, its `reports/snapshots/<sha12>-<role>-...` snapshot, `reports/<NNN>-<role>...`), and `submit` snapshots only those. Residuals stated plainly: non-SQL migrations (`.py`, `.js`, `.rb`) have no `FILE:` cross-check; a contract or migration evidence file the agent writes by hand (echoing the validator's lines) still passes the text checks, and is caught only by the verifier or the user reading it (its path and sha12 are in `pipeline`, `next` and the gate record); the probes cannot see a browser or benchmark outside the conventions listed.
- **A103. The run language comes from the user's own words, not the newest captured prompt (amends A99).** What: `agent.sh run-language [ID]` reads, in order, a `Language: tr|en` line of TASK.md; the `>` blockquote lines of TASK.md (the user's report, A33/A67) when they hold three or more words; the OLDEST captured prompt (`.agents/local/prompts/history/`) of six or more words, i.e. the task prompt. A prompt shorter than six words (`approve commit`, `evet`, `onay`) is a reply and never evidence; no signal is English. The Turkish heuristic is unchanged except for a few more ASCII function words (`ben bunu sunu nasil neden evet hayir onay tamam`). — STANDARD.tr e2e round 4: A99 took the newest prompt of three or more words; the newest history files were the harness's English approval replies and system prompts, so `run-language` printed `en` for a Turkish run and the commit approval block was English again. — Limits: a run with no TASK.md quote whose first long prompt is English reads as English even if later prompts are Turkish; the heuristic limits of A67 still apply. — Alternatives rejected: majority vote across all prompts (a few long English system prompts outvote one Turkish task), newest prompt of a longer minimum (still flips on long system prompts), a config `language` key (a second source that can disagree).

- **A104. `submit` has one stdin: two `-` sources are refused before reading, or split on `=== FINDINGS ===`; `--findings none` is zero rows.** What: a real Codex worker called `submit --report - --findings -` with one heredoc, so both flags read the same stream; submit failed with "the report is empty", then "BAD 1: want severity|path:line|finding|evidence", twice, and the dispatch blocked. Now `submit_result` counts the `-` sources (`--report`, `--findings`, `--questions`) before reading anything. More than one is refused with `only one of --report/--findings may read stdin (-); write one of them to a file ...`, naming the corrected command, except the pair `--report -` + `--findings -`: that reads stdin once and splits it on the exact line `=== FINDINGS ===` (report above, rows below; a document without the line is refused with the same message). `--findings none` is zero rows (any role; the validator already allowed zero rows). An answer-only task submits `--findings none` or one `info|-|answer|<one line>` row. A rejected row or empty report now names the corrected form. Role texts, the dispatch prompt template, PROTOCOL.md and the skills' "no findings" line say the same; the old "output only the table header row" line is replaced because the script writes the header. Alternatives rejected: (1) splitting any two stdin sources by guessing (no deterministic rule); (2) making `--findings -` win and ignoring the report (silently drops evidence); (3) a dispatch-side rewrite of the worker command (hides the contract from the worker).
- **A105. A defect the request does not ask for is declared in TASK.md, and only the user's own `scope` approval makes its fix part of the run (amends A60; COMPLEX X-13, F-6).** What: in a COMPLEX or CRITICAL run whose request (TASK title, `## Goal`, the user's `>` quotes, the `## Suggested class` line) names no defect, a line of `## Context`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Constraints` or `## Risks` that speaks of a defect or a fix (`defect`, `bug`, `regression`, `fix`, `fixes`, `fixing`, Turkish `kusur`, `düzelt`) needs at least one `## Pre-existing defects` entry; every entry carries `decision: report` or `decision: fix`; a `###` heading (the section nested in Context, as models write it) counts, also for the A60 `decision: fix` check, which used to read only `##`. `freeze` and `refreeze` refuse before any other approval check (`agent.sh task_defect_errors`), `handoff IMPLEMENTING` repeats the check, `next` prints `fix TASK.md ## Pre-existing defects` instead of the approval steps, and `validate-task.mjs` reports the same error (and warns that `decision: fix` needs the user's `scope` approval). A `decision: fix` keeps the A60 rule: the freeze needs a `scope` approval bound to the PLAN.md hash, which `approve` records only from a captured user prompt holding an approval phrase and the word `scope`; an answer to a specialist or lead question, or a blanket "use your recommended option", never creates it. The A60 INTENT.md provenance check now also refuses a `scope` decision answered by a blanket recommended-option reply unless the decision is to report (the reply is recorded verbatim and is the user's, but it does not decide a fix). Role and skill texts: task author, lead, architect and plan-contract keep an unrequested defect fix out of the task and the plan, and the completion report names each `decision: report` defect under `## Known Limitations / Follow-up`. Why: in COMPLEX run r4 (`eval-COMPLEX-r4.md`) the task author asked an intake question about the `paginate` floor defect, the harness's generic reply "Use your recommended option for every open question" came back, and the author wrote the fix into TASK.md as a delegated Context decision, AC-6 ("15 books at pageSize 10 give totalPages 2, also without a tag filter") and a Risk, with no `## Pre-existing defects` section; A60's gate is keyed on that section, so nothing asked for a `scope` approval, REVIEW_PLAN judged the fix requested by the task, and `paginate` changed (X-13 and F-6 unmet). Validated against the run's real TASK.md: the freeze now refuses with `mentions a defect or a fix the request does not ask for: The paginate defect is fixed with a ceiling ...`; with the defect declared `decision: fix` it stops at `next=agent.sh request-approval <ID> scope`, which the harness never answers (X-13: stop at a scope request); with `decision: report` it freezes. Across the recorded e2e runs (TRIVIAL, STANDARD, STANDARD.tr, CRITICAL, COMPLEX) the rule fires only on COMPLEX tasks that mention the paging defect without the section (six runs; the three of them that changed `paginate` are among them); no TRIVIAL, STANDARD or CRITICAL task fires, because a defect fix is the request there or the class is below COMPLEX. Limits, stated plainly: the trigger is a word list, so a task author who describes the folded fix without any of those words passes the freeze, and REVIEW_PLAN (proof-review PLAN-CHECK rule 3) stays the second line; a STANDARD feature task that folds a defect is not checked (STANDARD defect tasks often state their goal positively, "every book is reachable", with no defect word, and would be refused). Alternatives rejected: the path rule "plan scope paths minus the paths TASK.md names need a `scope` approval" (on the real run `src/service.js` is named in TASK Context because the tag filter needs it, so the fix is not caught, while `public/index.html` and the test files are not named and would stop every COMPLEX run at an approval the harness never gives); "criteria not traceable to a TASK.md criterion" (AC-6 is a TASK criterion: the leak is in TASK.md itself); a `scope` approval for every `planned breaking` `## Contracts` entry (the CRITICAL scenario's requested column removal is a planned breaking change and would stop at `scope` instead of its destructive approval); making `## Pre-existing defects` mandatory in every task (every fixture and task gains a section for no signal; the word trigger asks for it only where a defect is mentioned).

- **A106. An approval's single-use is per capture, not per text (amends A41, A68; COMPLEX final run).** What: `agent.sh approve` identifies the user prompt it reads by its capture identity `session:time:sha256` and records it as `capture_id` in the approval (`capture_sha256` stays for audit). It refuses a second approval of the same kind from the same `capture_id`; a different capture with identical words is accepted when it is newer than the current request (`time > requested_at`, unchanged), carries the approval phrase and kind word, and the bound is the current hash. Different kinds are untouched: one capture still covers `plan` and `commit` in one prompt, because the check is per kind slug. Why: in the final COMPLEX run the plan was approved by "Plan approved.", the plan was legitimately changed (A105), a new plan request was made and the user answered with the same words; the old text-hash check refused it, so a user could never answer a second request with the same words. Forgery: capture files are written only by the runtime prompt hook (`proofline-hook.sh prompt`), and the lead hook allows writes only to run artifacts and `.agents/local/assignments/`, so `.agents/local/prompts/` is not writable by a model (enforcement test A106-4); a copied capture would also need a newer `time` than the request, which the model cannot produce in a capture the hook did not write. Rejected: keying on the history file name (the per-session `<session>.json` is the file `approve` reads, and a same-second prompt would collide in history); dropping single-use (a replay of one capture would approve two requests).
- **A107. A report is not evidence: `submit` re-derives the validator result, re-checks every cited evidence file and re-runs a recorded reproduced command (amends A93, A102).** What: (1) `agent.sh submit` runs the skill validator of the submitting role and focus itself (verifier: `validate-verify.mjs`; reviewer `tests`: test-trust `gate.mjs`; reviewer `plan`, `rules`, `rules+tests`: proof-review `validate-findings.mjs` then `gate.mjs` over the focus's `findings.json`, when the skill and node are installed) and uses its result. An invalid report is refused with the validator's errors; the optional `--validator-result PASS|FAIL` that the agent declares is compared with the recomputed value and a mismatch is refused naming both; a PASS the validator computes as FAIL is refused the same way. (2) Every evidence file a submission cites (`--evidence PATH[@SHA256]`, repeatable, or `PATH@<64 hex>` in a finding row's evidence column or the report) must be a regular file inside the run, in a folder the role reports in (or `reports/`, `worker-evidence/`), and its sha256 must equal the cited one: a missing file, a file outside those folders, or a file changed after it was hashed refuses the submission. The result keeps `EVIDENCE: <path> <sha256>` lines and `record` checks them again. (3) For a gate result of PASS, `submit` re-runs the recorded `reproduced` items itself: the verifier's `## Commands` entries and cited evidence files that carry `command:`, `exit:` and `output:` lines. Only a command that is the configured `commands.build|test|lint` or a frozen PLAN `## Verification commands` entry is executed (at most three, in the project root, with a timeout when `timeout` exists); a different exit status or a missing recorded output line turns the result into FAIL with a blocking finding, and items none of which is an allowed command are a blocking finding too (nothing a report names is ever run). Evidence classes stay measured, reproduced, traced, judged; no role, agent, gate or skill is added. Why: A93 and A102 left the accepted residual that a fabricated but self-consistent report passes, because every check read the report's own text; "no evidence, no claim" had a hole at exactly the place the claim is made. The control plane can now disprove a recorded command and a recorded hash without trusting the writer. Rejected: running every recorded command (cost: a test suite twice per round; three is the bound and the verifier's own run is the first); executing any command a report names (arbitrary execution from model text); making the verifier agent re-run commands as a rule (policy-only, the same writer); requiring a findings JSON for every focus now (other focuses keep the findings-derived result until their findings file is mandatory, listed as a residual). Residual: a report whose commands are all outside the configured and planned set has nothing to re-run and is a blocking finding for the verifier, but an evidence file that is not a reproduction record (measured, traced, judged) is checked for existence and hash only; reviewer focuses without a mapped validator (contract, concurrency, performance, config, migration, data, security, qa) are not yet re-derived. Review round 1 (no silent skip): (a) which gates are reproduced-class: only VERIFY (its `## Commands` records are `reproduced`). A VERIFY PASS (verify-proof installed) with nothing re-runnable is a blocking finding `no re-runnable reproduced evidence`; every other gate (REVIEW_*, SECURITY, QA, the risk focuses) is judgment, trace or measurement unless it cites a command record (`command:`/`exit:`/`output:`), and a PASS that re-ran nothing records the info row `NOT_RERUN: <gate>:<focus> no reproduced evidence; this gate is not reproduced proof`, which verify-proof must not cite as reproduced proof. (b) A mapped focus (verifier, reviewer tests/plan/rules/rules+tests) whose skill is installed but whose validator cannot run (no node, no findings.json) refuses a PASS whether or not `--validator-result` was declared; a skill that is not installed records the info row `NOT_VALIDATED`; the other focuses are unmapped and keep the findings-derived result. (c) A compared item needs a recorded output line that equals a whole line of the re-run output (trimmed); a missing line or a bare substring such as `ok` compares nothing and is a blocking finding. (d) Every command an AC row cites as `command:` proof is re-run (not capped) or is a blocking finding (not configured or planned, no exit status, no Commands entry); other allowed items run up to three. (e) A bare `evidence:<path>` mention (no hash) in a row or report is checked for existence and then hashed; plain prose paths are not. (f) The planned commands are read from PLAN.md only while its sha256 equals the frozen `plan_sha256`; a plan edited after the freeze contributes none. Alternatives rejected in this round: making an absent validator a silent fallback (the declared-versus-omitted asymmetry), accepting a substring of the output (a fabricated `ok` matches), re-running only the first allowed command. Residuals: unmapped focuses; configured commands are read from the live config (the config is bound by policy at the freeze, not re-hashed here); a measured, traced or judged evidence file is checked for existence and hash, not re-derived; a cited path in prose without `evidence:` or `@sha256` is not seen. Review round 2: (g) a silent command records `output: (no output)` (an absent line with a recorded exit means the same) and matches an empty re-run, comparing the exit status only; a non-empty re-run with none recorded is a mismatch. (h) A recorded output line holding a time, duration, date, pid, address or UUID is refused with the instruction to record one stable summary line; the verifier skill and role say so. (i) A gate that is not reproduced-class ignores a cited command that is not configured or planned (it is never run and never blocks; the gate records `NOT_RERUN`); only the verifier's AC-cited commands are blocking when not re-runnable. (j) A frozen plan hash that is missing or not 64 hex denies every PLAN command (only configured `commands.build|test|lint` run); this is defence in depth, because `submit` already refuses a run whose freeze does not match (`freeze mismatch`), which the scenario exercises. (k) Every `command:`/`exit:`/`output:` triple of a cited evidence file is re-run, at most three per file. Residuals: a verifier PASS written while verify-proof is not installed is not reproduced-class (no validator and no re-run requirement apply; the lead's `next` treats the gate by its record only); a re-run executes the project's own command in the project root, so a command with side effects (writes, network) has them on every submit, the same as the verifier's own run, and the database guard and the runtime hook do not cover a process started by `agent.sh`.

- **A109. Self-test shards are balanced by unit weight, six shards (amends A76).** What: `tests/selftest.sh` assigns each unit to a shard by weight instead of `index % N`: the units are taken longest first and each goes to the lightest shard (`tests/selftest-weights.txt`, seconds from one CI run, default 15 for an unlisted unit); a shard starts its heaviest units first. CI runs six shards instead of four and prints every unit's time (`SELFTEST_SLOWEST=999`). `SELFTEST_LIST=1` prints a shard's units, `SELFTEST_SLOWEST=K` the K slowest. `risk-test` `sc_unsupported` (one process, about nine minutes) is split at its independent run boundaries into `sc_unsupported`, `sc_unsupported_inconclusive`, `sc_unsupported_rows` and `sc_unsupported_block`; each builds its own run and every assertion is kept. Every unit lands in exactly one shard (checked: the six shard lists joined equal the one-shard list, 120 units), so no test is dropped and no assertion changes. Why: measured on pull-request runs of the `ci` workflow, the four shards took 5.0, 14.4, 5.5 and 4.0 minutes (run 38594862821; a manual run with all unit times took 4.1 to 12.2 minutes): the round-robin put the heavy units (`cli-test`, `risk-test sc_unsupported*`, the `lifecycle-test` loops) together and which shard was worst changed from run to run, so the wall time was the worst shard, not the total (about 25 minutes of unit time over four cores, 6.5 minutes when balanced). With the weights and the split the six shards took 2.8 to 7.9 minutes (run 38609632577); the floor is now `cli-test` alone, 470 s, one single-process suite. Rejected: only raising the shard count (index % N still pairs heavy units by luck; eight shards cost eight runner setups for no better floor); splitting `cli-test` into scenario units (a 165-case single-process suite whose cases share state; the change is larger than the gain and risks the suite's own meaning); dropping or shortening slow scenarios (tests are not removed, A76); dynamic work distribution across jobs (needs a shared queue the runners do not have). A stale weight only costs balance, never coverage; refresh the file from `SELFTEST_SLOWEST=999` output when units are added.
- **A110. visual-proof browser measurement runs as its own Linux and macOS CI job on the runner image's own browser, and `measure.mjs` retries a browser start timeout once (amends A82).** What: the step moves out of the `fixtures` job into the job `visual-browser` (pushes to `main`, nightly, manual runs; pull requests never run it), in parallel with the fixtures and benchmark work instead of after it. `measure.mjs` retries `launch` once when the browser prints no DevTools endpoint within the start timeout, and the timeout message carries the tail of the browser's stderr. Why: measured on `ubuntu-latest` (Chromium and Chrome 154 preinstalled, nothing installed by the workflow): `--no-sandbox` works there (kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 forbids the sandbox), the fixture measures 117 checks in about 40 s and `expect.mjs` finds exactly the 27 planted failures with the traps clear; one main run had failed with `browser did not start within 30000 ms` and the next two runs passed, so the cause was a cold-start hang, not the flag. A retry bounds that flake without loosening any assertion; a second hang still fails the step. Rejected: raising the start timeout (a hang stays a hang and the step gets slower); installing a browser in the workflow (A82: tooling is detected, never installed); making the step non-blocking (a measured pass must stay distinguishable from an unmeasured one).
- **A108. Approval detection is fail-closed: a positive grammar, anything else is ambiguous (amends A41, A68, A79).** What: `text_has_approval` (used by `agent.sh approve`, hence by the prompt hook's `approve-pending`) took any text that held an `approval.phrases` entry as a substring plus a kind word, so "do not approve the plan", "approve the plan?" and "disapproved, plan" approved. Now the reply is normalised (ASCII case folding under `LC_ALL=C`, ASCII punctuation removed, apostrophes dropped, other bytes unchanged) and approves only when EVERY word is (a) a word of an allowlisted approval phrase (default list: `approve, approved, yes, ok, okay, go ahead, lgtm, commit it, push it, onay, onaylıyorum, onayliyorum, onaylandı, onaylandi, onayladım, onayladim, evet, tamam, olur`; `approval.phrases` still overrides), (b) a word of the kind's own words (`kind_words`: the kind word, `destructive migration delete drop`, `single step`, `budget round rounds`, the finding id), or (c) a filler (`the, a, an, it, this, please, for, with, to, and, lütfen, lutfen, bu, planı, plani, için, icin`); it also holds a whole allowlisted phrase and a kind word (unchanged requirement; hash binding and A106 per-capture single-use unchanged) and no question mark. Any other word, a negation, a hesitation, an extra clause or anything unrelated, makes the reply ambiguous: no approval and no rejection, the request stays pending, and `next` prints "the user's last reply is not an explicit approval ... relay the question again" (`approval_wait_o`) until the lead asks again with `request-approval`. Every approval question lists the accepted phrases and the filler words next to the `approve <kind>` instruction (Turkish block in a Turkish run, A99; English otherwise). Why: the absence of a rejection word is not consent; an approval is a security decision (D3, D13) and a wrong yes writes an approval the user never gave. A longer legitimate reply is re-asked; that is the accepted cost of failing closed. Tests: `scenario_approval_fail_closed` in `lifecycle-test.sh` (ambiguous, empty, unrelated, negated and hesitant answers leave the request pending, under the C and a UTF-8 locale; every allowlisted TR and EN phrase approves; the question lists the answers); existing approval texts of the suites were shortened to the grammar. Rejected: a hold-word denylist on top of the substring match (first form of this decision: it leaked on any negation it did not list: "I shouldn't approve", "I cannot approve", "yes, delete nothing", "onay vermiyorum", "onay yok", "onaylamıyorum", "just kidding"; a denylist cannot be complete in two languages with suffixes); requiring the whole message to be exactly one phrase (a kind word and a polite filler are normal); fuzzy or model-judged intent (not deterministic); changing the A79 `accept <id>` check (already a start-of-prompt plus no-negation rule, unchanged).
- **A112. A non-TRIVIAL plan with a `## UI` section declares `visual_writes:` at plan time (amends A78, A81, A82, A98).** What: `validate-plan.mjs` reports a missing `visual_writes: <how the data the page writes is thrown away>` line as an error when the class is not TRIVIAL (STANDARD, COMPLEX, CRITICAL: the classes whose pipeline has a QA gate, so QA's visual focus runs for a UI plan) and the plan has a `## UI` section (the same line shape `validate-visual.mjs` reads as the same-origin-write allowance), and `agent.sh freeze` refuses the same plan (only when gates are enforced) with a message naming the line to add. The designer role, the plan-contract sections reference and the PLAN templates say to write it whenever QA visual will run; `visual_writes: none, <why>` is accepted when the page sends no same-origin writes. TRIVIAL (no QA gate, A96) is unchanged. The line patterns of `agent.sh`, `validate-plan.mjs` and `validate-visual.mjs` are identical in shape and a test asserts they accept and refuse the same sample lines. Why: an end-to-end COMPLEX run froze a plan without the line, QA visual ended INCONCLUSIVE, the fix needed a plan amendment and a second plan approval, the fourth reply exceeded the three-reply cap and the run stopped at IMPLEMENTED; the need is knowable when the plan is written. Alternatives rejected: keying it on COMPLEX/CRITICAL only (STANDARD has qa: yes, so a STANDARD UI plan hit the same INCONCLUSIVE and amendment); leaving it to QA INCONCLUSIVE and an amendment (the defect itself: it costs a second approval); raising the reply cap (hides the miss, loosens a harness limit for a plan defect); auto-approving amendments (the user's approval of what QA may write is the point of A41); deriving a default (the line is a free-text allowance of how data is discarded, not a path, so no safe default exists and inventing one would widen what QA may write).
- **A114. A headless Claude worker is started with an explicit permission mode (amends A46, A56).** What: `dispatch.sh` passes `--permission-mode <mode>` to every Claude worker it starts, from config `dispatch.claude_permission_mode` (`bypassPermissions` default, `acceptEdits`, `default`; `config-check` refuses any other value). With `bypassPermissions`, dispatch first verifies that `.agents/hooks/proofline-hook.sh` exists and `.claude/settings.json` wires a `PreToolUse` hook; otherwise the step is BLOCKED with a message naming `proofline doctor`, and no unconfined worker is run. The mode is ledgered (`dispatch claude_permission_mode=...`) and printed in the dispatch line. The Codex branch is unchanged. Why: a real mixed run (Codex lead, Claude reviewer and verifier, and failover) ended BLOCKED at IMPLEMENTED: a headless `claude -p` in default mode cannot approve `agent.sh submit`, `fingerprint`, test commands or file writes, so no dispatched Claude worker could record a result; all-Claude runs only worked because native Task subagents inherit the lead's permissions. A worker cannot be prompted, and the confinement is the PreToolUse hook (role write paths, scratch guard, stash guard, destructive-SQL guard, no `agent.sh approve`), which runs in every permission mode. Rejected: inheriting the lead's mode (not detectable from a headless child); `--allowedTools` lists (arbitrary test and build commands cannot be enumerated); dispatching Claude workers only through Task (breaks a Codex lead and failover); an unconditional bypass without the hook check (an unconfined worker). Dependencies and residuals: WebFetch, WebSearch, MCP and Task tools are unreachable for the worker only because its `--agents` tools list (generated agent or `tools.conf`) omits them; the hook check is the script present, non-empty and parsing plus a `PreToolUse` entry for it in `.claude/settings.json` (settings.local.json-only or plugin-provided wiring is refused, fail closed); the worker still inherits user-level Claude settings (possible follow-up: `--setting-sources project,local`).
- **A111. Every `git stash` subcommand is denied in the project's working tree for a specialist; evidence worktrees stay free (amends A71).** A STANDARD.tr end-to-end run failed C-3 on one item: the QA subagent ran `git stash list` in the project tree. The command is read-only but is a `git stash` invocation, and the A71 hook let it through. What the hook does now (`adapters/claude/hooks/proofline-hook.sh`, `stash_guard`): for a specialist during an active run it reads the scanned commands (nested `sh -c`, pipelines, `;`/`&&` lists, env and `cd` prefixes included), skips git's global options (`-C <path>`, `--work-tree`, `-c`, `--no-pager` and other flags) and denies `stash` with any subcommand (bare, list, show, push, pop, apply, drop, clear, create, store, branch) unless the effective directory (hook cwd moved by `cd` and `git -C`) lies inside a registered worktree other than the project; the denial names the evidence worktree as the allowed alternative. `git stash` text as an argument of another command (`grep`, `echo`) is not a git invocation and stays allowed. Fail-closed on what the text cannot say: the hook does not expand shell variables, so a `-C`/`cd` path is resolved only when it is a literal path, or starts with `$TMPDIR` or `$HOME` (expanded to a literal and resolved physically, symlinks and `..` included). Any other variable, a command substitution or backticks, `cd -`, `$OLDPWD`, `pushd`/`popd`, `env -C`/`sudo -D`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, or a `cd` that sits in a subshell, pipe or background job before the stash is read as the project, so the stash is denied (a wrong denial costs one retry with a literal path). A first word after the options that is not a plausible subcommand name (a value of an option the hook does not know) followed by the word `stash` is read as a stash. Known value-taking global options are skipped (`-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--namespace`, `--super-prefix`, `--exec-path`, `--config-env`, `--attr-source`; `--list-cmds` and `--exec` are skipped with their value too). A directory that does not exist when the hook runs is unresolved (a failed `cd`, or a link made later in the same command), so it is read as the project; an evidence worktree is therefore created in one call and used in the next. Command substitution: the scanner splits an unquoted `$(...)` or backtick pair into a nested command, so the records alone do not see `git -C $(pwd) stash list`; a text safety net covers it. Every `git [known options] stash` (or a `$`/backtick where the subcommand goes, `git $S list`, `git stash${IFS}list`) in command position that no record resolved to an evidence worktree is denied, including behind wrappers (`find -exec`, `watch`, `parallel`, `ssh`, `setsid`, `chronic`, `unbuffer`, `script -c`, `su -c`, a function body). The net skips a match whose command word only prints or searches (`echo`, `printf`, `grep`, `rg`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`, `head`, `tail`, ...), and a word after `git` that is not an option (`git log stash`, `git diff main..stash`, `git branch stash`, `git commit -m stash`, `git grep stash`, `git config stash.x`) is never a stash. Known limits, not closed: a function or alias that wraps `git stash` defined in an earlier call or an obfuscated subcommand (`git st""ash`, a built string run by `eval` is already refused by A34) is not seen, and a printing word followed by a real stash in the same segment is skipped. Other cases the text does not see (reviewer's LOW findings, accepted): a quoted substitution or variable in subcommand position (`git "$S" list`, `git "$(echo stash)" list`), `echo stash | xargs git`, `` `which git` stash ``, `git stash\ list`, and a stash run by another program (a Python `subprocess` list form). `GIT_WORK_TREE=`, `GIT_DIR=`, `--work-tree` and `-c core.worktree=` anywhere in the same git invocation make the target the project, so the stash is denied. Fail-closed false positives, accepted (retry with a literal `git -C <worktree> stash` in its own call): a `git stash` inside the message of a command that is not a printing word (`git commit -m "... git stash ..."`), `(cd <worktree> && git stash)` in a subshell, and `git --git-dir=<worktree>/.git --work-tree=<worktree> stash`. `git checkout --` and the other mutating subcommands keep the A71 rule unchanged. — Rationale (recorded by the author): C-3 says the command is not invoked in the project tree, and a subagent cannot be expected to know that `list` is the safe subset the rule never named; the hook is the deterministic place. — Alternatives rejected by the author: loosening EXPECTED C-3 to allow read-only subcommands (moves the target to hide a product gap and leaves `show` and `stash@{n}` forms ambiguous); accepting it as model behaviour (the hook exists to make this deterministic, and the run was scored FAIL for it).
- **A113. `submit` allocates an explorer's report name (amends A43, X-4/M-2).** Parallel explorers each wrote `reports/001-explorer.md`, overwrote each other, and one was resubmitted: three explorer results where COMPLEX allows two. Now the explorer writes its report anywhere in scratch and passes it with `submit --report <file>|-` (any `--artifact` is ignored; BLOCKED without `--report` stores the reason as the report). `submit` validates the content first, then picks the next free `reports/NNN-explorer.md` with an atomic noclobber create (parallel submits cannot get the same name, capped at 1000 attempts), copies the content there and cites a snapshot of it in the result and ledger row; a submit refused after the allocation (language scan, validator, record) removes the file and its owner entry again. The allocation is remembered per dispatch token under `reports/.owners/`: the same token updates its own report, a re-dispatch under a new token gets a new name, and a tokenless submit succeeds and gets a new name every time (it cannot update one). An explorer that names a report path itself (`--artifact reports/001-explorer.md`, `reports/./001-explorer.md`, `reports//...`: paths are canonicalised in `normalize_artifact` before every check) is refused with the corrected command, and `record` accepts an explorer result only when it cites a `reports/snapshots/` copy made by `submit`, so `record --file` cannot cite another dispatch's live report. The hook's owns.conf still lets an explorer Write `reports/NNN-explorer.md`; only `submit` decides what is accepted. `dispatch.sh` also claims its sequence number with an atomic `mkdir`, so parallel dispatches no longer share a token, log or submission status. Rejected: serialising explorers (loses the parallelism `max_explorers` exists for and still leaves name choice to the model); letting the lead rename files afterwards (the overwrite has already destroyed one report and its result cites it); lead-assigned names via a reservation command plus a `REPORT:` line (first draft: nothing forces the lead or the explorer to obey, and it left stubs for roles that never needed one); per-token owner files over a name the explorer chooses (first-submitter-wins is defeated by a direct Write before submit). Known limit: a result may still cite an existing snapshot of another explorer's report through `record --file` (snapshots are immutable and content-addressed, so it cannot be altered, only reused); the lead's EVIDENCE.md consolidation reads each result's own header.
- **A115. A TRIVIAL freeze refuses an executable-code scope (amends A31, A61).** A real run had the lead author TASK.md with Suggested class TRIVIAL, classify TRIVIAL and freeze a plan scoping `src/service.js` and `tests/service.test.js` (two paths, inside the TRIVIAL bound). Nothing at freeze judged code against text; A31 fired only at IMPLEMENTED, so the lead reclassified STANDARD and refroze after the code existed: C-4 (a transition recorded twice) and S-6 (QA_PLAN before IMPLEMENT) were broken. Now `pipeline_check` (freeze and refreeze, the only ways to a frozen plan; `handoff IMPLEMENTING` verifies the plan hash, so a code scope cannot be added later without a refreeze) fails a TRIVIAL plan whose `## Scope` paths match the glob list A31 uses (`review.executable_code`, one shared helper `paths_executable`): "the TRIVIAL pipeline covers text and configuration only; scope has executable code: <paths> — classify STANDARD". Test files are code by that list; `.html`, `.css`, `.md`, `.json`, `.txt` are not, so a copy fix in `public/index.html` stays TRIVIAL. A31 stays as the check of the real diff at IMPLEMENTED and CODE_DONE; it now fires only when `review.executable_code` is wider at the diff than at freeze. `next` and the lead lifecycle name the rule. Rejected: forcing the class from the lead-authored Suggested class (the lead authors it, so it only repeats the claim); keeping only the late A31 check plus a refreeze (violates C-4 and S-6 by construction); a file-count threshold (the two-path bound is what let two code files through).
- **A116. `cleanup` also removes the run's `.agents/local/assignments/<ID>/` directory (amends A11).** What: after every existing precondition passes, `cleanup` deletes `.agents/local/assignments/<ID>/` together with the run directory; a symlink or non-directory there is refused with a clear message before anything is removed, so both directories stay; a missing directory is fine; other runs' assignment directories and the parent are never touched. Why: the lead's per-run assignment files outlived the run and accumulated. Rejected: a separate `agent.sh prune` (a second command to remember, and it needs its own "which runs are finished" rule that cleanup already has); garbage-collecting by age (can delete a live run's assignments, and the age threshold is arbitrary).
- **A117. `.claude/` is ignored as a whole in this repository; `proofline init` never ignores it in a project; the e2e harness and evaluators clean up their own temporary output.** What: the repository's `.gitignore` carries the single line `.claude/` instead of five individual entries (nothing under `.claude` is tracked). `proofline init` keeps adding only `.agents/local/` and `.agents/runs/`; the CLI test asserts, after one and two inits and with a pre-existing `.gitignore`, that no `^/?\.claude(/|$)` line appears. `tests/e2e/run.sh` installs a trap on EXIT (and HUP, INT, TERM) that stops a lead process group still alive and, without `--keep`, removes the project copy and the isolated Codex home, including after a dry run or a failure (before, only a completed non-dry run did); `out/` always stays, the whole run directory stays with `--keep`. `evaluate.md` and the e2e README tell an evaluator to write only its evaluation file and remove every scratch file, copy, extracted tree or temporary worktree it made, leaving nothing in the repository checkout. `capabilities-test.sh` asserts the dry-run cleanup and `--keep`. Why: agent state, progress notes, evaluations and worktrees under `.claude/` kept appearing as untracked files, and a per-file list always missed the next one; an installed project's `.claude/settings.json` is meant to be committed, so the rule must not travel with `init`; failed or interrupted harness runs and evaluators left copies and worktrees behind. Rejected: cleaning by age (a sweep deletes what a live run still uses and hides the leak instead of ending it); ignoring only specific `.claude/` files (the list is always one file behind); having `init` ignore `.claude/` (it would hide the project's committed Claude settings and agents).
- **A118. A stale-lock break never strips a live holder of its pid.** What: `acquire_lock` takes a dead holder's `pid` file by renaming it to `pid.brk.<pid>` and removes the lock only when the renamed file still names the dead holder; otherwise it puts the file back and keeps waiting. Before, a waiter that had read a dead holder's pid removed whatever `pid` file was there when it acted, so a holder that took the lock in between lost it and two commands ran the read/modify/write transaction at once (ledger sequence and allocation collisions, seen as a rare `sc_parallel_lock` failure on CI). `gates-test` `sc_lock_break_race` reproduces it deterministically with a fake `cat`; the test fixtures also use captures dated one hour ahead (a capture 5 s ahead went stale on a slow machine) and no longer let cleanup of the fixture directory decide the exit status. Why: mutual exclusion is the lock's only job. Known limits: a waiter killed (kill -9) between the rename-aside and the `rm`/`mv` back leaves the lock directory with no `pid` file and a `pid.brk.*` file, so every later waiter times out after `PROOFLINE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (120 s by default); the old code had the same class of window, and the leftover file now also makes `rmdir` fail. If a live holder releases while its `pid` file is renamed aside, its release is skipped, the directory keeps a dead pid and the next waiter breaks it normally (one spurious `lock-break` ledger row); harmless. No further stale-lock heuristic is added. Rejected: a second mutex around the break (the acquiring side would still not take it); `flock` (not in POSIX sh, absent on macOS by default); a mkdir-only lock without a pid file (a crashed holder could never be told from a live one, so it would never be broken); a sleep in the tests (hides the race, does not close it).
- **A120. The Write/Edit tools may not write outside the project copy, and the e2e harness replies to a question only while one is open (C-18, C-14; amends A97).** What: (1) *Hook.* In the COMPLEX run 3 the designer called `Write` on a path whose directory name had a hyphen where a separator belongs (`.../-Users-...-proofline-<session>/scratchpad/e2e-root/.../project/DESIGN.md` instead of `.../-Users-...-proofline/<session>/...`), and the same for `design/UI.md` and `ui.json`; the files landed in a new sibling tree under `/private/tmp/claude-501/`. The cause was not a string-prefix bug (`relpath` matches `"$root"/*`, so `<project>-x` is outside): `path_ok` returned success for every `@outside` path, so A97's shell guard had no counterpart for the file tools. the pretool loop (after `target_ok`) now refuses an outside target of Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and Codex `apply_patch` unless it is inside a registered git worktree or under the runtime's own storage (`~/.claude/projects/*/memory/`, `~/.claude/projects/*/tool-results/`, `~/.claude/plans/`; `settings.json`, `hooks/`, `rules/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `agents/`, `skills/` and `commands/` stay refused); a symlink among the parents is still resolved first. (2) *Harness.* `tests/e2e/run.sh` sent the scripted question reply whenever no approval was pending, up to `E2E_MAX_REPLIES`; the lead of that run had stopped on a request only the user could fulfil (delete a stray file) and four replies changed nothing. A new `tests/e2e/question-open.sh` decides: a reply goes out only when `agent.sh next` says "a question is pending" or the lead's last message holds a question mark; otherwise the loop stops and `summary.txt` records `stopped=no-open-question` with the last run state (`stopped_state`). Plan approvals are unchanged; destructive, single_step, scope, budget, commit, push and waive requests are still never answered. Why: both were real defects found by the evaluation; EXPECTED C-14 and C-18 are unchanged. Alternatives rejected: a longer `E2E_MAX_REPLIES` or a lower one (hides the loop); matching the model's wording for "no question is open" (language-dependent); denying outside writes only inside a run (the shell guard A97 already applies before one). Residual: a model that stops without a question mark while it does want an answer gets no reply (the run then ends as unfinished, which is visible); the runtime-storage paths are matched by pattern only.
- **A119. A stray file in a run directory is recoverable: the hook refuses `sed -i` with an option-looking suffix, and the lead has `agent.sh discard-stray`.** What: (1) the hook denies `sed -i` (also `-ni` and similar) when the next word starts with `-` (`sed -i -E`, `-i -e`, `-i -n`) or with text glued to `-i` that starts with a letter or `-` (`-iE`, `-ie`, `-in`, `-i-E`), for every caller; on BSD/macOS sed that word is the backup suffix, so the command leaves `<file>-E` beside the target (seen as `runs/T-1/QA_PLAN.md-E`). The message names the portable ways: the Write/Edit tool, `sed -E ... file > scratch && mv scratch file`, `perl -pi -e`. GNU `sed -i.bak`, `sed -i '' ...`, `sed -E` and `sed -n` without `-i` are unchanged. (2) `agent.sh discard-stray <ID> <file-name>` (lead only, run not terminal, completion report not published) removes one TOP-LEVEL regular file of the run directory: the argument is a single file name (no `/`, no `..`, no leading `.`), never a symlink or directory, and its lower-cased name must not equal a protected top-level name of the `known_control_artifact` registry (TASK, PLAN, RUN.yaml, COMPLETION_REPORT, LEDGER.log, VERIFY, EVIDENCE, QA_PLAN, QA_REPORT, `pid` and the registry directories), whether or not the pipeline needs it now. The comparison is case-insensitive because macOS/APFS is: `plan.md` and `PLAN.md` are one file there. Deletion is `rm -f -- <canonical run dir>/<name>`. It writes a `discard-stray` ledger row with the path and sha256 and `next`/`handoff`/`verify-scope` name the command in their "unexpected run artifact" refusal. The hook needs no change for the command: the lead may run any `agent.sh` subcommand and every other role is refused by the existing allow-list and by `require_lead`; raw `rm` in a run directory stays denied. Why: the stray file made `handoff` refuse while the hook denied `rm` for every role, so a whole COMPLEX run deadlocked with no legal way out. Known limits: strays inside subdirectories are not handled (validation tolerates them, and a subpath would make the registry depend on case and symlink resolution); the check-then-delete is not atomic (a TOCTOU window exists; the command is lead-only and the lead is the only writer of that directory at that moment); the `sed` check is a word heuristic like the rest of the scan (a script held in a variable or `xargs sed -i -E` is not seen) and also denies `-iE`, `-ie`, `-in` (glued suffix) and the harmless `sed -i -f script file` / `-i --`; a stray whose name equals a protected name in another case can never be discarded. APFS also folds some Unicode (U+017F reads as `s`, U+212A as `K`), so `discard-stray` accepts only `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` names (checked under `LC_ALL=C`) and also refuses any name that is the same file (same inode, compared with `ls -di`) as a protected name, so whatever else the filesystem folds cannot reach a control artifact; `RUN.yaml.tmp` is protected too. The `sed` deny does not see a backslash-escaped command word (`sed\ -i -E`), an option word held in a variable (`a=-E; sed -i $a`) or built from `${IFS}` (`sed -i${IFS}-E`). Rejected: letting roles `rm` in the run directory (reopens the writable-run-state hole the hook closes); auto-deleting unknown files at `handoff` (silently destroys a file that may be evidence, and hides the cause); renaming the stray (it stays in the run directory and still fails `validate`).
- **A121. The e2e harness records the database before and after a run and a verdict (CRITICAL K-9, K-13; amends A95).** What: `tests/e2e/db-probe.mjs` copies the bytes of `data/reading-list.db` to a temp file and probes the copy read-only; it prints the first two lines of the old probe (`columns=`, `legacy_notes_non_null=`) unchanged, then the `legacy_notes` sha256 and short values, per-table columns and row counts, the applied migrations (`schema_migrations`, else `no migrations table`) and the sha256 of the file bytes (`no database` if absent). `run.sh` writes `db-probe-before.txt` right after the project copy is prepared and before any lead starts, `db-probe.txt` after the run, `db-probe-diff.txt` and `db_unchanged=yes|no` in `summary.txt`; the dry run does the same and `capabilities-test.sh` asserts `yes` on an untouched copy. Why: an evaluation could not judge K-9 because the old probe held only the columns and a count: no migration list, no stored values, no content hash and no earlier probe to compare. EXPECTED files are unchanged. Alternatives rejected: relying on transcripts only (shows what the lead said it ran, not what the file holds); running sqlite3 against the live file (opens it, may create a journal or change it, and the project's own tooling is what the run must not trigger). A probe that cannot run (no node, non-zero exit) writes `probe failed: <reason>` and the verdict is `db_unchanged=unknown`, never `yes`. The `-wal` file next to the database is hashed on its own line (`db_wal_sha256=`, `absent` if none) so an uncheckpointed change shows; `-shm` is ignored. Residual: the probe opens a copy of the main file only, so the stored values in an uncheckpointed WAL are not read, only detected through the WAL hash.
- **A122. The debug-proof guard also reads the task's own text (amends A35, A105; STANDARD S-6).** What: the `handoff IMPLEMENTED` guard that requires `reports/NNN-debug.md` fired only when the TASK title or Goal held a defect word, so a pagination bug fix titled "Every book is reachable through pagination" passed `CODE_DONE` without the report in two regression runs. It now also fires when a line of `## Goal`, `## Context`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Constraints`, `## Risks` or a user `>` quote uses the words of A105 (`defect`, `bug`, `regression`, `fix`, `fixes`, `fixing`, Turkish `kusur`, `düzelt`; one shared list, `defect_sec_re`/`defect_sec_tr`, used by `task_defect_errors` too). `## Pre-existing defects` entries are findings and do not count. TRIVIAL and the existing exemptions stay. The failure names `reports/NNN-debug.md` and the debug-proof skill. EXPECTED is unchanged. Why: the trigger must not depend on the lead's wording of the title. Rejected: title-only keywords as today (the miss); always requiring the report for STANDARD (a feature has nothing to reproduce); asking the model whether the task is a bug fix (not deterministic); reading the RED `expected_failure` (the tdd-proof skill tells implementers to write ordinary actual-vs-expected text, so it flags nearly every feature run). Limit: the word list is a heuristic. A lead that keeps defect words out of TASK.md avoids the guard (a model-honesty limit, not enforceable here), and a Constraint such as "do not fix other bugs" asks for the report although the run is not a fix; the lead then writes the short reproduction.
- **A123. A fix round may touch a frozen plan-scope path that shares an acceptance criterion with a failing finding.** A COMPLEX run failed after fix round 1: the gate's `fix_scope` held only the finding paths (`app.js`, `repository.js`, `routes.js`), the correct fix also needed `src/service.js`, a file of the frozen plan scope; `handoff IMPLEMENTED` was refused, the lead asked for an amendment and a second plan approval that nobody could give, and the run ended at PLANNING with every gate stale. Rule: the bound `verify_fix_bound` enforces is the existing union `fix_scope` (finding paths, A77 symbols dropped) plus every path of the frozen PLAN.md `## Scope` whose `criteria:` list shares at least one criterion with a plan-scope path of the failing findings, found with `scope_mappings` (`fix_scope_siblings` in `agent.sh`). A finding path that is not in the plan scope contributes no criteria; a path outside the plan scope, or sharing no criterion, stays refused (scope creep, and the A60 scope approval for unrequested fixes, are unchanged). The gate record's `fix_scope` is not rewritten; `agent.sh next` (open fix round) and the refusal print the computed allowed paths (`fix_path=` lines, `fix_allowed_paths`) for the implementer's `ALLOWED_SCOPE`, and the refusal names the way on (a path the plan never scoped needs the user's scope approval, a PLAN.md amendment and `refreeze`; `amend` works from CODE_DONE only). The regression-test rule (a frozen-scope test path is always inside the fix) is unchanged. Tested by `scenario_fix_scope_shared_criteria` and `scenario_fix_scope_no_criteria` in `lifecycle-test.sh` (the older fix-scope scenarios now give `impl_test.txt` its own criterion). — Alternatives rejected: the whole plan scope in every fix round (no bound: a fix for one criterion could rewrite unrelated files); asking for an amendment (a second plan approval for a change inside the approved plan, the dead end of the run); letting the lead widen `fix_scope` by hand (an unchecked, unrecorded widening by the role that dispatches the fix). — Limits: a plan whose scope entries all list the same criterion lets any plan path be fixed; a file the fix needs that the plan never scoped still needs an amendment.
- **A124. A dispatch in flight is visible, a worker that wrote nothing is BLOCKED with a reason, and the implementer prompt states the window (amends A46, A114).** What: (1) *In flight.* `dispatch.sh` writes `dispatch/<NNN>-<role>-<runtime>.running` (task, role, runtime, pid, start time, "wait for the command to return; do not re-dispatch") before it starts the worker and removes it when the attempt ends; its first lines are `pid=` and `role=`. The marker stays until `finish` (the EXIT trap) removes it, so it covers window-close, metrics and the status check as well as the worker; a retry or failover attempt replaces the previous attempt's marker.
