No signal trap was added: where `sh` runs the EXIT trap on TERM or INT (bash in POSIX mode, as on macOS) the marker goes with it, and after SIGKILL or under dash it is left behind and goes stale. `agent.sh next` and `pipeline` read the marker: with a live pid `next` prints `next=wait: dispatch.sh <ID> <role> in flight (pid N); ...` instead of the dispatch instruction (SKILL.md rule 1 says do what `next=` says, so an obedient lead no longer re-dispatches) and `pipeline` prints `in_flight=`; a marker whose pid is dead is stale, and so is a marker older than `dispatch.timeout_seconds` + 60 s even with a live pid (pids are reused; one attempt cannot outlive its timeout); `next` removes stale markers with a `note=stale dispatch marker removed` line (it mutates state, dead or over-age markers only), so a legitimate retry is never blocked. `next` and `pipeline` name the first live marker and say others may be in flight (`dispatch/*.running`). `check-result` on an empty or missing `.md` with a live marker says `dispatch in flight (pid N): wait for the dispatch command to return` instead of `malformed header: missing ROLE`. (2) *Nothing written.* A worker that exits non-zero (not 124) or yields no result and leaves its log empty gets one line in that log and `dispatch.sh` exits 6 with `BLOCKED_REASON: <role> on <runtime> produced no output (exit N); log: ...` instead of exit 1 with an empty file. (3) *Prompt.* For a role that writes code (implementer, designer while IMPLEMENTING) the dispatch suffix says that `dispatch.sh` already opened the write window (it leaves no file until `window-close` writes `worker-evidence/WINDOW-<n>.yaml`); for every role, without `--prompt-file`, it says that no assignment was given (do the role's default step from the run's TASK.md and PLAN.md); neither is a reason to report BLOCKED. `DISPATCH.md` tells the lead that `D` is synchronous. Why: in a Codex-lead failover the lead issued the verifier `dispatch.sh` and `cat dispatch/*.log` in one parallel tool batch, read the still-empty files as "empty result", re-dispatched, and ended its turn while the second verifier was still running (`agent.sh next` still printed the dispatch line, which the lead obeyed); the harness's 300 s alarm, of which the lead had already used about 3 min 40 s, was a contributing factor and killed both, so both outputs stayed 0 bytes (isolated HOME, `PROOFLINE_REAL_HOME`, A46 and A114 were not at fault: the same Claude reviewer ran fine from that lead, and a hand run with time to finish produced output). In a hand-driven run a Codex implementer was dispatched without `--prompt-file`, found no assignment under `.agents/local/assignments/` and no window (the open window is only a fingerprint held by `dispatch.sh`), and submitted BLOCKED. Verified by `dispatch-test.sh` (0-byte worker, marker while running and gone after, prompt lines present for the implementer and absent for a reviewer with an assignment). Alternatives: refuse a second dispatch of the same role while one runs (explorers and focus-split reviewers legitimately run in parallel under one role name); write the marker into the `.log` (a command-template runtime's stdout is copied to the `.md`, so the marker would become the result); require `--prompt-file` for the implementer (breaks hand-driven runs that rely on the plan alone); a window file the worker can read (a second source of truth beside the fingerprint bracket).
- **A125. Front matter, YAML and TOML must parse in a strict parser, and Markdown links must resolve; a dependency-free test guards both.** What: GitHub rendered `skills/evidence-map/SKILL.md` with "Error in user YAML: mapping values are not allowed in this context at line 2 column 674". The `description:` was a plain scalar holding `: `, which YAML forbids; Claude Code and other runtimes read the same front matter. The audit found the same defect in `exploit-proof` and `proof-review` (the latter also 1318 characters, over the 1024-character `description` limit of the Agent Skills format). Fixes: the three descriptions are double-quoted (text unchanged for `evidence-map` and `exploit-proof`; `proof-review` shortened to 947 characters (with the quotes), dropping the gate-rule and `config` focus detail that its own references already state); `docs/reference/generate-skills.sh` now removes the quotes and escapes of a quoted description (before, `plan-contract` and `proofline` rows kept stray quotes); `skills/proofline-lead/references/LIFECYCLE.md` pointed to a missing `DISPATCH.md#implementer` anchor (now `#3-implementer`); the root `README.md` pointed to the superseded results section of `tests/e2e/README.md` (now the current one); four templates (`data-design` x2, `proofline-lead` completion report, `ui-design` ledger) held unescaped `|` inside table placeholders such as `<yes|no>`, which splits a GFM cell (now `\|`). New `tests/skills/frontmatter.test.mjs` (in `node --test tests/skills/`, and in the always-run `static` CI job so documentation-only pull requests are checked too): a strict YAML subset parser for every Markdown front matter, every tracked `.yaml`/`.yml` and the Codex `.toml` agents (plain scalar with `: ` or a trailing `:`, `#` in `name`/`description`, indicator-led plain scalar, tab indentation, unbalanced quotes or flow collections, text after a closing quote, duplicate keys, missing closing `---`; for skills a `name` equal to the directory and a `description` of at most 1024 characters: that limit comes from the external Agent Skills format, is documented nowhere else in this repository, and the test applies it), and a Markdown check (unclosed fences, relative links and anchors, table column counts, heading level jumps, forbidden `v2`/`2.0` wording, `agent.sh <subcommand>` names in code spans against `agent.sh`, cited `A<n>` against this file). It also checks the known-bad evidence-map shape fails. Why: GitHub was the only thing that noticed, after the release. Alternatives rejected: installing a YAML library (a dependency in a repository whose rule is "nothing is installed"; Node 22 ships no YAML parser); relying on GitHub to flag it (after merge, invisible to agents that read the file). Residual: the parser is a subset (block scalars, flow collections and anchors are checked for shape only, not evaluated); `control-plane/agents/config.yaml` is read by `agent.sh`'s own awk reader, which strips the outer double quotes and never unescapes, so its backslashes inside double quotes are accepted verbatim (a real YAML parser would reject them; the file is not meant for one); Turkish approval words in `agent.sh`, its tests, `docs/decisions.md` and `tests/e2e/tasks/*.tr.md` are product data, so the "English only" rule is not machine-checked.
- **A126. The debug-proof guard ignores a task whose only defect is a declared pre-existing one (amends A122, A105).** What: a COMPLEX feature run (e2e A1, tag books) was refused `handoff IMPLEMENTED` because the A122 word scan matched `fixes` in a Context assumption ("the request fixes only case-insensitivity") and `defect`/`fix` in a Risks line that discusses the `paginate` defect the task had declared under a nested `### Pre-existing defects` with `decision: report`. The lead reworded TASK.md and refroze, which needed a second plan approval the reply cap forbids, so the run stopped at PLANNING. Now, in the A122 scan, Goal, `>` quotes and Acceptance criteria always count; Context, Constraints and Risks count only when the task declares no `## Pre-existing defects` entries (the rule `task_defect_errors` already applies to the request, same section parser, `###` nesting included); an entry with `decision: fix` is a requested fix and always asks for the report. The refusal states both remedies: write `reports/NNN-debug.md` with the debug-proof skill when the task repairs a defect, or declare an unrelated defect as `decision: report` (no reword, no refreeze). `agent.sh next` never ordered `tier` before `handoff IMPLEMENTED` (the lead chained it by itself). Why: a declared defect with `report` is explicitly not part of the request, and discussing it in prose must not make a feature a defect fix. Rejected: reverting the A122 extension (S-6 bug-fix runs would pass without a report again); allowing a refreeze after one approval (weakens the reply cap); dropping the guard for COMPLEX (the pagination miss was a COMPLEX-class risk too). Limit: a real bug fix that also declares an unrelated pre-existing defect and names its own defect only in Context or Risks is not asked; its title, Goal, quotes and criteria still are. A dummy `decision: report` entry costs nothing at plan time; after freeze it needs an amendment and a plan approval and it is named in the completion report; the guard does not check that the entry's path exists or lies outside the plan scope. A `####` heading level is not matched as `Pre-existing defects`.
- **A127. A plan-level VERIFY failure routes to amendment and refreeze, never to a fix round on control artifacts; a submit under a typed token no longer loses its status file (amends A123, A107, A124).** What: a Codex-lead failover check (e2e check 3) ended at VERIFY. The plan's `## Verification commands` held one negative grep; the verifier could not count its own positive greps (A107 re-runs only planned or configured commands) and failed AC-2..4 with a row on `PLAN.md`. `agent.sh next` then offered an implementer fix round with `fix_path=PLAN.md` and `fix_path=VERIFY.md`, frozen control artifacts the implementer cannot edit, and the lead read the docs as "an amendment always needs a scope approval" and stopped to ask for one. (1) `fix_allowed_paths` drops every control artifact of the run (`known_control_artifact`; a path under `.agents/runs/<ID>/` or a top-level control name as findings spell it: PLAN.md, VERIFY.md, TASK.md, RUN.yaml, LEDGER.log, QA_PLAN.md, QA_REPORT.md, EVIDENCE.md, COMPLETION_REPORT.md; no second list), so `fix_path=` never names one; a product path that shares a directory name (`reports/x.csv`, `design/tokens.json`) stays a fix path. (2) `next` counts the blocking rows a plan answers: the row path is a control artifact of the run; script rows (UNSUPPORTED, risk signal) are excluded as `ns_b` does, and row text is never matched, so a code row that says `verification commands fail: expected 3 got 2` keeps its fix round. When every non-script row is such a row there is no fix round and `next` prints `amend PLAN.md ## Verification commands (lead owns it ...), then agent.sh refreeze <ID> <AMENDMENT>; a scope approval is needed only if the amendment adds scope paths`, then the rest of the route: a PLAN.md change gives a new plan hash, which voids the worker evidence (`valid_evidence_file` binds `plan_sha256`) and every gate, so the implementer is re-dispatched to re-record RED and GREEN (a real failing test, then a real change: GREEN is refused when no implementation file changed since RED; a path with a `tdd_exemption` needs no evidence), then `handoff IMPLEMENTED`, then every gate again, VERIFY included. A commands-only amendment on a non-exempt path therefore has no honest RED: the plan's Verification commands must be complete before freeze, and `next` says so; when the verifier merely failed to cite a configured or planned command, A107 rows get a hint to re-dispatch it (`dispatch.sh <ID> verifier`) instead. Evidence validity is unchanged (integrity). `amend` refuses before CODE_DONE (a reopen needs a finished run), so the route is the amendment file under `amendments/`, the PLAN.md edit and `refreeze`; a refreeze asks for a `scope` approval only when the new plan adds scope paths and for a `budget` approval only when the fix budget is exhausted (both unchanged, asserted). `scenario_plan_level_verify_fail` walks the route to CODE_DONE. A gate mixing plan and code rows keeps its fix round, now without control paths. (3) GATES-AND-FIXES.md and GATES.md say exactly this. Anomaly: the haiku verifier recorded two FAILs (003, 004) yet `d001-verifier-claude.status` never existed, so `dispatch.sh` read "no submission" and re-ran the verifier on sonnet (005). `submit` writes the status under `--agent` when typed, else `PROOFLINE_AGENT`, and writes nothing when the token is empty; a rejected submit also writes a file, so every submit of that attempt ran with an empty token. The generated role files tell a worker to pass `--agent <token from your start context>`, a hook-supplied id that a headless `claude -p --agent` worker never receives; a typed empty value overrode the token `dispatch.sh` exports, while the sonnet rerun omitted it and wrote `d002`. Product defect in token precedence; the exact typed value is inferred, because the worker transcript is not kept. Now `PROOFLINE_AGENT`, when set, wins over `--agent`, unless the typed id is a subagent the hook registered (SubagentStart writes `.agents/local/submissions/<id>.started`): a nested subagent inside a dispatch worker inherits `PROOFLINE_AGENT` and would otherwise write the worker's status file and be blocked by the SubagentStop hook; lead-native subagents have no such variable and keep `--agent`. And the `dispatch resubmit` ledger note carries `token=` and `status_files=` so a missing file shows next time. Why: the control plane must not depend on a model copying a token it was never shown. Rejected: a dispatch fallback that accepts a recorded result without a status file (parallel dispatches of one role, or a lead-side `record`, make the attribution a guess, and a false accept skips a gate); rewording the role files only (a model can still type a wrong token); a second fix-path list for control artifacts (drifts from the registry); letting `amend` run before CODE_DONE (it reopens a finished run). Limit: a plan row is recognised by its path only; a row that complains about the plan without naming a control artifact gets a fix round, and the lead's diagnosis (GATES-AND-FIXES.md step 1) covers it. The subagent marker is a convenience, not a boundary: `submit` checks that some `<id>.started` exists for the typed id, not that it belongs to the caller, so a worker can type another live subagent's id, and an inline interpreter (`python3 -c "open(...,'w')"`) can write into `.agents/local/submissions/`, the same gap as every other `.agents/local` file; the impact is limited to writing that subagent's status file. SubagentStop removes its marker after its own status check; markers of a subagent that never stops are not cleaned up (`cleanup_run` does not know the ids; they are empty files under git-ignored `.agents/local`).
- **A128. The e2e harness answers every pending plan approval, also the second one after an amendment, and reports its reply cap (amends A95, A120).** What: three COMPLEX runs (A1, B1, REG) ended with an unanswered second plan approval. Cause, two defects in `tests/e2e/run.sh`: (1) `pending-kind.sh` read the approval kind only from `agent.sh next`, but after an amendment during a fix round `next` still prints the fix-round step (`agent.sh handoff T-1 IMPLEMENTING`) while the lead has already asked `request-approval T-1 plan` (`approvals/003-request-plan.yaml`, no answer); the kind was empty and the loop took the question path; (2) there, the commit/push guard grepped the lead's message, which holds the approval question with its "accepted answers: ... commit it, push it ..." list, found "commit it", and broke silently (no `stopped=` line). Fix: `pending-kind.sh` takes the run's `approvals/` directory and, when `next` names nothing, reads the newest file: `NNN-request-<kind>.yaml` is a request nobody answered (any kind, so a commit or scope request is still never answered); the file slug is mapped back to the kind (`kind_slug` in `agent.sh` only turns `:` into `-`, so `waive-F-1` is `waive:F-1`); the decision moved to `tests/e2e/reply-decision.sh`: only exactly `plan` is answered as an approval, every other kind (and any unknown one) stops unanswered, and with no kind the lead's text is searched line by line for a commit or push request, skipping the accepted-answers line of an approval question (English `accepted answers:`, Turkish `kabul edilen onay sözcükleri:`; a genuine commit request is also covered by the newest approvals file); the reply cap is checked only when a reply would be sent and then ends the run with `stopped=max-replies` and the pending state (plan replies stay counted in `plan_approval_replies` and in the cap, default 6). C-14 (tests/e2e/expected/COMMON.md) says at most 3 harness replies were needed; with the default E2E_MAX_REPLIES of 6, any COMPLEX run with an amendment and refreeze now legitimately shows 4+ replies: decision needed from the maintainer (EXPECTED not changed). Tests: `pending-kind-test.sh` builds `approvals/` directories (second plan request, every kind slug, both accepted-answers labels); `reply-loop-test.sh` runs the real loop of `run.sh` against a stub lead (plan pending until the cap gives `stopped=max-replies`, every other kind gets no reply). Rejected: letting the lead run `approve` (the approval is the user's reply); answering any lead message containing "approve plan" (the text is also in the accepted-answers list of questions); removing the cap (a lead that asks forever must stop); excluding plan approvals from the cap (an unbounded loop is the failure the cap exists for).
- **A129. Freeze and refreeze refuse a TASK.md acceptance criterion that maps to no scope path and has no explicit test (amends A101, A127).** What: a Claude lead froze a TRIVIAL plan whose AC-2 ("No other change") was in no scope entry's `criteria:` and had no named test. `freeze` only checked that each scope entry has a non-empty `criteria:` (A101); `validate-plan.mjs` would have said `AC-2: maps to no scope path and no explicit test`, but the lead never ran it, so the defect surfaced at VERIFY (`PLAN maps AC-2 to no scope path ... command proof requires tdd_exemption on every mapped PLAN scope path`) and cost an amendment, a refreeze and a re-recording of the evidence (A127). Now `agent.sh freeze` (so `refreeze`, which is `freeze` with an amendment), right after the A101 check and before anything is recorded, runs the plan-contract validator (`.agents/skills/plan-contract/scripts/validate-plan.mjs PLAN.md TASK.md --class <class>`) and refuses only on its two coverage errors, `<AC>: maps to no scope path and no explicit test` and `scope <path>: maps to no criterion`, quoted verbatim, with the fix: add AC-n to `criteria:` of the PLAN.md scope entries that implement it, or name an explicit test for it in `## Tests`. Every class, TRIVIAL included. Every other validator error stays advisory at freeze. Like the other validator calls it runs only where the skill and `node` are installed. `agent.sh next`: when a failing VERIFY row says an AC maps to no scope path or that command proof requires `tdd_exemption`, the plan-level route adds the right edit target, the `criteria:` of the PLAN.md scope entries (front matter) and a planned command proving the AC, not only `## Verification commands`. Tests: `scenario_freeze_ac_coverage` (TRIVIAL plan, AC-2 unmapped while every scope entry has criteria: refused, naming AC-2; accepted once mapped; refreeze refused, then accepted with an explicit test) and the `next` text case in `scenario_plan_level_verify_fail`. Existing fixtures are unchanged: they do not install the plan-contract skill, so the check is skipped there. Why: a plan defect must be refused at PLAN time, by the same rule the validator applies, not found by the verifier. Rejected: running the whole validator at freeze (unrelated checks such as sections, class limits or Assumptions would block freezes the lead can still repair later; the contract stays advisory); leaving it to the lead (the lead did not run it, and the cost is a whole round); catching it at VERIFY (the status quo: late and expensive); a second coverage rule in `agent.sh` (would drift from the validator). Limit: without `node` or the installed skill the check is skipped; a row is recognised by its text for the `next` hint only.
- **A131. The e2e harness chooses the scripted question reply per scenario, and replies to a question only when one is really open (amends A95, A120, A128; CRITICAL K-3, K-5, K-6, C-14).** What: a CRITICAL regression run on main 9e70f03 (FAIL 30/35) answered every lead question with one generic text ("Use your recommended option for every open question."). The intent-grill question's recommended option was the non-destructive one ("stop using the column, keep the data"), so the reply steered the task to `destructive: no`: no destructive stop, K-3, K-5 and K-6 could not occur; the generic text also could not settle the later high-risk assumption question, and a 4th reply went out when none was open (`stopped=no-open-question` came only afterwards, because the lead's explanation held a question mark). Fix: (1) `run.sh` uses `tests/e2e/replies/question.<SCENARIO>.txt` (line 1) as the question reply when the file exists, else line 1 of `replies/<SCENARIO>.txt`; plan replies still come from line 2 of the generic file. `question.CRITICAL.txt` is the user's intent only: the data in the legacy column is no longer needed, never keep it, the column should go. It must never carry process or design words (stages, expand/contract, ordering, a destructive stop, "never run a migration"): those are what the product must discover and do itself (K-3, K-6, K-13), and a reply that supplies them leads the witness; only the keep-or-discard decision belongs to the user (K-16). It creates no approval: the approval grammar (`text_has_approval`) rejects any reply without an allowlisted phrase, and the reply holds no such phrase and no question mark (the test checks it against `approval_phrases` of `agent.sh`); a blanket reply never creates an approval (A60, A106, A108). (2) `question-open.sh` takes the task id: a question mark in the lead's last message counts only when no task exists yet (the intent-grill question is chat-only) or `agent.sh next` names no `agent.sh` step; a recorded pending question (`a question is pending`) always counts. A lead that explains why a blanket reply is refused, while `next` names a concrete step, gets no reply. The harness still never answers a destructive, single_step, scope, budget, commit, push or waive request. This file is harness INPUT (the user's words), not an answer key: every EXPECTED file is unchanged. Tests: `reply-loop-test.sh question-file` runs the loop for CRITICAL and COMPLEX against a stub lead (CRITICAL sends the per-scenario text, COMPLEX the generic one) and checks the text against the approval allowlist; `pending-kind-test.sh` covers the new open/none cases. Rejected: one reply text per scenario holding several branches of answers (the harness would be reading the model's wording); having the harness answer `accept <id>` (an assumption acceptance is the user's own decision); removing the question-mark rule (the intent-grill question is chat-only). Residual: a chat-only question while a task has a named next step gets no reply, and the run ends as `stopped=no-open-question`, which is visible.
- **A130. `NOT_RERUN` is a gate-record field, not a findings row; the completion report names every finding id and every not-reproduced gate (amends A107, A98).** What: A107 made `submit` add an info findings row `NOT_RERUN: <gate>:<focus> no reproduced evidence; this gate is not reproduced proof` to every non-verifier gate that re-ran nothing. Three e2e runs (TRIVIAL, STANDARD, STANDARD.tr) then had a lead write 'findings none' or 'no findings' for gates whose record carried that row, which an evaluator scored untruthful (C-22); the COMPLEX run failed C-22 the same way (fix round 1 where the pipeline said 2 of 2, REVIEW_DATA labels that did not match the gate), so the lead takes fix-round counts and labels from `agent.sh pipeline` and the gate records; the STANDARD report also described an info row that lived only in a report file, and `publish-completion-report` checked headings only, so a report with no finding ids was accepted. Now: (1) `submit` writes the marker as the gate-record field `not_rerun: "<gate>:<focus> no reproduced evidence; this gate is not reproduced proof"` (same style as the A98 `unsupported:` field, carried to `record` by a `NOT_RERUN:` trailer line of the result file) and adds no findings row, so 'findings none' is true for a clean gate. (2) `agent.sh pipeline` prints `not_rerun.<GATE>:<focus>=NOT_RERUN (not reproduced proof): <reason>`; `next` tells the lead to list each in the report. The old info row of records made by an earlier version is read the same way (`risk_not_rerun`). (3) `publish-completion-report` refuses a report that does not name, for every required gate, the id of every finding row of the current gate records (info rows included; UNSUPPORTED rows stay under A98's `## Unsupported Checks`), the refusal naming the gate and the missing ids; `none` is therefore accepted only for a gate with no finding row. The id must stand on a line that also names the gate apart from its ids, so 'scenarios QA-1 to QA-9' does not name a QA finding; every miss is collected and reported in one refusal with the line to add, and `agent.sh next` lists each gate's ids and not-reproduced lines before the report. The `NOT_RERUN:` trailer is sanitised (one line, no quotes, backslashes or control characters, 300 characters) and a focus matches exactly. It also refuses a report without the line `<GATE>:<focus> ... not reproduced (NOT_RERUN)` per `not_rerun` gate and one that calls such a gate reproduced. verify-proof rules 9 and 11, PROTOCOL, the lead's REPORT.md section and the report template say so. Tests: `sc_evidence_gap_gates` (field, no row, empty findings, `pipeline` line), `sc_evidence_gap_legacy` (old info row still honoured), `sc_report_finding_ids` (omitted id refused, `none` for a gate with an info row refused, missing or contradicting not-reproduced line refused, complete report accepted). Why: a bookkeeping marker must not pollute the findings a human or report reads, and a report must not be able to skip the findings. Rejected: telling the lead to mention info rows (an instruction the lead already had and missed twice; nothing checked it); deleting the marker (A107's semantics, that a gate without a re-run is never cited as reproduced proof, would be lost). Limit: the `NOT_VALIDATED` info row (validator skill not installed) is still a findings row and must now be named by id; the id match is textual (an id anywhere in the report counts).
- **A132. Each explorer's scratch report path is per dispatch, `decide` bounds explorer slots, and `git -C $VAR <subcommand>` is not a stash (amends A113, A111; X-4, M-2).** A COMPLEX regression run ended with three explorer results against `max_explorers: 2`. Cause: both parallel explorers wrote their findings to the same scratch file (`scratch/r.md`, a name each picked), the second overwrote the first before `submit`, `reports/001` and `reports/002` had the same content, and the lead dispatched a third explorer for the "lost" one. A113 made the REPORT name unique but left the scratch INPUT name to the model, and nothing enforced the limit. (1) The SubagentStart hook text, the SubagentStop resend text and `dispatch.sh` (which now claims its sequence number before it builds the prompt) name the exact file `.agents/runs/<ID>/scratch/<token>-report.md`; `roles/explorer.md` and evidence-map say to use it or `--report -`. `submit` refuses an explorer `--report <file>` whose path is not `.../<token>-...` (a delimited component, not a substring; a stdin report, the BLOCKED reason and a tokenless submit are exempt). (2) `agent.sh decide <ID> explorer` refuses when the slots of the planning phase are taken. A slot is a DELIVERED report (an explorer result with `RESULT: DONE` recorded after the last `freeze`/`refreeze` ledger event) or an explorer dispatch still running (`dispatch/*-explorer-*.running` with a live pid). BLOCKED and NEEDS_INPUT hold no slot (the retry and the ANSWERS re-dispatch complete the same slot), nor does a dispatch that returned nothing, so a lost slot is re-dispatched without exceeding the limit. The count restarts at each freeze and refreeze, so an extra explorer after a plan amendment is allowed; a limit of 0 (TRIVIAL) is not checked here. The refusal names the limit, the delivered results and the running count. Native Task starts pass `decide` too (the lead calls it before every dispatch). (3) The A111 text safety net counted any `git -C $VAR ...` as a stash: its pattern allows `-C` as a bare flag and then reads the `$` of the flag's value as "a variable where the subcommand goes". Three command lines of the run (`git worktree add ...` with `git -C $W/wt status`, `git -C $WT status`, `git -C $W apply`) were denied as `git stash` although none contains the word. The awk now skips such a match only when the option is not itself a value (`git -c -c $S`), and what follows the value is whitespace and a bare literal word (`status`, `apply`); a quote, `$`, backtick, `-` or the end after the value keeps the count (`git -C $W "$S" list`, `git -C -C $S`, `git -C $W -C $S`, `git -C $W $S list`), and a real `git -C $W stash` still matches longer. A111's bypass battery is unchanged; these cases are new DENIED tests beside it. HONEST LIMIT: the three real command texts (kept verbatim in `tests/enforcement/a132-commands/`) are no longer denied as a stash, but they are STILL refused, now by the A97 write rule ("the command writes `$W/wt/$f` ... which cannot be resolved"), because they copy or redirect to a path built from a shell variable. That rule is correct fail-closed behaviour and is not changed here; such commands need literal write paths, so the stash false positive is fixed for `git -C $VAR` commands that write nothing through a variable, not for these three texts. Rejected: a counter file for slots (a second source of truth beside `results/`); counting decisions or every result file (a crashed, BLOCKED or NEEDS_INPUT dispatch would block its own retry); a Task-tool hook denying the Nth+1 subagent (the lead already passes `decide`, and the hook cannot read the class); `submit` choosing the scratch name (the file must exist before submit); resolving variables assigned earlier in the same command in the write rule (a new parser inside a deny rule). An explorer counts once however often it resubmits (distinct allocated reports, not result files), and a running dispatch whose submission is already recorded counts as its delivered result, not twice. Test hygiene (same change): `test-lib.sh`, `selftest.sh` and the other self-tests now exit 2 when their temp directory cannot be created, because with an unusable `TMPDIR` a fixture was built in the current directory (the real repository) and committed into it; `dispatch-test.sh` runs a test-lib script with a missing `TMPDIR` in a throwaway repository and checks exit 2 and no commit or config change. Residual: a lead that starts several explorers in one call before any dispatch marker exists is bounded only by the next `decide`. Known limits: (a) the stash net's new `match()` with a dynamic regular expression was run locally with macOS awk only; mawk and gawk (CI's awk) are covered by the CI selftest, not by a local run. (b) A quoted variable or substitution in subcommand position (`git "$S" list`, `git -C "$W" "$S" list`) is not seen by the net; this A111 limit existed before A132 and is unchanged.
- **A133. End-to-end items are tagged `[invariant]` or `[quality]`; C-14 allows 3 answers +1 per refreeze (maintainer decision 2026-10-17; amends A95, A131, C-14).** What: (1) Every numbered item of `tests/e2e/expected/` (COMMON, TRIVIAL, STANDARD, STANDARD.tr, COMPLEX, CRITICAL, FAILOVER, CAPABILITIES) carries exactly one tag after its title; no item is removed, loosened or reworded beyond the tag. `[invariant]` is a security or process guarantee and must hold in every run; `[quality]` depends on model behaviour and is scored as a rate. A doubtful item stays invariant. A run passes when every applicable invariant item is met and the quality met-rate (met / applicable) is at least 90%; CAPABILITIES `N-` items follow the same tags. (2) C-14 now reads: at most 3 answers, +1 for every refreeze (answers are harness replies, plan approvals and question replies together; each refreeze after an amendment allows one more); tagged invariant. This closes the open item in `tests/e2e/README.md`. (3) `tests/e2e/evaluate.md` tables get a tag column (after the status column, so the benchmark parser is unchanged) and the verdict line is `E2E: PASS|FAIL (invariant <met>/<applicable>, quality <met>/<applicable> = <pct>%)`; the `CAPABILITIES:` line likewise. Why: one model slip in a wording item failed a whole scenario (COMPLEX passed twice in 11 runs), while security and process guarantees must never be traded for a rate. Quality items (all others are invariant): F-9 (report content), X-3 (acceptance-criteria content), X-9 (which tests the run wrote), K-4 (contract text in the plan). Kept invariant on purpose although they depend on the model: C-22 (a false claim in the report is an evidence failure), K-12, K-6 (what the stop message says), S-3 to S-5 (the fix itself), S-11 (states that commit and push await approval), K-2 (evidence), K-3 (the `destructive` flag drives K-6, K-7 and K-9), X-10 (carries the design-sync VERIFY outcome). Rate: invariants are judged per run and must be 100%; the quality rate is met / applicable quality items pooled per scenario over all runs of that scenario in the campaign (a single run also reports its own rate), and the scenario passes at 90% or more. Known limit: results in `tests/e2e/README.md` were scored before the tags and are not re-scored; no scenario was re-run.
- **A134. A full approval sentence approves, for every kind; the approval stays fail-closed (amends A108).** What: "I approve the plan" and "Planı onaylıyorum" were re-asked: the A108 grammar has no word `i`, and the Turkish object `planı` is a filler, not the kind word `plan`. Now `text_has_approval` also approves a reply that, after the A108 normalisation (ASCII case folding, punctuation and apostrophes removed), EQUALS one full sentence of its own kind (`approval_sentences`): `i approve|i approved <object>` and `<object> onaylıyorum|onayliyorum|onayladım|onayladim`, optionally with the run id (`... for <ID>`, `<ID> için|icin <object> ...`). Objects: plan `the plan | planı, plani`; destructive `the destructive step | the destructive change | yıkıcı adımı, yikici adimi | yıkıcı değişikliği, yikici degisikligi`; single_step `the single step | tek adımı, tek adimi`; scope `the scope | kapsamı, kapsami`; budget `the budget | another round | bütçeyi, butceyi | bir round daha`; commit `the commit | commit'i`; push `the push | push'u`; `waive:<ID>` `the waiver of <ID> | <ID> feragatini` (the finding id is required, as before). Whole-reply equality, so "I approve the plan but not the migration", "onaylıyorum ama ...", "maybe I approve the plan", "I do not approve the plan", "planı onaylamıyorum", "approve?", an empty reply, a sentence quoted INSIDE other text (the reply is then no longer equal to the sentence), while a reply that is only the quoted sentence (`"I approve the plan"`; quotes are punctuation) still approves, and another kind's sentence ("I approve the commit" for a plan, another run id or finding id) stay unapproved and are re-asked; the question mark rule, hash binding, per-capture single use (A106) and the A108 word grammar are unchanged. The approval question shows the first English and the first Turkish sentence of its kind, capitalised as in the docs (`or the whole reply as one full sentence`). Turkish case folding stays ASCII only, so an upper-case non-ASCII letter (`BÜTÇEYİ`) does not match; the ASCII variants and lower-case forms do. The sentence list is built in, not read from `approval.phrases`. Why: the maintainer decided that approval stays fail-closed and that the natural full sentences users type (and `docs/guides/prompt-catalogue.md` quotes) must work. Tests: `scenario_approval_fail_closed` in `lifecycle-test.sh` (every sentence of every kind except waive approves, the listed negatives do not, under the C locale) and `sc_waiver` in `gates-test.sh` (waive sentences, bare `the waiver`, wrong id and wrong kind refused). The harness replies of `tests/e2e/replies/` (`Plan approved.`, `Plan onaylandı.`) are unchanged and still approve (`reply-loop-test.sh`). Rejected: adding `i` and the Turkish object forms to the filler list (loosens every reply: "i approve" plus any kind word would pass in any order); a denylist for the new sentences (A108's finding); an id-less `the waiver`.
- **A135. A Codex lead runs on the base model, never the cheapest (amends A100).** What: `execution_policy.lead_base_model.codex: gpt-6-sol` in `control-plane/agents/config.yaml` is the single source of truth (the lowest model of the Codex ladder `gpt-6-luna gpt-6-sol gpt-6-astra` that meets the lead tier floor 2; it is also the shipped economy lead row). `exec-policy.sh check-lead --runtime RT [--model M]` exits 3 with `LEAD_BELOW_BASE` (naming the base model) for a lead model below it and `UNKNOWN_MODEL` for one outside the ladder; an unset model is refused (`LEAD_MODEL_UNSET`: the runtime default cannot be verified), so the caller passes the model it really runs. When an installed `.agents/config.yaml` lacks the key the base is derived from the ladder and the lead tier floor of `roles.conf`, so enforcement never turns off, and `proofline doctor` warns about the missing key. `tests/e2e/run.sh` runs it on `E2E_CODEX_MODEL` for a Codex lead and for the FAILOVER resume, before the first `codex exec` and every `codex exec resume` (both use the one variable); with `E2E_CODEX_MODEL` empty it defaults to the base model, so `-m` is always passed, so `E2E_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-luna` now exits 2. `proofline doctor` fails with `lead model:` when the Codex lead resolves below the base and passes otherwise. Workers (implementer, tester, reviewer, explorer, verifier) and mixed runs with a Codex worker may still use `gpt-6-luna`. Why: the lead plans and decides; a floor-class model cannot carry that, and A100 let the harness select it. Alternatives: docs only (rejected: the maintainer wants it enforced); raise `lead` tier floor to 3 (rejected: the economy profile deliberately leads on the standard tier). Not covered: a lead launched outside the harness, by hand with `codex` and its own default model, is not seen by the resolver (doctor checks the model the policy resolves, not the one a human typed).

- **A136. Merging a pull request requires every check green, enforced on the merge path by a wrapper and a hook, not by an instruction (amends A41, A111; CONTRIBUTING "Merge when CI is green").** What: the maintainer's rule is that nothing is merged unless CI is completely green. A written rule was not enough, so the merge path itself checks. (1) *Wrapper.* `proofline merge <PR-NUMBER> [--merge|--squash|--rebase] [--delete-branch] [-R OWNER/REPO]` (`bin/lib/merge.sh`, in the CLI because it must work in a repository that has no `.agents/`, such as this one; default method `--merge`). It runs a fresh `gh pr view <PR> --json number,state,isDraft,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` and refuses unless the answer is for that PR, `OPEN`, not a draft, has a 40-digit head SHA and a NON-EMPTY rollup in which every check run is `COMPLETED`/`SUCCESS` and every status context `SUCCESS`. Pending, failed, cancelled, timed out, stale, neutral and unknown entries refuse (neutral and cancelled are not green); no checks at all refuses (green cannot be proven). A `SKIPPED` check run passes only when `gh pr checks --required` does not list it as required and every required check is a pass (the CI of this repository skips whole jobs on documentation-only pull requests and `visual-browser` on every pull request, and GitHub itself counts a skipped check as passing; a skipped REQUIRED check refuses). Then the head SHA is read again with a second `gh pr view` and must equal the checked one, and the merge runs as `gh pr merge <PR> <method> --match-head-commit <sha>`, so GitHub itself refuses if the head moved after the check. Fail closed, naming what was seen: gh or jq missing, gh failing (offline, not logged in, no such PR; gh's text is quoted), output that is not the expected JSON, a PR argument that is not a plain number (a URL or branch name cannot be verified). `--admin` (overrides the checks) and `--auto` / `--disable-auto` (merges later, without a fresh check) are refused by the wrapper itself. (2) *Hook.* `proofline-hook.sh` runs a merge guard on every PreToolUse Bash call for every caller (lead, subagent, headless worker), with or without an active run, AND in a project where proofline is not installed (when the plugin hook is on, it protects every repository the session works in; every other hook rule stays a no-op without `.agents/config.yaml`). On the scan records it denies: `gh pr merge` whatever the spelling (the words `pr` and `merge` among the arguments of any command word that is not a printing or searching word, so `-R o/r`, flags between the words, `GH_TOKEN=x`, `env`, `command`, `sudo`, `timeout`, `nohup`, `xargs`, `ssh host`, `sh -c`/`bash -lc` (also nested), quoting, an absolute path and a variable as command word are all seen; `--admin` and `--auto` are one more case of the same denial); `gh api` whose arguments name a merge endpoint (`.../pulls/N/merge`, `.../merges`), `mergePullRequest`, `enablePullRequestAutoMerge`, `enqueuePullRequest`, `auto_merge` or a `git/refs/heads/<main|master>` update; `gh alias` (an alias could hide `pr merge`); `git push` with a protected branch as the destination (`main`, `master`, `canonical_branch`, the `origin/HEAD` branch; `+main`, `HEAD:main`, `x:refs/heads/main`, `--all`, `--mirror`, a refspec built from a variable or substitution), and a bare push or `push origin HEAD` while a protected branch is checked out in the directory the command runs in (`git -C <literal path>` is followed; an unreadable `-C`/`--git-dir`/`--work-tree` is protected); `git merge` while a protected branch is checked out, or in a command that switches to one (`--abort`/`--quit`/`--continue` pass); `git update-ref refs/heads/<protected>`. Every denial message names `proofline merge`. Read-only `gh pr view/checks/list`, `gh api` reads of other endpoints, feature-branch pushes, `git merge` on a feature branch, `git pull --ff-only`, commit messages and `echo`/`grep` text that mention `pr merge` are allowed. (3) *Runtimes.* The guard is the same script for Claude Code (plugin hook and project install) and Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`), so the denials are identical where the hook runs. Codex limit: project hooks load only when the project is trusted and reviewed (`/hooks`), and the Codex wiring calls `.agents/hooks/proofline-hook.sh`, which exists only in an installed project, so a Codex session in a repository without proofline installed has NO guard and only the wrapper's own checks; a headless run needs `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`. Codex tool names other than shell are not scanned. Tests (`tests/enforcement/merge-guard-test.sh`, a stubbed `gh` on `PATH`, a throwaway repository under `$TMPDIR`; no git config outside it is touched): all green merges with `--match-head-commit`; red, pending (check run and status), neutral, cancelled, no checks, null rollup, head mismatch, draft, merged PR, wrong PR number, malformed SHA, unparsable output, gh failing, `--admin`, `--auto`, a URL, gh missing, jq missing and a skipped required check are refused with the reason; a skipped non-required check merges; about 60 spellings of a direct merge are denied by the hook (with the wrapper named) and the wrapper, feature-branch pushes and read-only commands are allowed; the guard also runs in an installed project. The hook half fails against the hook of `main`. Rejected: an instruction in the lead's prompt (the point is that an instruction is not enough); a GitHub branch-protection rule alone (needs repository admin rights, is not part of this repository, and `--admin` bypasses it for an owner; recommended in addition, not instead); requiring a wrapper-issued token file for `gh pr merge` (a second state file, and the hook cannot tell whether the file is fresh); letting `--admin` through with a reason (the maintainer decision is that it is always denied); `--auto` through the wrapper (it merges later, after a check this wrapper did not make; the lead re-runs `proofline merge` once CI is green); counting a SKIPPED check as a failure without condition (it would block every pull request of this repository: `visual-browser` is skipped on all of them). Known limits (a heuristic on the command text, like A111): (a) a script or program the model writes and then runs, `sh -c "$VAR"`, `eval`, a command word built by the shell at run time that is not `gh`-adjacent, `gh api -F query=@file` and a merge through the web UI or another tool than Bash are not seen; with a run active the existing rules (`eval`, non-literal command word, nested shells) already refuse several of them, with no run they pass. (b) `gh pr list --search merge`-like commands that carry the words `pr` and `merge` as separate arguments are denied (one retry with other words). (c) `git pull` of a feature branch into a checked-out `main`, and `git branch -f main`, create a local merge or move without a push and are not denied; the push to the remote is. (d) The `--required` lookup relies on gh's text `no required checks` to tell "none required" from a failure; any other error refuses. (e) The wrapper needs `jq` (the hook needs `jq` or `node`). (f) A project that does not load the hook at all (plugin off, no install, Codex untrusted) is protected by nothing but the wrapper, which the model can skip; the maintainer should keep branch protection on as well. Review round 1 (this supersedes the text above where they differ). WORDING: the guard denies the spellings it can read; it does not make a merge impossible. GitHub branch protection with required status checks is the fail-closed backstop and must stay on. (i) `git push -o -n origin main` and `git push origin main -o -n` were read as a dry run: the value of `-o`/`--push-option`/`--receive-pack`/`--exec`/`--repo` is now skipped, and only a real `-n`/`--dry-run` flag lets a push through; `--repo=X`/`--repo X` supplies the remote, so the next word is a refspec. (ii) Denied without a run and without an install: a variable, substitution or backtick where the `gh` subcommand goes (`m=merge; gh pr $m 7`, `gh pr "$M" 7`, `gh pr $(echo merge) 7`, `gh $SUB merge 7`, `gh api $EP`; a literal subcommand followed by a variable, `gh pr view $N`, is fine); `curl`/`wget`/`http`/`https`/`xh`/`xhs`/`aria2c` aimed at `github` with a `pulls/N/merge`, `merges`, `git/refs`, `contents`, `graphql` or `auto_merge` path; `gh api` with `--input`, a field read from a file (`=@`), a `mutation`, a write (`-X`/`-f`/`-F`/`--field`) to `contents/`, or to `git/refs|commits|trees` that names main/master or a variable; text with `gh pr merge`, a merge endpoint, `git merge` or a push to main/master that is piped, here-doc'd or here-string'd into `sh|bash|zsh|dash|ksh`, passed to `python|node|ruby|perl|php|lua -c/-e`, `awk system(`, `eval`, or a `git -c alias.X=!...`; `git merge`/`git push` after a `cd` the text cannot resolve (`cd -`, a variable, `pushd`, a `cd` in a subshell or pipe), after `env|sudo -C`, or with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`--git-dir`/`--work-tree` (the directory is then unknown, which is protected); a `PATH=` assignment (env or export) in a command that names gh, merge or proofline; any command naming `PROOFLINE_SELFTEST`. (iii) The wrapper resolves `gh` and `jq` itself, prints `using gh at <path>`, refuses a PATH with an empty or `.`/`..` entry or an existing relative directory, and refuses a gh or jq found in the project, the working directory or a temp directory unless `PROOFLINE_SELFTEST=1` (the tests set it; the hook denies a model command that names it). (iv) The wrapper now ALWAYS asks `gh pr checks --required` and refuses when a required check is not a pass or is missing from the rollup, which covers a workflow that has not registered its check yet right after a push; with no required checks configured, an empty rollup still refuses, but a rollup that holds only the checks registered so far looks green, so a repository without branch protection and with late-registering workflows (workflow_run) can still be merged too early. HONEST LIMITS, not covered: a script or program the model writes and then runs (its text is not scanned), a payload assembled at run time (`'gh pr '+'merge'`, base64, a file read by an interpreter), `eval`/`sh -c "$VAR"` that does not match the text sinks above, an HTTP client with the URL in a variable or file, a gh extension, the GitHub web UI or another tool than Bash, a fake `gh` placed in a system directory, `git pull` of a feature branch into a checked-out main and `git branch -f main` (local only), and a `cd` into a main checkout hidden behind a variable inside a subshell (denied as unknown only when the text shows the `cd`). Not tested: a real GitHub repository (the stub replays gh's JSON shapes; `statusCheckRollup` and `gh pr checks --json name,bucket` follow the documented gh output), Codex and the plugin wiring end to end, mawk/gawk (CI's awk) on the new scan paths beyond the existing selftest run.
- **A137. A user who already said the data is not wanted and the column should go is not deferred or refused at intake (amends A131, A32, A55; CRITICAL K-3, K-5, K-6).** What: a CRITICAL regression run on main 3fefcd5 never left intake (3 replies, then lead-4 refused a 3rd relay). Evidence: the task author's round 1 asked D-2 with options (a) export values and keep the column, drop as a follow-up | (b) keep values, drop as a follow-up | (c) discard and drop here, 'needs your explicit approval', recommended (a); the harness reply (intent only, A131) answered the data question but no letter; round 2 asked 'drop in this task or a follow-up (D-6)', (c) 'the workflow doesn't allow me to write that criterion'; round 3 asked 'Shall I take (a)?'. Root cause: not the harness. `roles/task_author.md` carried one unconditional rule: criteria only for the non-destructive step, the drop is a follow-up, 'Must not write a criterion that needs the drop'. So even after the user said the values are not wanted and the column should go, the task author kept offering the deferral as the recommended option, asked a process question (this task or a follow-up; intent-grill rule 5 forbids implementation questions) and called the user's own intent unwritable. An intent-only reply cannot answer a question whose options differ only in step order. Fix: (1) `roles/task_author.md` splits the rule: when the fate of the values is open it asks only that and writes the non-destructive step; only when the user's OWN words say explicitly that the stored values are not wanted (or may be discarded) AND that the column should go does it write the whole removal as criteria (app no longer reads, writes or returns it; the column no longer exists after the new migration), leave the order of steps to the plan, and never offer the deferral as the recommended option, ask whether or when to drop, or refuse the criterion. Hedged, partial or inferred wording ('maybe', 'no longer need the column') is not that statement and gets the data-fate question (keeping or discarding data is the user's decision, K-16). The destructive stop is the safety (A55), not an intake refusal. (2) `roles/data_architect.md`: such a task gets the drop as a `contract` step, a separate later migration, still `destructive: yes`, still behind the destructive approval (A32 unchanged; `single_step` stays forbidden). (3) `tests/e2e/replies/question.CRITICAL.txt` is UNCHANGED (A131): the role fix has to prove itself alone, and a reply that adds 'now, not later' leans toward an answer key. No EXPECTED item, safety rule or approval grammar changed; no answer key. Tests: `tests/skills/task-author.test.mjs` (role text and generated agent carry the explicit-statement rule and the hedge rule; the reply file stays intent-only and unchanged); both fail on main. Not tested: a live CRITICAL run (the next regression round decides). Rejected: letter replies per question number (an answer key, A131); loosening the budget of 3 replies (C-14).
- **A141. The freeze accepts a destructive step in phase `contract` (a separate, later migration file) as well as `deferred` (amends A52, A55, A137; CRITICAL K-3, K-6).** What: after A137 the CRITICAL run left intake but stopped in PLANNING with no PLAN.md. Conflict: `roles/data_architect.md` (A137) plans a requested column drop as a `contract` step (`design/DATA.md` S3, `| S3 | contract | drop_column | ... | yes |`), but `plan_migration_shape` (`control-plane/agents/scripts/agent.sh`, awk `if (dest == "yes") { if (ph == "deferred") late = 1; else early = 1 }`) and `migrationShape` (`skills/plan-contract/scripts/validate-plan.mjs`) counted only `deferred` as late, so the `contract` step counted as early (one-step) and the shape was `missing`; `single_step` is forbidden for it (A52). The lead refused to patch around it. Why a rule fix: `deferred` means not in this change's diff (data-design M4 fails if it is); a task whose user said the data is not wanted and the column should go has acceptance criteria that need the drop in this change (A137), so `deferred` cannot carry it, while `contract` is the phase MIGRATION.md already defines for drops after no code reads the old shape. K-3 asks for a drop 'in a separate, later migration', which a distinct migration file after the stop-reading step is. Fix: both shape checks treat a destructive step in `contract` or `deferred` as late; a destructive step in `expand`, `backfill` or `switch`, or a destructive plan with no preceding non-destructive step, is still one step and refused. Unchanged: the plan is `destructive: yes` (A55), CRITICAL, the destructive approval after FREEZE and before IMPLEMENT bound to the PLAN.md hash (A69, K-6), `single_step: yes` only with the task's own words (A52) and then its own approval, the destructive-SQL hook. Tests: `tests/skills/plan-contract.test.mjs` (fixture `fixtures/plan-contract/critical-data-section.md` is the plan section of the CRITICAL run: accepted; `single_step`, drop in expand and a missing header refused; the old assertion that `contract` is one step now asserts it is accepted), `gates-test.sh` refreeze scenario uses a `contract` step through freeze and the destructive approval. Not tested: a live CRITICAL run. — Rejected: planning the user's wanted drop as `deferred` (cannot meet the A137 criteria, reintroduces the intake stall); allowing `single_step` for it (A52).

- **A138. A docs-writer skill and a shared writing profile (`writing:` config block).** What: (1) `control-plane/agents/config.yaml` gets `writing: { profile: auto|ste|plain, strictness: relaxed|strict }` (defaults `auto`, `relaxed`); `agent.sh config-check` validates both values and refuses an unknown `writing.*` key. `auto` means English text follows a simplified-technical-English style (`ste`) and Turkish text a plain-language style (`plain`). (2) The profile is written once in our own words in `tests/shared/writing-profile.md`: instruction sentence at most 20 words, explanatory sentence at most 25, paragraph at most 6 sentences, noun phrase at most 3 words, one instruction per sentence, active imperative instructions, one word per thing, warning as instruction then risk. `tests/shared/check-writing.mjs` measures only the first three (sentence and paragraph length; front matter, code, tables, headings, comments and link targets ignored; a list item or a sentence that opens with a base-form verb is an instruction), prints the other five as judged, and exits 1 only under `strict`. Per D29 each skill carries a copy (`references/WRITING.md`, `scripts/check-writing.mjs`); `tests/shared/check-shared.sh` fails when a copy differs. (3) New skill `docs-writer` with modes `create`, `update` (diff or range) and `audit`, owned by the architect role (no new role) and reachable as `/proofline docs create|update|audit`. Its evidence script `scripts/check-docs.mjs` proves that quoted repo-internal links (and anchors), file paths, `--flags`, project subcommands and config keys exist and prints `doc:line: <kind> not found: <claim>`. (4) Knowledge step (`LIFECYCLE.md` section 7): a task that changed user-visible behaviour also runs docs-writer `update`; documents under `knowledge_scope_root` in the step, other documents as paths in the frozen plan scope. No new gate, no new state. Why: documents drifted from the code and no check named the missing fact; sentence length was a matter of taste. Alternatives rejected: one shared file read by several skills (D29); a language model to judge length (a script decides, models propose); checking noun phrases and voice by script (needs a parser, false positives); a new docs gate (cost; the knowledge step already exists); copying a standard's text or glossary (we summarise the rules in our own sentences, D33). Tests: `tests/skills/docs-writer.test.mjs` (both scripts, config validation, copies identical) and `fixtures/docs-writer`. Not tested: Turkish text (the instruction heuristic is an English first-word check, so for other languages the sentence class can be wrong; relaxed only warns); a live docs run.
- **A139. A persistent project wiki: the `llm-wiki` skill, `/proofline wiki`, and `docs/wiki/` as default knowledge scope.** What: new skill `skills/llm-wiki` (0.0.1), structured like the reference workflow's wiki: the folder `docs/wiki/` with `CLAUDE.md` (rules), `KNOWLEDGE-PIPELINE.md`, `index.md`, `log.md`, `lint-report.md`, `raw/sessions/` -> `sources/<kind>/` -> `concepts/`, plus `entities/`, `decisions/`, `lessons/`, `syntheses/`, `archive/`; pages join through `[[slug]]` links and carry `title`, `status` (`current|accepted|archived|contradicted`), `source` (a repository file that exists) and, for a contradicted page, `contradicts`. The two rule templates ship as `assets/CLAUDE.template.md` and `assets/KNOWLEDGE-PIPELINE.template.md`. Scope: no new config key. `docs/wiki/` is added to the default `knowledge_scope_root` (now `DESIGN.md docs/design/ docs/adr/ docs/wiki/`), so the existing `in_knowledge_scope` logic applies unchanged (an existing install keeps its own `knowledge_scope_root`, so a wiki write stays implementation scope there until the user adds `docs/wiki/`; the new default applies to new installs): a path under the prefix is knowledge work, any other path is implementation scope; Transaction A reads the wiki on demand and read-only, Transaction B (optional, only for a changed durable contract) ingests, logs, lints, then `knowledge-done`. `.agents/KNOWLEDGE.md` states the flow. One dependency-free validator `scripts/validate-wiki.mjs` is the lint: it writes `lint-report.md` and checks exactly missing `source`, a `source` that is not an existing repository file, invalid `status`, contradicted without `contradicts`, duplicate titles, broken `[[wikilinks]]` (errors, exit 1) and possible orphans (warning); the report is never read as input. `/proofline wiki ingest|query|lint` is routed to the lead (slash command only); the lead role lists the skill. Differences from the user's earlier private llm-wiki skill, where the reference structure wins: `[[wikilinks]]` instead of relative Markdown links; a `source:` repository path instead of a `sources:` list that may hold task IDs (a task ID is history, run directories are disposable); `docs/wiki/CLAUDE.md` as the schema; a status set with `accepted` and `archived`; `log.md` as a dated bullet list of real operations only; no query log entry inside Transaction A; lint also writes `lint-report.md` and checks provenance, duplicate titles and statuses, but no longer checks stale claims, missing concept pages or one-way links (judgement checks stay with the agent); `raw/sessions/` for factual session summaries. Why: knowledge a run produces is otherwise rediscovered by the next run, and the knowledge transaction is the one place where documentation writes are already scoped and checked; reusing `knowledge_scope_root` adds no mechanism. Rejected: `wiki.enabled` and `wiki.path` keys (redundant with the scope root; never writing under it is the off state); a new gate or role; a terminal `proofline wiki` command; copying run artifacts into the wiki. Tests: `tests/skills/llm-wiki.test.mjs` (7), `fixtures/llm-wiki` (selfcheck plants seven defects), and `sc_wiki_knowledge_scope` in `control-plane/agents/scripts/gates-test.sh` (a wiki path is knowledge scope, a path outside is not). Not tested: a live run that writes the wiki (no e2e scenario).

- **A142. An explain-html skill (`/proofline explain <topic|TASK-ID>`).** What: new skill `explain-html` (architect, standalone) explains a topic, a task, a review or a completion report as one self-contained HTML page: inline SVG diagrams, inline CSS and JS, light and dark theme, semantic landmarks, `lang`, SVG titles, visible focus, fluid layout, no video. The page text follows the writing profile (copy of `tests/shared/writing-profile.md`, checked by `check-shared.sh`). A task id is read from `.agents/runs/<TASK-ID>/` (`TASK.md`, `PLAN.md`, review files, `COMPLETION_REPORT.md`); a missing file is named on the page, not guessed. Output goes to `.agents/local/explain/<slug>.html`, already ignored by `proofline init` (`.agents/local/`) and by the skill's `.agents/local/.gitignore`; it is copied elsewhere only when the user asks. `scripts/check-html.mjs` checks only: an external reference (URL scheme, `//host`, `fetch`, `import`, `@import`, `<link href>`, `<script src>`, non-data `<img src>`; the SVG `xmlns` is allowed), a non-empty `<title>`, a size of at most 500 KB. Why: a page is the quickest way to understand a run, and an offline file is safe to open and share. Contrast, landmarks and layout are judged by the agent, not by the script. Version 0.0.1. Rejected: a new gate or role (an explanation proves nothing about the product); an HTML parser or an accessibility engine in the validator (a dependency for a check the agent can judge); a CDN or web font (breaks offline use and leaks the read); an e2e test (the validator test and one fixture are enough for a page generator).

- **A140. The README states status and model expectations briefly; every end-to-end result lives only in `tests/e2e/README.md` (amends A132's documentation rule).** What: the root README lost the "Support levels" table and all per-scenario results. It gains "Status" (version 0.0.1, Claude Code primary, Codex, mixed and failover experimental, a count of more than 900 automated tests) and "What to expect from AI behaviour" (guaranteed invariants versus model-dependent output, a lead needs a base-level model). The tier and adapter rows moved to `tests/e2e/README.md`. The CONTRIBUTING checklist now asks that the README "Status" claims no more than the tests show. Count method: 736 passed (`node --test tests/skills/`) + 42 passed (`sh tests/fixtures/check-fixtures.sh`) + 149 self-test units (`SELFTEST_LIST=1 sh tests/selftest.sh`, equal to the sum of the six CI shards) = 927, written as "more than 900". Lead rule stated as the code has it: only `exec-policy.sh check-lead` (doctor, e2e harness) refuses a Codex lead below the base model or without a model; no other runtime has a base model configured.

- **A143. Read roles change nothing in the project tree, and the completion report's numbers come from the records (amends A71, A111, A130; C-3, C-22).** What: (1) *Read roles.* QA, reviewer, security reviewer and verifier (found by the same caller identity as every other hook rule: the `proofline-<role>` agent type, or `AGENT_ROLE` in a headless worker) may not change a file of the project working tree while a run is open. The PreToolUse hook denies Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit on a project path, redirections, `tee`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `truncate`, `dd of=`, `install`, every in-place editor (`sed -i` in all spellings, `perl -i`/`-pi`, `ruby -i`, `awk -i inplace`, `patch`, `ed`, `ex`, `vi`, `vim`; the hook reads every operand that is an existing project file) and the git subcommands `checkout`, `apply`, `stash`, `reset`, `restore`, `clean`, `switch`, `rebase`, `merge`, `pull`, `rm`, `mv`. A git command is allowed when its effective directory (`git -C`, `cd`) is a registered worktree other than the project (A111 rules, extended). The old rule exempted any command that contained `git -C`, `git worktree` or `--work-tree` from the git check; `git -C . checkout -- f` and `git worktree list; git checkout -- f` passed. For a read role the exemption is gone: each git command is resolved on its own, and a wrapper (`find -exec`) that hides the directory is denied. A target the text cannot resolve (unexpanded variable, substitution, a `..` component, a directory that does not exist yet) is read as the project. The denial says where the evidence worktree is: create it under `$TMPDIR` in its own call (`git worktree add --detach "$TMPDIR/<name>" HEAD`), then use its literal path. Allowed in the project: the role's own run files (`owns.conf`) and `.agents/runs/<ID>/scratch/`. The role texts say it (mutation and trials only in the evidence worktree). The lead, the implementer, the designer and the explorer are not affected. (2) *Report facts.* `agent.sh report-facts <ID>` prints a Facts block from the records: class, required gates with status and every finding id, fix rounds used of the maximum, refreezes (ledger), files changed (task-owned paths), worker-evidence run records (total, ended pass, ended fail; a RED record ends fail on purpose, so this is not a count of failing tests). `publish-completion-report` removes an earlier block, validates the report as before (the generated block never satisfies a check), refuses a number in the lead's text that is not a recorded value, then appends a fresh block. The check reads digits and the English number words one to twenty ("Two tests"), directly beside the words (a verb as in "step 3 tests the lookup", "test files", "test cases", "test suites" and "0 tests failed" are not counts): before them (`7 tests`, `3 required gates`, `2 fix rounds`, `1 refreeze`) or after them with `:` or `=` (`tests: 40`, `gates: 5`), fenced code skipped. Allowed values: tests = the worker-evidence run counts; gates = the number of required gates and 0; fix rounds = used and the maximum; refreezes = the ledger count. The lead skill, the report template and `next` tell the lead not to count. — Why: the rule that a read role never changes the project tree was only partly enforced: the git check was skipped by any command that contained `git -C` or `git worktree`, and `ed`, `ex`, `ruby -i` and `awk -i inplace` were not seen. C-22 asks that a report claim points to a record, but the counts of tests, gates and fix rounds were typed by the model (A130 saw a wrong fix-round count). — Known limits: a script that writes by itself (`python -c`, `node -e`, an npm script) is not seen; no record carries the number of individual tests, so only run counts are checkable and any other test number is refused; other phrasings ("cases", "assertions", numbers in table cells, number words above twenty, Turkish number words) are model text and are not read; the read-role guard works only while a run is active; for a read role `find -delete`, `find -exec <writer>` and `xargs <writer>` must start in a registered evidence worktree (`xargs` is judged by the directory the command ends in; a read-only `xargs grep rm` can be refused by mistake); a read role's variable evidence-worktree forms such as `W=$TMPDIR/x; git -C $W apply` are now denied on purpose (A132's `git -C $W apply` case changed): create the worktree in its own call and use its literal path; `python`/`node` writes are unseen; a fix round written as the ordinal of one round (`fix round 1`) must equal a recorded value too; report-facts shows gate status for the current tree, so it reads `stale` after publish changes the task file. — Rejected: a new gate or role (the existing hook and publish step are enough); parsing free prose (not deterministic); letting the lead copy the numbers (the model would still type them); a variable table for `W=$TMPDIR/x; git -C $W ...` (the A111 rule of a literal path that exists is simpler).

- **A144. The README shows only the short story, `proofline help` lists every session command, and `proofline init --role ROLE=RUNTIME` sets a per-role runtime (amends A140; reuses `runtime.roles` of D6).** What: (1) *README.* The risk-signals bullet shrinks to three sentences (which risks add checks; an unrunnable check is UNSUPPORTED and never a pass). Its full text and the whole "Capabilities and what tests them" section, with the table and the counting paragraph, move to the new page `docs/concepts/testing.md` (long sentences were split for the writing profile, every claim unchanged; the risk-signals paragraph became a short intro, one bullet per focus and two closing paragraphs); the README links to it from "What it is" and "Documentation". The "Status" test-count sentence stays. The quick start gains the `--role` line and two notes: the wiki has no on/off setting (start it with `/proofline wiki ingest README.md`), and Codex needs one `/hooks` approval in the project folder. `proofline doctor` already warns about that approval whenever Codex is a runtime (`codex trust`); it cannot check the approval itself, so the note says "warning", not "failure". (2) *Help.* `proofline help` adds `docs create|update|audit`, `explain <topic|TASK-ID>` and `wiki ingest|query|lint` to "agent session", and the CLI dispatches them like `review`, `audit` and `debug` (it prints the instruction for the lead's session, with a usage error for a missing or unknown subcommand). A CLI test extracts the session commands from the help and from the routing row of `skills/proofline/SKILL.md` and fails when they differ in either direction. (3) *`init --role`.* The flag repeats; each value is `ROLE=RUNTIME`. ROLE must be a file name in `roles/*.md` (lowercase letters and underscore only), RUNTIME must be `claude` or `codex` and must be in `--runtimes`, like `--lead`. An empty, malformed, unknown-role or unknown-runtime value stops `init` before anything is written. The value goes to `runtime.roles.<ROLE>`; the last value of a repeated role wins. `runtime.roles` was already read (`exec-policy.sh runtime`, used by `agent.sh decide` and so by `dispatch.sh`; validated by `config-check`), so no read change was needed. The only code change outside `init` is that `cfg_set` in `bin/lib/config.sh` now also writes a 3-level key under an existing 2-level parent (`init` adds the parent `roles:` when an older config lacks it, turns a hand-edited `roles: {}` into a parent line, and refuses any other inline value with a message). Why: a reader should see what the project is and how to start in one screen; help and the entry skill must not drift; and a mixed team (for example a Codex implementer under a Claude lead) needed a hand edit of the config. Rejected: a new gate or role (none is needed); validating roles from a hard-coded list (the roles directory is the source); a `--role` that skips the `--runtimes` check (a role on a runtime that is not set up would fail at dispatch). Not tested: a real mixed run with an overridden role (the CLI test checks the config and the policy lookup).

- **A145. Standalone deliverables go to their project location after approval, evidence stays local; DESIGN.md defaults under `docs/design/`; task-author splits, sizes, sprints and optionally distributes work; project-wide decisions are ADRs with supersede (amends D10, D26).** What: (1) *Output.* A standalone skill writes its deliverable to the project location only after the user approves it. Evidence, ledgers and raw output stay in `.agents/local/<skill>/<target>/`, git-ignored. (2) *DESIGN.md.* The default moves to `docs/design/DESIGN.md`. An existing install keeps its path; `upgrade` offers the move and never moves the file. (3) *task-author.* Splits a large request into tasks, sizes each S, M or L, and groups them into sprints. Optional team distribution reads `.agents/local/team.yaml`, git-ignored, so no names reach the repository; assignments are informational. Tasks gain optional fields `size`, `sprint`, `assignee` and `depends_on`. (4) *Decisions.* A project-wide decision from an intent grill becomes an ADR; a new ADR that contradicts an older one supersedes it. A task-level decision stays in the task. The existing ADR mechanism is reused. Why: deliverables belong where the team reads them; evidence does not belong in the repository; team names stay out of the repository. Rejected: a new decision store (duplicates ADRs); writing deliverables without approval; moving DESIGN.md automatically on upgrade (rewrites user files); team names in the repository (privacy); a `[task]`/`[project]` extra column in INTENT (breaks validate-intent), so the prefix goes on the question cell. Known limit: the rule "the team question is not asked again when `.agents/local/team.yaml` exists" is checked only against the SKILL.md text; no product code reads `team.yaml` (accepted by the maintainer). Known limit: the planning block (`size`, `sprint`, `assignee`, `depends_on`) sits after the `# Task:` H1 and its optional **Status:** line, so `agent.sh` keeps reading the H1 on line 1. Known limit: in markdown.sh `strip_plan`, a planning block with no closing `---`, or a plain `---` horizontal rule as the first content after the H1, makes the rest up to the next `---` be treated as the block; the failure is loud (import reports MISSING fields), nothing is lost. Follow-up (separate job, not done now): task Markdown is parsed in three places (markdown.sh import, markdown.sh create, validate-task.mjs); move to one shared reader later. Known limit (fixed in 0.0.4): in validate-task.mjs `knownIds`, the inner `names` variable shadowed the outer one, so the file-name match `<ID>-*.md` never fired. Known limit: without `--tasks-dir`, the lookup also scans the file's parent directory, which is lenient; in run directories a `TASK.md` neighbour can add the id `TASK`, while unknown ids are still rejected.

- **A146. UI direction alternatives, redesign without DESIGN.md, a judged `character` aspect, font rationale (0.0.4; amends A145).** What: (1) ui-design offers 2-3 directions derived from evidence; the user picks one and the pick is recorded; never for `conform`. (2) A redesign from code without a DESIGN.md keeps the component inventory and does not use the current visual language as a reference. (3) visual-proof judges a `character` aspect for COMPLEX and CRITICAL when the basis is new or redesign; the `--ui` flag supplies the basis. (4) Font rationale: self-hosted web fonts, licence, performance. (5) DESIGN.md holds only the system. (6) Fix: task-author `depends_on` finds a task by the file name `<ID>-*.md` (the shadowed `names` variable of A145 is fixed). Why: output was generic, a redesign without DESIGN.md had no path, and character drift was never checked. Rejected: a new agent; a new mode; a separate visual-quality file; aesthetic rules in the validator; a style catalogue. Known limit: without a task file the validator cannot check `task_quote` against the user's sentence, only that it asks for a visual change. Known limit: `character` is required only when `--ui` supplies the basis. Known limit: the self-approval check does not scan the alternatives text. Known limit: the `character` judgement is the model's and never closes the gate alone.

- **A147. False-alarm fixes, method-skill precedence, foreign-context warnings, implementer TDD record, proven commands (0.0.5).** What: (1) visual-proof does not measure a non-HTML response (`not_measured`); content a setup injects is registered with `mark(el)`, a function handed to the setup script (not a page global), and is hidden and skipped while measuring; overflow inside a closed `<details>`, `[hidden]` or `[inert]` is ignored while the page has no horizontal scroll. (2) During an active run proofline's method skills (TDD, debug, review, plan, UI audit) are used instead of overlapping skills from elsewhere; language- and ecosystem-specific skills stay free; files other skills produce go to the run's `scratch/`. No skill is blocked. (3) `proofline doctor` warns, never FAILs, about foreign SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks and about skills whose name overlaps a method skill, and about empty `commands.build|test|lint`. (4) The implementer instruction spells out the `tdd.json` block; a retry on code that already exists gets RED from the test run in a separate worktree at the base revision, then GREEN, without asking the user. (5) When `commands.*` are empty and the run proved a command, the lead asks one question after cleanup to write them. (6) `plan_section_present` no longer prints a grep error when PLAN.md does not exist yet. (18) The knowledge step (wiki ingest, `design_docs`, ADR, lesson candidates) also runs for a FAILED or BLOCKED run: `agent.sh knowledge-done` accepts them (no ledger entry, so cleanup still sees `terminate` last) and the lead command is `/proofline knowledge TASK-ID`. `delivery-check` and `draft-pr-body` refuse until `knowledge_state` is `KNOWLEDGE_DONE` or `not_applicable`; `proofline deliver` reports it. docs/wiki, docs/design and docs/adr are knowledge scope, so they are inside the delivery scope. Why: a run that failed still teaches something, and a pull request must not outrun it. Why (earlier items): a real run had 858 blocking visual rows that were all probe side effects, a Codex implementer returned RED/GREEN without the JSON block (`validate-tdd.mjs` exit 2), and foreign skills and hooks competed with the proofline method. Rejected: blocking other skills (ecosystem skills are useful and the gates verify the result whichever skill produced it); auto-merging a FAILED run's pull request. Known limit: the visual-proof setup script runs in the page's own JS world, so page code that intercepts it could obtain `mark` and hide an element; the gate guards against accident, not a hostile page. Known limit: the stray-file deletion rule (baseline of untracked files at the run's first hook event) cannot tell a file the user created later from one the run created, and a run already in progress without a baseline deletes nothing. Known limit: the draft pull request for a FAILED run is printed as a `gh pr create --draft` command and opened by the lead after the push approval; `proofline deliver` does not open it. Known limit: the content fingerprint still includes `.agents/` files, so a user edit to `config.yaml` can stale gates; only the scope check and tier ignore it. Known limit: Claude subagent token counts depend on `agent_transcript_path` or a path derived from `transcript_path`. Known limit: a run created before `knowledge_state` existed can neither pass delivery nor record the knowledge step (recreate or edit the run). Known limit: `knowledge-done` writes a ledger entry also under the open-run check removal; the FAILED-run draft body printed by `deliver` merges stderr into the body.

- **A148. 0.0.6, efficiency: selective gate repetition, one recorded build and test per commit, plan sections, interactive intake, digest.** What: (1) Each gate records the set of files it looked at; after a change only gates whose set changed go stale.
