The PreToolUse hook denies a model command that produces evidence (`agent.sh build-record` and `verify-*`, test, build and lint runners, a reviewer's, security reviewer's or verifier's `git diff`/`git show`) without that prefix, but only when `rtk` is on `PATH` and a settings file names it; `ls`, `git status`, `git log` and exploration reads stay free. Why: a compressed test or diff is not evidence. Rejected: `exclude_commands` (cannot separate evidence from exploration); a proofline config switch (the user's hook is the fact, not a setting).
- **A195. 0.0.35, a repeatable real-session smoke test (related A100, A117).** What: `tests/real-session/smoke.sh` drives a real Claude Code session with a cheap model (`SMOKE_MODEL`, default haiku, economy profile) in a throwaway fixture with a local bare origin: `/proofline run` (a TRIVIAL task whose implementer writes a file), `/proofline deliver` and a two-task `/proofline batch`, with the script playing the user (approvals, the merge on the origin). It prints a step-by-step PASS/FAIL table and checks that every Skill-tool call was redirected. With rtk installed it runs a second pass that also loads the user's settings (so the rtk hook is active). CONTRIBUTING: a pull request that changes hooks, skills, roles or the control plane runs it and pastes the table. It is not part of CI and not part of `selftest.sh` (it calls a model). Rejected: running it in CI (cost, secrets, flakiness); reusing `tests/e2e/run.sh` (it scores a whole scenario against EXPECTED files and takes far longer).
- **A196. 0.0.35, a Codex worker in a run worktree can take the shared lock, and the lead can record any proofline failure as friction (amends A185, related A171).** What: (1) since 0.0.33 a run in a worktree keeps approvals, metrics, prompts, batch and friction state and the lock that guards them in the main tree's `.agents/local` (A185), and `agent.sh submit` takes `<main>/.agents/local/.lock` (a `mkdir` in that folder). `dispatch.sh` gave a Codex worker only the worktree's own `.agents/local`, so a Codex implementer in a worktree edited its files and then failed at `submit` ("cannot take the lock ... its directory is not writable"; seen in real use, TASK-011). The shared lock moves to its own folder, `<main>/.agents/local/locks/shared.lock`, and when the run's root is a worktree under `<main>/.agents/local/worktrees/` dispatch adds exactly `<main>/.agents/local/locks` as one more `--add-dir`. `approvals/`, `prompts/`, `windows/` and `batch/` of the main tree stay read-only to the worker (write access would let it forge an approval record or a captured user message, the hole closed for the lead in 0.0.26); `submit` writes nothing else in the main tree. Old installs: a main-tree process still takes `.agents/local/.lock` as before, and a worktree process waits (read-only) for a live holder of it before taking the new lock, so an upgrade with a run in flight keeps mutual exclusion. The worktree's own `.agents/local` stays a writable root as before (not widened by this change). A run in the main tree gets no extra root. The code comment names the reason. (2) `agent.sh friction-note <ID>` accepts a third controlled kind, `proofline_bug`, for any proofline failure the lead worked around; the friction report counts it on its own line, apart from "asked to run a command". Why: the lead could not record the lock failure because only the two user-command kinds were accepted. (3) The smoke test (A195) runs its batch with a Codex implementer when Codex is installed. Rejected: granting the main tree's whole `.agents/local` (it holds approvals and captured user messages); a lock path inside the worktree (two worktrees would no longer exclude each other); free-text friction kinds (they could carry identifying text into the report). Not-tested: a real Codex sandbox in the self-tests (the argv is checked with a fake runtime and the write access with file permissions; the smoke test exercises the real one when Codex is installed).
- **A197. 0.0.35, freeze warns about a document path in scope without `tdd_exemption` (related A147).** What: a path in the plan scope that is a document (under a `design_docs` document, the knowledge scope, or an entry of the new `verification.doc_paths`, default `docs/ *.md *.mdx *.rst *.adoc`; a directory entry ends in `/`, `*.ext` is a suffix) and has no `tdd_exemption` makes `agent.sh freeze` print ONE warning line on stderr that names the paths and the fix (a specific exemption, or a proof such as design-sync finding the drift first and then passing clean). Freeze does not stop. The plan-contract skill says the same under "Tests are scope". Why: in real use a plan wrote `DESIGN.md` into scope without an exemption; the missing RED/GREEN showed only after the implementer finished, and the fix was an amendment, a refreeze and a rewritten QA plan. Rejected: stopping the freeze (a project may prove a document by a test); `*.txt` in the default list (fixtures and product files use it).
- **A198. 0.0.35, code that is already edited without RED is bound by put-back, RED, restore, GREEN, and the instructions now say it (amends A147).** What: the recorder (`worker-evidence`) already supports the path: it refuses GREEN unless an implementation file differs from its state at RED, so RED must be recorded while the change is put back and GREEN after it is restored. The implementer instruction (A147) told the opposite: RED from a separate worktree at the base revision, GREEN in the live tree; that RED is never recorded, and a RED recorded with the change in place makes GREEN fail. `roles/implementer.md` (and so the generated agent files) and the tdd-proof skill (5a) now spell out, for changes that someone else left in the tree before the implementer started (never its own work): save the changed file, put it back to the base content with the edit tool (a failing stub for a file the plan creates, never a deletion), run the test, record RED, restore, record GREEN, all in one turn; asking the user for missing evidence means the path failed. The GREEN refusal names the same way out. Test: an earlier implementer edits inside its window and records nothing, the next one binds it and the handoff accepts it; RED with the change in place is refused at GREEN with the put-back hint. The smoke test (A195) runs this takeover as a step. The first smoke run showed why the limits matter: told to "put the change back", an implementer deleted its own new file to get RED and could not restore it (parked batch task), so the text now excludes the implementer's own work and forbids deleting. Rejected: a recorder switch that accepts RED from a worktree (the record would claim a run the recorder never saw); letting the next implementer adopt an unattributed tree (the mutation-ownership check exists to refuse that).
- **A199. 0.0.36, a Codex worker gets a permission profile that lists its writable paths one by one (amends A196, related A185).** What: `dispatch.sh` no longer starts a Codex worker with `-s workspace-write` and `--add-dir` folders (which made the whole `.agents/local` of the run's tree writable, including `windows/`, the implementer's write windows). It selects the Codex permission profile `proofline-worker` (`default_permissions`, `extends = ":workspace"`, defined with `-c`, built by `codex_profile_args` in `dispatch.sh`): `.agents` read-only; writable only `.agents/runs/<ID>` (report, result, gate record, worker-evidence, ledger), `.agents/local/locks`, `.agents/local/submissions`, in a worktree also the main tree's `.agents/local/locks`, and the git `worktrees` folder (mutation evidence); the run's own `approvals/` and `waivers/` are read-only again. The same profile applies to a Codex worker in the main tree. Windows, approvals, prompts and batch are read-only in both trees. To make that possible every lock now lives in `.agents/local/locks/`: a tree takes `locks/shared.lock` (main tree) or `locks/tree.lock` and the main tree's `locks/shared.lock` (worktree); the old `.agents/local/.lock` is still taken where the folder is writable (so an older process is excluded) and, where it is not, a live holder of it is waited for, never written. Verified in a real Codex sandbox without a model (`tests/real-session/codex-sandbox.sh`, `codex sandbox -P`, Codex 0.165 on macOS Seatbelt): a worker writes product files and its own record paths, `agent.sh submit` and the evidence recorder succeed, and writes to windows, approvals, prompts, batch, the run's approvals and the rest of `.agents` are refused, for a run in the main tree and in a worktree; the smoke test's Codex step (`SMOKE_ONLY=codex`) repeats the probe against the installed scripts and runs a two-task batch with a Codex implementer. Limits: `worker-evidence/WINDOW-*.yaml` files sit in a folder the worker must write (RED and GREEN records), so a forged window record there is stopped by the delivery checks (mutation ownership, scope), not by the sandbox; a profile path rule applies to paths that exist when the process starts (dispatch creates the folders first). Why: the 0.0.35 report named the open `windows/`. Rejected: keeping `--add-dir .agents/local` and relying on the delivery checks; a profile file in the user's `config.toml` (proofline never edits the user's Codex config).
- **A200. 0.0.37, retro findings of TASK-011/012/013: less proofline-caused rework, no core invariant loosened (amends A147, A157, A171, A185, A188, A196, A199; related A153).** What: a measured retro (about 28 percent of the time of two tasks was rework the process caused, about 31 percent task size) produced 24 items, each shown in code first and then fixed; none may loosen a gate, an approval or an evidence rule, and CONTRIBUTING now names six "Core invariants" that bound this and every later patch (item 22). One line per item, "what it speeds up | why no core invariant is loosened" (item 23: every item was checked against the six rules; none needed an exception, so none was left out):
  - item 1: pre-flight questions (path-limit split, document `tdd_exemption`, new dependencies, unmeasurable criteria, the reason for a class) are asked task by task, with lettered options, in the batch summary instead of at freeze at night, where they parked tasks | answers are recorded only from the user's captured message (`batch-answer`, `batch-answers`), a split answer is capped at the ceiling the summary showed and only while the batch approval stands, new dependencies stay unapproved (the task parks), an exemption or class answer only adds a freeze note, content paths are still hashed and reviewed. `path-kind` and `validate-plan.mjs` share one rule (content and document paths do not count towards the path limit; a file with code is never content) and warn while the plan is written.
  - item 2: build record and VERIFY stop waiting on empty `commands.*` | `doctor --commands` / `--apply-commands`, the plan step and the batch summary find the commands, prove them by one run and propose them in one question; written only after a proof run and only on the user's "approve commands" or a batch approval naming that proposal, an unproven command is never written, a missing build record goes to the lead as `MISSING STEP (lead)` and not to the reviewers as a note. Known limit: the legacy `proofline init` path still writes unproven discovered commands unless `--verify-commands`.
  - item 3: no debug-proof round for a task that merely says "fix" | the trigger is the task type or label (`bug`, `defect`) and `decision: fix`, which still require the proof and all gates; an unlabelled task that fixes a bug is not blocked by the script, only the reviewer may ask for the root-cause proof.
  - item 4: task-author splits code from work that needs a user decision (design rationales, text approvals) and the PLAN template shows a document `tdd_exemption` | guidance only, no gate, approval or exemption logic changed.
  - item 5: after a fix round or amendment a gate re-runs when the fingerprint of its inputs changed (`focus_untouched` and `gate_inputs_unchanged` in `agent.sh`), not all of them | a `pass` REVIEW_PLAN, RULES, DATA or SECURITY record is carried over only when every changed path is a test path (SECURITY also needs that no changed test touches security behaviour: identity, authorization, input validation, secrets); SECRETS, REVIEW_SMALL, REVIEW_TESTS, QA and VERIFY always run; any product, dependency or configuration change or an undeterminable delta runs everything; refreeze invalidates only gates whose fingerprint changed. Known narrowing: REVIEW_PLAN and RULES are not re-run on a test-only fix round, as the item asks.
  - item 6: the visual verifier reads the pattern rationales and audit notes of DESIGN.md, and a FAIL that the gate counted as PASS is gone | only a rationale approved by the user downgrades a finding: approval kind `rationale:<pattern-id>`, bound to the sha256 of the exact DESIGN.md line, recorded only from the user's reply (`design-rationales` lists them); an agent-written rationale never passes a finding, a FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE report never counts as PASS, and a PASS needs an independent `reviews/visual-proof/report.json` that says PASS.
  - item 7: the design audit is cached by page content (`design-audit.mjs`) | the judged review is reused only for pages whose screenshots are byte-identical, the measurement is always recomputed, any difference is judged again. The browser part of the cache is not exercised in the test environment.
  - item 8: the verifier re-run tolerates volatile fields (`repro-normalize`) | a narrow, tested list: ISO timestamps, `HH:MM:SS`, durations after in/took/duration/elapsed/time or in parentheses, a trailing duration on the `[build] Complete!` line; counts, names, pids and exit status stay exact, so a real difference is never normalized.
  - item 9: `next` and a gate's FAIL message show the real finding and the real remedy (no "amend PLAN.md ## Verification commands" when `report.json` is missing), and `refreeze` and `amend` errors show the expected format with an example | message text only, no check changed.
  - item 10: in a batch the lead does not stop at CODE_DONE; it delivers and starts the next task itself and gives one status line during long waits | no gate or approval is touched; delivery is still covered by `batch-cover` under the batch approval.
  - item 11: `batch-next` holds back a task that depends on, or touches the same code path as, an earlier unmerged task, and the hook denies more ways for the lead to advance a protected branch | only adds refusals.
  - item 12: `decide --agent-path` refuses a role the config gave to another runtime (Codex) and names the dispatch command | adds a refusal only.
  - item 13: `knowledge-done` checks the page, the secret scan and the wiki lint before DONE, and the check `handoff DONE` objected to moved there | the same checks, earlier; it fails closed when the lint cannot run (`node` or `validate-wiki.mjs` missing) and has no waiver path.
  - item 14: `next` and the completion report remind the lead of `friction-note proofline_bug` and the report counts the notes | a reminder only.
  - item 15: a dropped connection or an SSL/TLS error is retried on the same runtime, resuming from the RESUME note, at most `dispatch.network_retries` (default 3, at most 6) times after `dispatch.network_backoff_seconds` (default 15, doubling, at most 300 s) | the retried step must still submit through `submit`, so the fingerprint and hook checks are unchanged; a task failure, a timeout and a sandbox that blocks the network (`workspace routing discovery failed`) are never retried.

Verification: `sh tests/invariants/invariants-test.sh`, the gate, batch, lifecycle, enforcement and CLI suites, the A200 scenarios of the smoke test (`SMOKE_ONLY=a200`, not in the default run because they use a real model).

Now the baseline emulates `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` explicitly, checks `matchMedia`, and reports "not measured" when the baseline still reports reduce or the reduced emulation did not take effect. `motion-diagnostics.json` and richer assertion messages make a CI failure diagnosable. Two deliberately broken fixtures (a CSS animation entrance, a JS-triggered entrance) in `fixtures/visual-proof-design/motion/` and an OS-level reduced-motion test keep the check's power. Evidence: reproduced locally with Chrome's `--force-prefers-reduced-motion` (old code a false PASS, new code FAIL); manual CI run 40888400754 on the branch: `static` (macos-latest) and `visual-browser` (macos-latest) pass where they failed before.   - D10 only launchers remain (listed in the ADR: `agent.sh`, `dispatch.sh`, the two git hooks, `bin/proofline`, `bin/proofline.cmd`, the pinned hook command strings, and `proofline-hook.sh` as a transitional launcher in stages 10-14); a CI check enforces it as a shrinking allowlist of shell files, `ci.yml` run steps and hook strings from stage 1 and strictly from stage 15 | 6: all three hook forms (plugin, project, Codex) exit with the blocking code when PreToolUse cannot start, so a missing Node or hook file blocks rather than fails open.
  - D11 Windows: proofline's own logic runs without Git Bash at the end (Git for Windows still provides git and runs the git hook launchers); each stage states what a Windows user needs; the README keeps "WSL or Git Bash" until Windows CI jobs pass | 6: no Windows support is claimed beyond what a test shows.
  - D12 one ecosystem reader in Node; `ecosystems.tsv` and the three `ecosystems.sh` copies go when their last reader goes | 2 and 6: risky-path and ecosystem data still come from `ecosystems.json` only, so SECRETS and SECURITY triggers do not change; the glob dialect is proven equal by a differential test before anything depends on it.
  - D13 each stage is its own pull request and patch version, ends with the real-session smoke, and has a rollback (the engine switch in `.agents/local/engine` until stage 10, which hook processes started by the runtime also read; the previous release installed with `proofline upgrade` from its checkout, a path verified in `bin/lib/install.sh` and covered by a downgrade test from stage 1; a revert always) | 4 and 6: evidence is taken on the code that ships, and a stage that misbehaves can be switched back without touching run state.
  - D14 no new test seam reaches a decision: stubs stay files inside the fixture, as `test-lib.sh` writes them today; no `PROOFLINE_TEST*` variable or clock seam is added; the fixture-file override that serves the shell `test-lib.sh` is temporary and goes in stage 15, and the Node harness injects stubs through the in-process `io` only; the hook's deny of `PROOFLINE_TEST*` assignments covers the model's own Bash commands in an installed project with an open run, not the repository's tests or CI; a test shows that no such value changes SECRETS, execution-policy or approval results outside the harness | 2 and 3: an agent cannot swap the secret scan or move the time an approval check compares.
  - P1 tool-call economy (ADR section 8.3): when a role makes many tool calls for one decision, one command or script does the work and only the short result the decision needs enters the context; raw output stays in a file in the run folder. Moved commands keep their bytes during the migration and get output budgets per command class from stage 2; a follow-up issue measures tool calls and context bytes per role after stage 2 (measuring adds no command) (from records.jsonl, history.tsv, HOOKS.log and runtime session logs where they exist, plus one new record file) and, only after stage 10 when the shell engine can no longer be selected, adds combined commands for the most call-heavy jobs and names them in the role texts, so the one-to-one 132-command map holds while both engines exist | Invariant not loosened: 4 and 6: combined commands are deterministic control-plane code that records its command line, input hashes and raw output for an independent re-run, a script a model writes is still not evidence, and a summary prints the finding count and says when it is truncated while the raw file stays.
  Requirement change, recorded now and carried out later: today CONTRIBUTING says Node 22.13 is needed for the skill tests only; after stage 1 Node 22.13 is a runtime requirement of proofline. The migration pull requests (stage 1 first), not this one, edit CONTRIBUTING and the README; this change does not alter what users must have today. Why: process cost is structural in shell (each hash, `stat` and field read is a process; earlier fixes in A188 and A203 were overtaken, the approval path went from 206 to 544 processes); the duplication of parsers and codecs is kept equal only by textual tests; `set -e` workarounds, awk dialects and GNU/BSD differences are recurring hazards; Windows has no path; and Node already ships 149 files and is used by `freeze`, `record`, `knowledge-done` and the hook. Rejected: keeping shell and fixing only the awk hot spots (done twice, does not last, leaves the duplication and Windows); another language (a compiled binary needs a build and per-platform downloads, another scripting runtime would be a second runtime beside the Node the skills already need); a daemon (lifecycle, caching across commands rejected in A203, a socket that can record approvals is a new attack surface for invariant 3); bundling npm dependencies (supply chain in the approval and gate path, an install step proofline does not have, and no need for a general YAML parser); a big-bang rewrite (no per-command proof or rollback); porting tests with or before the code (a test and its code changed together can agree on the same mistake). Open questions, each with a recommended default for the maintainer to confirm (ADR section 16): the pinned fail-closed guard in all hook forms (failing open is not offered, invariant 6); `agent.sh` and `dispatch.sh` as permanent launchers; the shell and Node invariant suites overlapping for at least one full release. Estimate: 74-111 agent-days over 15 stages, about 15-23 weeks (estimates; basis and a re-plan point after stage 2 in the stage plan). Related A173, A180, A188, A203.
- **A210. Node migration: direction change, a migration and not a redesign; no backward compatibility, no engine switch, no equivalence rig, no shell hook (patch 0.0.45; supersedes the parts of ADR 0001 sections 5.3, 5.4, 6, 9 and 10 and of A204 to A209 that keep two engines; related #165, #182, #186, #187).** USER DECISION of 2026-11-02: nobody uses the old proofline versions; there is no backward compatibility; the goal is that nothing in sh and awk is left and proofline is written in Node. What was unnecessary and is removed: the engine switch (`.agents/local/engine`, `PROOFLINE_ENGINE`, `PROOFLINE_ENGINE_SH`: a moved command always runs in Node; `PROOFLINE_ENGINE*` stays refused to a model in the tripwire, and the core hands an input to the shell only through the internal `PROOFLINE_BRIDGED` guard for the features that are still shell: known issues, the batch summary, design-sync drift, an open pull request, a persistent waiver key, `lessons.sh bound`, a delivered run); every fallback to the shell for a moved command (the mandatory-argument screen of the `agent.sh` preamble, the 56 `BridgeToShell` sites that stood for a shell error text, which now fail in Node with `proofline: input not supported (<reason>)` or `proofline: a mandatory argument is missing or empty`); upgrade and old-run support (the `sh -c` wiring strings of 0.0.40 to 0.0.42 are no longer recognised or replaced, `yield.mjs` keeps only the plugin-yields-to-project rule); the byte-identical equivalence rig (`tests/equivalence`, its 34 files, the trace recorder, the CI jobs `equivalence` and `equivalence-macos`); the shell hook `proofline-hook.sh` (2,771 lines) with the released copies in `tests/legacy-hook` (`tests/legacy-githooks` is NOT removed: ten unmoved shell suites install the old shell git hooks from it); the tests that compared Node with the shell (`parity`, `c1`, `verify`, `library`, the shell-hook pairs of `events`, `prompt`, `pretool-bash`, `guards-file`, `kill-guard`, `stash-net`, `command-scan`); the shell-engine benchmark tooling (`tests/bench/agent-procs.mjs` and its baselines, the process and output budget tests that needed them; the Node hook keeps its process budget per event); `next-user.sh`, `kill-guard-test.sh` and the shell forms of `insights` and `queue`. What stays: the Core invariants (Node copy in `tests/invariants-node`; the shell copy stays until the last suite is gone), the real-session smoke, and absolute Node tests of every moved area (the recorded goldens `tests/fixtures/port-t3`, `tests/core/golden`, `tests/enforcement/recorded`, the `legacy-*` ports of the shell scenarios). File formats and behaviours stay unless a change is a clear benefit; the deliberate behaviour changes are: (1) no engine switch; (2) the error text of an input the shell answered with its own error (a backslash, a newline or a glob character in a name, an over-long number, an unreadable `PLAN.md`) is the Node core's, exit 1, and a recorded shell error text is no longer a compared behaviour; (3) `plan-section` reads its section name as a basic regular expression (`.`, `*`, a closed `[...]`; every other character is literal), as `grep` did; (4) `tm-scaled` clamps a negative number like zero; (5) the core answers an unknown command and the bare call with the usage text (exit 2) and creates the lock folder as the shell did; (6) an installed project without the core fails closed with exit 127, `proofline insights`, `queue` and the `Next step:` line need the core (`cli next-line` replaces `next-user.sh`); (7) the installer no longer copies or merges the shell hook and the 0.0.40 to 0.0.42 strings; `doctor` probes and checks the Node hook only and the `engine:` line says whether the core is installed; (8) #187: the answers of the user-only kind (an assumption acceptance, the split override, a question marked `USER_ONLY:`) are recorded as the user's by the prompt hook alone, in process, from the message it is handling and only when the message is one of the answer forms the question lists (the single open question of its kind; otherwise nothing is recorded and the lead asks again); `answer --captured` and `--amend` without that hand-over are refused (a planted `prompts/history` file or capture is never the user's answer); a typed answer is the lead's; `next` no longer records an approval from a capture, it reports a missed approval and the lead asks the user again; a message of the second the question was asked in is not its answer; an INTENT `scope` decision is asked as a question marked `USER_ONLY: scope D-<n>` with its accepted `options:`, and the freeze takes the user's hook-recorded answer to it as the provenance of the INTENT round (the A171 split question carries `SPLIT:` and its options the same way); the batch pre-flight answers (`batch-answer`, shell, reading `prompts/history`) and the history fallback of the INTENT provenance check stay as on main; `next` and the skill texts no longer tell the lead to run `answer --captured` (the user answers in their next message); (9) the bash guard names the seams `PROOFLINE_BRIDGED`, `PROOFLINE_TEST*` and the retired `PROOFLINE_ENGINE*` in any form, with or without an open run, and treats `tar -C`, `unzip -d`, `curl -o` and `wget -O/-P` targets as write targets; (10) CI fast mode (A205, A209) has no date: it ends when the last legacy shell test is gone. #186 (the two cases the shell answers) is closed as an accepted limit and then done in this release (unknown command and bare usage in Node); #182 (the real-session smoke fixture fix) and #187 are in. Why: the plan kept two engines alive and paid for it (a rig of 2,100 lines, 25 macOS legs, a hook in two languages, shell texts copied byte for byte); the work is a migration of the same behaviour to one language, not a redesign. Rejected: keeping the rig until stage 10 (it cannot find a defect the golden recordings do not, and it pins the shell code that has to go); a compatibility layer for old installs (nobody has one). Re-plan (epic #165, estimates in agent-days): stage 4 lifecycle and gates (#169) 8-12, stage 5 delivery (#171) 4-6, stage 6 dispatch and batch (#172) 5-7, stage 7 discovery, helpers, CLI and skill scripts (#173) 6-9, stage 8 harness, fixtures and CI, end of fast mode (#176) 6-9, stage 9 the no-shell check (#180) 1-2. Not tested: a live Claude Code session with the new wiring (the real-session smoke runs it before the release).

- **A211. Session-bound user answers verified live on Claude Code and Codex; a real-session smoke row for the hook-recorded path (patch; refs #196; follows A210 item 8, #187).** The prompt hook records a user-only answer only when its session equals `asked_session`, which `agent.sh ask` takes from `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, else `CODEX_SESSION_ID`, else `CODEX_THREAD_ID` of the lead's Bash environment. Checked LIVE: (1) Claude Code (real session, haiku, `SMOKE_ONLY=a196`): `asked_session` equals the `session_id` of the stream-json transcript and of the hook payload, and the next prompt of the same session is recorded as `answered_by: user` with its `source_message`; (2) Codex (codex-cli 0.166.0, `codex exec`): a command run by the model has `CODEX_SESSION_ID` and `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, both equal to the `session id` Codex prints for the session, and the hook payload of `UserPromptSubmit` carries `session_id` with that same value (payload fields: `session_id`, `turn_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `model`, `permission_mode`, `prompt`), so the variable names read by `ask` are the real ones and the binding needs no change; the hook process itself has no `CODEX_*` session variable, which is why the id is read from the payload there. A message of another session records nothing (the same smoke row asks a question under another session id and answers it from the real session: no `answered_by: user`). Known limit, safe direction: a Codex lead started from inside a Claude Code session inherits `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` of its parent, which `ask` reads first, so `asked_session` is then the parent's id, no Codex prompt matches, nothing is recorded and the task stays parked. Not run: the Codex hook-recorded answer end to end through proofline's own wiring (the smoke row is Claude Code only; the Codex hook payload and the variables were probed with a throwaway hook). Rejected: taking the session from the hook payload only (the lead's `ask` runs in a command, not a hook, and has no payload). Not-tested: Codex answer through the installed `.codex/hooks.json`.

  Known limit (kararını bekliyor): a security review found that the lead model can start a nested headless runtime in its own session (`python3 -c ... subprocess.run(['claude','-p',text,'--resume',$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID])`, perl `system`, `find -exec`, a node script), which the Bash guard allows (`command-scan.mjs` matches the command word only); the resulting `UserPromptSubmit` carries the asking session id, so the model can forge a user-only answer. Pre-existing, outside #196 scope, tracked in a comment on #169. The guard code is not changed here. The Codex smoke row is left out of this entry (env and payload ids verified live; the end-to-end Codex row was not run).

- **A212. Node migration, stage 4, package 4A: 14 run-lifecycle commands run in Node (patch; #169; follows A210).** Moved: `baseline`, `discard-stray`, `branch`, `tier`, `classify`, `verify-assumptions`, `delivery-check`, `db-check`, `ask`, `status-block`, `tree-inspect`, `tree-accept`, `task-source-status`, `task-source-relocate` (`core/commands/runcmds.mjs`, `core/questions.mjs`, `core/statusblock.mjs`, `core/knownissues.mjs`, `core/dbguard.mjs`, `core/slug.mjs`). File formats, run folder, output texts and exit codes stay; the commands are proved by absolute Node tests (`tests/core/run4a-classify.test.mjs`, `tests/core/run4a-records.test.mjs`, 36 tests) and by the existing ports that now reach the Node code (`legacy-recovery`, `legacy-questions`, `tests/tasks/status-block-test.sh` with the real adapters). Deleted from `agent.sh` (9222 to 8992 lines): the 14 arms, the 14 names in the preamble list of commands that still run as shell code, and the functions `baseline`, `remove_pending_baseline`, `discard_stray` (and its protected-name list), `branch_setup`, `derive_task_slug`, `class_rank`, `classify`, `tree_inspect`, `tree_accept`, `task_source_status`, `task_source_relocate`. Deleted from the shell suites: `gates-test.sh` `sc_tier`, `sc_tier_paths`, `sc_ask`, `sc_class_floor`, `lifecycle-test.sh` `scenario_tree_recovery`, `scenario_task_source_status`, `scenario_task_contract_relocate` and the discard-stray half of `scenario_hardening` (every row is in `tests/legacy-port-map.tsv`; the `ls -di` stub case is dropped, the Node command reads the inode with `stat`). SHELL FUNCTIONS THAT STAY, and why: `tier_record`, `tier_effective`/`tier_compute`, `verify_assumptions` and the `assumption_*` family, `ask_question`, `status_block_update` with `status_block_body`/`status_block_run` and the `sb_*` helpers, `delivery_check` and `db_guard_check` are called IN PROCESS by commands that are not moved yet (`freeze`, `refreeze`, `handoff`, `start`, `terminate`, `cleanup`, `deliver-plan`, `deliver-step`, `deliver-merged`). They cannot call the Node command instead: a command holds the run and shared locks for its whole transaction, and a nested `sh agent.sh <command>` that takes the locks waits for its parent until the lock timeout (checked: `tier` of a lead and `ask` lock). They go with their last user in packages 4B and 4C. Only two Node/shell pairs are guarded against drift, by a differential test in `run4a-records.test.mjs`: `sb_scrub` against the Node `scrub`, and the slug table of `core/slug.mjs` against `task-integrations/slug.sh` (the adapters run it until stage 7). The other pairs are NOT guarded: `tier_record`, `ask_question`, the question texts of `verify_assumptions`, `status_block_body`, `delivery_check`, `db_guard_check` and the known-issue functions (`ki`, `ki_untouched`, `finding_known_issue`, `ki_gate_facts`); each is tested on its side only, and a change to one must be made in both until its shell copy is deleted. Deliberate changes: (1) `baseline` stops on a symlink in the working tree before anything is written (`cannot baseline symlink: <path>`, exit 1); the shell printed the same message from inside a command substitution, went on and recorded an empty hash for it, so the run then failed `validate`; (2) `answer` and `ask` update the status block in process (the lead's `answer` no longer starts `sh agent.sh status-block`), and the time bound covers the adapter child (the block itself is built in process); a timeout reads `timed out after <n>s` in the note and the log; (3) `delivery-check` reads the design-sync drift natively (the one `node` child of the shell function is the one `node` child here, its JSON is parsed in process); (4) `verify-assumptions <ID>` is read-only and takes no lock, as before; the freeze's asking mode is NOT reachable from the command line (an `ask` word is ignored); package 4B calls `verifyAssumptions(ctx, id, true)` in process under freeze's locks; (5) the list of known issues is read through `known-issues.sh` as a child (`canon`, `lookup`) and the decision whether the task touches the place is Node (`core/knownissues.mjs`), so the status block no longer needs the shell for a non-empty list; (6) a title with a line break gets a one-line slug in Node (the shell printed two lines); (7) `task-source-relocate` refuses a new path with a control character, a quote or a backslash, and `setRunValue` refuses any value with a control character or a quote (security review: a path with a line break wrote extra lines into RUN.yaml, overrode sealed sections, and the ledger then sealed the modified file); (8) `answer` builds the status block in process but releases the command locks before the adapter child runs (a slow tracker holds no lock), as the Node code did before this package; (9) `baseline` in a repository without a commit stops with `baseline needs a commit` and writes nothing (the shell stopped on `set -e` of `rev-parse HEAD`, with git's text). Test fixtures (`test-lib.sh`): the agent.sh of a fixture is the real file with a four-line prologue that sends the 14 commands to the Node core (installed in `.agents/core4a`, outside `.agents/scripts`); everything else runs the shell code as before. It goes with the last shell suite. Rejected: the core beside agent.sh in every fixture (it hands every moved command of stages 1 to 3 to Node too: 21 of the first 52 units of the full self-test failed, because the shell scenarios of `approve` and `answer` write captures and expect answers by the rules of the shell engine, A210 item 8); nested calls of moved commands from shell code (lock wait, above); porting `slug.sh` out of the adapters here (stage 7). Performance (external processes counted by shims, plus the launcher `sh`; wall time of the median of 5 runs, macOS, before = shell on 0.0.46, after = this change): `classify` 54 / 1.19 s to 2 / 0.11 s; `tier` 54 / 1.30 s to 3 / 0.14 s; `baseline` 28 / 0.65 s to 4 / 0.13 s; `delivery-check` 496 / 12.3 s to 8 / 0.26 s; `db-check` 14 / 0.46 s to 1 / 0.09 s; `status-block` 56 / 1.08 s to 2 / 0.12 s; `verify-assumptions` 11 / 0.23 s to 1 / 0.08 s; `tree-inspect` 14 / 0.20 s to 2 / 0.10 s. The stage target of `delivery-check` (at most 6) is not met: the content-patch check at CODE_DONE needs the tier, that is `git diff --name-only`, `--numstat`, `-U0` and `cat-file --batch`, plus `branch`, `rev-parse` and `status`: 7 git processes and the node process; kararını bekliyor (accept 8, or merge the diffs in a later package). Not-tested: the `known_issues` key of the status block against a real approved record (the logic is `core/knownissues.mjs`; the list needs a user approval chain); a Windows run of `db-check` (the walk uses `lstat` and `fnmatch` rules written for POSIX paths); `status-block` against a live tracker (fake `gh` and `curl` in `tests/tasks/status-block-test.sh` only). Constraint: `delivery-check` runs `secret-scan.sh` as a child (stage 5) and the task adapter script as a child (stage 7). Smoke (macOS, model haiku): hermetic setup, doctor, `/proofline run` and `/proofline deliver` PASS on this change; the batch step FAILs both on this change and on 0.0.46, with DIFFERENT causes (T-3 parks on a QA plan error on 0.0.46 and on an unrecorded worker window of the Codex implementer on this branch); that it is the same model-dependent defect is unproven; the first smoke of this branch found a defect the shell scenarios could not see (a task worktree reports an absolute git dir, `wtLinked` joined it to the root) and `run4a-classify.test.mjs` now covers `branch` from a detached task worktree. The default smoke of round 1 found a second defect of this package that no test had: `delivery-check` ran the main tree's `secret-scan.sh` over the paths of a run worktree without `--root`, so the scanner looked in the main tree (`no such path`) and parked the task; `runSecretScan` now passes `--root` and `run4a-records.test.mjs` covers it with a real linked worktree.

- **A213. Node migration, stage 4, package 4B: `start`, `freeze`, `refreeze`, `handoff`, `terminate`, `amend`, `reopen` and `cleanup` run in Node (patch; #169; follows A210 and A212).** Moved: the eight commands with everything only they used: the task-source contract of the freeze (`requireTaskCopyMatchesSource`, `requireTaskBoundaries`: Forbidden, Allowed scope and pattern references, A202), the plan-contract coverage check (`validate-plan.mjs` stays a node child), the pipeline artifact contract with the split question (A171), the scope-existence rule, the mutation budget, the approvals a freeze consumes (plan, scope, budget, the INTENT provenance), the hashes and the refreeze lifecycle; the handoff ladder (classification check, defect report, worker evidence, fix bound, scratch worktrees, language of the run folder, effective tier record); the end of a run (`terminate`, the run record of the metrics, `archive_run` with `tar`, `cleanup` and the removal of the run's worktree); `amend` and `reopen` (the budget question, the `raise-budget` it ends with). Code: `core/freeze.mjs`, `core/handoff.mjs`, `core/runend.mjs`, `core/reopen.mjs`, `core/runstart.mjs`, `core/lifeutil.mjs`, `core/commands/lifecmds.mjs`. File formats, run folder, output texts and exit codes are those of 0.0.47. Proved by absolute Node tests written with the area for `start`, the freeze checks (boundaries, scope existence, plan approval, mutation budget, language, UI, TRIVIAL), the handoff ladder, `terminate`, `cleanup`, `amend`, `reopen`, the lock hand-over and the waiver key (`tests/core/run4b-lifecycle.test.mjs`, `tests/core/run4b-freeze.test.mjs`, `tests/core/legacy-waivers.test.mjs` through the Node gate status; legacy-port-map rows added). NOT covered by a Node test, kept as black-box shell scenarios of `lifecycle-test`, `gates-test`, `deliver-test` and `cifix-test` (which run the Node commands through the fixture prologue) until the last shell suite is gone: the `single_step` approval, `verify_fix_bound`, `reopen_for_fix`, the K-6 refreeze reset to PLANNED, INTENT provenance, scratch worktrees, the split flow, a listed known issue and an accepted batch finding in `finding_waived`, and the `verify-completion-report` and `raise-budget` children. The shell suites (`lifecycle-test` 65 units, `gates-test` 94, `controls-test`, `identity-test`, `cifix-test`, `deliver-test` 30, `known-issues-test`: all PASS on the last commit). Deleted from `agent.sh` (+9 -1,027 lines; 8,992 to 7,976): the eight arms and their names in the preamble list, and 53 functions that no remaining shell command reaches (a reachability walk from the top-level code and the arms that are left, compared with the walk of 0.0.47 so that only what this change made dead goes): `start_run`, `freeze` with its helpers (`pipeline_check`, `split_check`/`split_state`/`split_token`, `freeze_approvals`, `verify_intent_provenance`, `require_task_copy_matches_source`, `require_task_boundaries`, `task_scope_bad`, `replace_hashes`, `set_task_source_revision`, ...), `record_handoff` with its helpers (`implement_approvals`, `verify_classification`, `verify_debug_result`, `verify_fix_bound`, `reopen_for_fix`, `verify_run_language`, `build_record_auto`), `terminate_run`, `cleanup_run`, `cleanup_worktree`, `amend_run`, `reopen_run`, `reopen_question`, `metrics_run`, and from the list of A212 `tier_record`, `verify_assumptions`, `db_guard_check` (with `db_snapshot`, `db_baseline_file`). SHELL FUNCTIONS THAT STAY, and why (A212 named them): `tier_effective`/`tier_compute`, `assumption_*`, `ask_question`, `status_block_*`/`sb_*`, `delivery_check`, `db_config`, `ki_*` are still reached by arms that are left: `record`, `gate`, `decide`, `deliver-plan`, `deliver-step`, `deliver-merged` (4C and stage 6), and by the arms of Node commands whose Node code still hands one input to the shell through `BridgeToShell` (`next`, `pipeline`, `digest`, `summary`, `report-facts` for a batch summary, a design-sync drift, an open pull request, a delivered run). They go with those. `archive_run` stays because `worktree-remove` (shell) calls it; its Node copy in `runend.mjs` writes the same file and a test reads the archive back, no drift test. The fixture prologue of `test-lib.sh` (`.agents/core4a`) stays: every shell suite builds its runs with `classify`, `baseline`, `freeze` and `handoff`, which are Node commands now. DELIBERATE CHANGES. (1) A command that still runs as shell code and is started by a Node command, or the reverse, runs as a child that takes over the locks of its PARENT: a lock whose pid file names the parent's pid is the parent's own transaction, it is neither waited for nor released by the child (`LockSet.acquire`/`takeOld` in Node, `acquire_lock`/`take_old_lock` in `agent.sh`). A lock held by anyone else is still waited for (test). A nested `sh agent.sh <command>` could not be used before: it waited for its parent until the lock timeout (A212). Used by: `handoff DONE` and `cleanup` (`verify-completion-report`), `reopen` (`raise-budget`), `cleanup` of a leftover worktree (`worktree-remove`), and, the other way, by `deliver-step cleanup`, `deliver-merged` (`cleanup`) and the CI-fix round (`amend`). The take-over proves nothing but "do not wait for this lock": a process that writes a lock's pid file with its own pid and starts a child gains no trust from it, only the wait it skips. (2) There is no flag, lock or argument that says "merged" (an earlier draft had `cleanup --delivered`, accepted from a lock-holding parent; review showed a parent can forge the lock's pid file, so it was dropped). `cleanup` removes the worktree of a delivered run only when the merge is on record: a `batch/merged.tsv` row of this run, or the `MERGED` file that `deliver-step cleanup` and `deliver-merged` write in the run's deliver folder right after their own proof (a pull request seen merged, git ancestry or content) and before they start `cleanup`. Weaker than 0.0.47 for a standalone delivery: the shell's claim was an in-process variable (`cleanup_merged_claim`) that no file could set; a batch delivery has `merged.tsv` as a second record, but a standalone delivery now relies on the one file `MERGED`. It is hook-guarded, not unforgeable: the runtime hook and bash guard deny a typed write to it, but a nested interpreter (`python3 -c "open(...)"`) is not seen, the same limit as A211. What it still buys: it holds the epoch of the proof and counts only when that is not older than the nonce of this delivery's summary (the check `merged.tsv` rows get), and `deliver-plan` deletes it with `PR` when it starts a new delivery, so a leftover does not prove the next one. The nonce comparison and the `deliver-plan` reset have no test of their own (`deliver-test` `scenario_wt_cleanup_pr`, `scenario_wt_cleanup_kept` cover the accepted record and `scenario_wt_cleanup_forged` the refused one). What it cannot do: tell a forged file from the real one. Consequence of a forgery: the worktree of a delivered, DONE run whose other checks pass (HEAD descends from base, task-owned changes committed, nothing untracked) is removed after its records were archived; nothing unmerged is lost from the repository. kararını bekliyor: accept this, or have `cleanup` check git itself (base branch on origin contains the delivered head), which needs the origin access `deliver-merged` has and `cleanup` does not. (3) `start` refuses a task path or an adapter name with a control character, a quote or a backslash before it writes RUN.yaml (the path is the adapter's stdout; a line break would have written extra lines). (4) `finding_waived` is decided in Node: a listed known issue, an accepted batch finding and a persistent waiver key (`findingKey`, `findingWaiverKey`: the same key `waive` computes in the shell, byte for byte on macOS and GNU `sed`, which both keep a missing final newline missing). Three `BridgeToShell` sites of `gates.mjs` are gone; a moved command has no shell code to bridge to. (5) Fixed: the Node walk of the run folder (`knownControlArtifact`) took `design/adr/0001-x.md` for a stray file; the shell `case` pattern `design/*.md` spans folders and the Node regular expression did not (found by `scenario_hardening`; `run4b-freeze.test.mjs` covers it). (6) The A169 redirect to a run worktree skips `start`, as the shell did. (7) `cleanup` runs its git calls from the main tree after the worktree is gone (a spawn with a deleted working directory fails); the shell used `git -C`. Found by `deliver-test`: the status-block strip of a task file must drop trailing newlines like a command substitution. Performance (external processes counted by PATH shims plus the launcher `sh`; wall time of the median of 5 runs, macOS, before = 0.0.47, after = this change): `freeze` 202 / 2.33 s to 5 / 0.15 s; `handoff IMPLEMENTING` 70 / 1.22 s to 5 / 0.13 s; `IMPLEMENTED` 210 / 3.06 s to 7 / 0.17 s; `CODE_DONE` 343 / 5.58 s to 15 / 0.26 s; `DONE` 490 / 8.39 s to 20 / 0.31 s; `terminate` 151 / 1.26 s to 5 / 0.13 s; `cleanup` 40 / 0.64 s to 5 / 0.13 s; `amend` 591 / 10.2 s to 12 / 0.23 s. The stage targets (freeze at most 8, handoff at most 15) are met except `handoff DONE` at 20: the `verify-completion-report` child is shell code until package 4C (kararını bekliyor: accept 20 until 4C). Known limit, safe direction: in a run worktree whose `.agents/scripts` differs from the project's (a task changed the control plane) the shell children (`verify-completion-report`, `raise-budget`) are refused by `proc.mjs` (a worktree's scripts are tracked content) and the command stops with that message; package 4C moves them and removes the limit. Rejected: porting `archive_run` out of `worktree-remove` here (it is stage 6); a `--merged` environment variable and a `--delivered` flag for the cleanup claim (D14: no environment seam; a flag is forgeable); deleting the black-box shell scenarios of `lifecycle-test.sh` now (they are the regression net of the Node commands and of 4C; the prologue goes with the last shell suite, A212). Not-tested: a live smoke of `start --task-file` with a real tracker adapter (markdown only); `worktree-remove` as the child of `cleanup` outside the fixture (the leftover-worktree branch is covered by `scenario_wt_cleanup_kept`). Smoke (macOS, model haiku): default run on the last commit: setup, doctor, `/proofline run` (368 s, 4B `start`, `classify`, `freeze`, `handoff`, `terminate`-free path to CODE_DONE), `/proofline deliver`, the Codex sandbox probe and `/proofline batch T-2 T-3` (both reach origin main, merges recorded, runs cleaned up and archived) PASS; the two status-block rows of the batch and the Codex row FAIL in that one run (the lead used the Claude implementer, no Codex dispatch seen; the main working tree was not fast-forwarded, so the final block had no task file to land in: model-dependent, the batch row itself passed). `SMOKE_ONLY=a202` three times: the 4A tree (baseline) all PASS; this change first run the batch row FAIL (T-3 parked on a genuine question, the frozen QA-6 expects two spaces where the task text gives three) with the T-2 block PASS, second run all PASS. The batch step is flaky on main as well (A212 recorded the same T-3 park on 0.0.46); no failure points at a 4B code path (no lock, internal-error or unsupported-input message in the transcripts).

- **A215. Node migration, stage 6 (first part): delivery runs in Node (patch; #171; follows A210, A213, A214).** Moved (8 commands): `deliver-plan`, `deliver-step` (commit, push, pr, merge, cleanup and the CI-fix steps ci-fix, ci-commit, ci-push, ci-merge), `deliver-merged`, `pr-state`, `task-source-done`, `platform`, `platform-warn`, `batch-ci`; and with them the open-pull-request lines of `next` (`ci_progress`) and the delivered-run branch of `questions`, which no longer hand the command to the shell (two `BridgeToShell` sites gone). Code: `core/platform.mjs` (the hosting platform of the origin remote, `git.platform` and `git.platform_host`, the failed-log readers of GitHub, GitLab and Azure DevOps, the platform tool lookup), `core/deliver.mjs` (summary, steps, CI-fix rounds, manual-merge proof from git, `batch-ci`), `core/commands/delivercmds.mjs`; `cli platform-info` serves `bin/lib/merge.sh` (the name may not equal an `agent.sh` command, so not `cli platform`). Deleted (git numstat): `scripts/platform.sh` -230, `deliver-test.sh` -706, `cifix-test.sh` -274, `agent.sh` +5 -808 (the 8 arms, the `ci-check` and `ci-task-command` arms, 43 functions: `deliver_plan`, `deliver_step`, `deliver_merged`, the whole `ci_fix_*` chain, `deliver_pr_view`, `deliver_ci_read`, `deliver_cli_path`, `deliver_create_cmd`, `task_source_done`, `ci_check`, `ci_absent`, `ci_task_command`, `platform_export_env`, `origin_url`, `origin_push_cmd`, the `sb_*` final-block functions, `delivery_check`, `ask_question`, `scan_knowledge_secrets`, `require_knowledge_done`, `require_no_knowledge_drift`, and the `deliver_pv` read before the locks), `batch.sh` -35 (`ci_once`, `ci_record`, `ci_cmd`), `platform-test.sh` -33 net, `status-block-test.sh` -25 (the block-only test, now `run6-sbblock.test.mjs`) (the failed-log reader block moved to `run6-platform.test.mjs`; the detection and config scenarios stay as black boxes on `cli platform-info`). SHELL FUNCTIONS THAT STAY, and why: `ci_chain_ok`, `delivered_mode`, `ci_fix_recs`, `ci_progress`, `deliver_dir`, `deliver_watch_cmd`, `deliver_platform` (now `agent.sh platform`), `tier_effective`/`tier_compute`, `assumption_*`, `status_block_*`/`sb_*` (the rest), `db_config`, `ki_*`, `archive_run` are still reached by the dead shell arms of the commands of stages 1 to 3 and by `worktree-remove` (stage 7); a reachability walk from the top-level code and the arms that are left finds no other unreachable function. DELIBERATE CHANGES. (1) THE MERGE IS PROVED IN PROCESS (resolves the A213 kararini bekliyor): there is no `MERGED` file any more. `deliver-step cleanup` (the pull request read MERGED through the platform tool) and `deliver-merged` (the delivered commit is on origin's base or its content is there, from git) call the cleanup of the run in the SAME process with the proof as a parameter (`cleanupRun(ctx, id, true)`); the standalone `cleanup` command removes the worktree of a delivered run only on a `batch/merged.tsv` row of this run that is not older than the nonce of the delivery summary. No file, flag, lock, environment value or argument can say "merged", so the standalone case is as strong as the in-process variable of 0.0.47 and stronger than the hook-guarded file of 0.0.48; `scenario_wt_cleanup_forged` is now a Node test that writes the old `MERGED` file, forges the lock and passes `--delivered` and `CLEANUP_MERGED`: nothing is removed. A failure after the approval was consumed (the run folder cannot be removed, a process dies) is repeatable: `worktree-add` always creates `batch/`, so the `merged.tsv` row is written BEFORE the cleanup in every worktree flow, and a standalone `agent.sh cleanup` then removes the run and its worktree (the row is not older than the nonce of the summary; test `run6-merged.test.mjs`, the retry case). Only a delivery in the main working tree without a `batch/` folder has no row: there `agent.sh cleanup` removes the run's records and keeps nothing to remove (no worktree exists); `deliver-merged` helps only for deliveries the user merges (it needs MERGE_HEAD or a summary with `merge_by: user`). (2) The platform tools get argument arrays and their JSON is parsed in process: `gh pr view --json ...`, `gh run list --json ...`, `glab mr view -F json`, `az repos pr show -o json` are read without `jq` and without `--jq`; a missing `jq` no longer makes a pull request unreadable. A fake tool therefore answers JSON. (3) NO ENVIRONMENT SEAM (D14): the delivery code does not read `PROOFLINE_SELFTEST`; a platform tool that resolves into the project, the working directory or a temporary folder is refused, as before, and the comparison is by the identity of the folder (device and inode of every ancestor of the tool, besides the real paths), never by the spelling of the path, so that an upper-case or mixed-case spelling of the folder on a case-insensitive file system (macOS default) is refused too (security review of 6A; `run6-platform.test.mjs`), in every test: the Node tests and `batch-test.sh` keep their fake `gh` under `tests/core/.fake-tools/` (ignored by the repository). `bin/lib/merge.sh` still reads that variable until it moves (stage 9). (4) A platform tool call is bounded to 180 s (there was no bound). (5) `deliver-merged` lists the delivered paths by line (a path with a blank was split in two by the shell). (6) `git.platform`/`git.platform_host`, `PROOFLINE_PLATFORM`, whole-host equality, the look-alike rule and the local-origin rule are those of A180/A186 (tests: `run6-platform.test.mjs`). (7) The fixture prologue of `test-lib.sh` sends the stage 6 commands, `ci-check` and `ci-task-command` to the Node core. Not done and not tested: the Windows `.cmd` shims of the platform tools (a `.cmd` is found on PATH but nothing wraps it), `az` and `glab` against a real service (fakes only, as before). Rejected: keeping the `MERGED` file with a nonce check (still a forgeable file); a Node-only seam for the tool location (D14); `jq` as a required tool. kararini bekliyor: none open (the A213 question is answered: no file claim exists any more; the alternative, a file that proves a merge, is the forgeable design A213 recorded). NEEDS FOR LATER STAGES (not done here, #171 scope): the task adapters `task-integrations/{markdown,github,jira,linear,_lib,slug}.sh` (762 lines; the status block, `start`, `publish-completion-report` and the final block of a delivery still run `markdown.sh statusblock` as a child), `bin/lib/merge.sh` as a core subcommand (it reads the platform through `cli platform-info` but still checks the pull request in shell; its tests are `merge-guard-test.sh` and the merge half of `platform-test.sh`), `cifix-test`'s batch scenario (needs `batch-plan`/`batch-cover`, stage 7), `batch-awake`/`batch-park` (stage 7). Performance (external processes counted by PATH shims including the launcher `sh` and `node`; wall time of the median of 5 runs, macOS, fake `gh` as a tool, a finished run; before = 4C head (0.0.48 shell delivery), after = this change; `tests/core` fixture, hooks installed): `platform` 14 / 0.07 s to 3 / 0.08 s; `deliver-plan` 586 / 11.40 s to 23 / 0.26 s; `deliver-step commit` 68 / 0.53 s to 9 / 0.13 s; `task-source-done` 20 / 0.33 s to 4 / 0.09 s; `deliver-step push` 91 / 0.63 s to 19 / 0.19 s; `deliver-step pr` 157 / 1.03 s to 19 / 0.19 s; `pr-state` 40 / 0.17 s to 4 / 0.09 s; `deliver-step merge` 191 / 1.16 s to 20 / 0.21 s; `deliver-step cleanup` 253 / 1.54 s to 49 / 0.44 s; `batch-ci` 21 / 0.17 s to 3 / 0.08 s. The stage target for `platform` (at most 2 processes besides the launcher) is met: launcher, node, and no git call for the project root. `deliver-plan` and `deliver-step` are far below before; `batch-ci` asks the platform once, as before; it now also refuses a `gh` that resolves into the project, the working directory or a temporary folder (the old `batch.sh ci` used a bare `command -v gh`). Verified: Core invariants (Node copy) and all Node tests (tests/core, tests/ci, tests/enforcement, tests/hook, tests/invariants-node), the type check, `shellcheck -S warning` on every edited shell file, the no-shell-logic ratchet, and the shell suites `batch-test`, `lifecycle-test`, `controls-test`, `identity-test`, `known-issues-test`, `task-adversarial-test`, `tasks-test`, `status-block-test`, `merge-guard-test`, `platform-test` and `cli-test`. Smoke (macOS, model haiku): default run: setup, doctor, `/proofline run`, `/proofline deliver`, the Codex sandbox probe, `/proofline batch T-2 T-3` (both reach origin main), both branch-name rows, the Codex row and `skill tool not used` PASS; the two status-block rows of the batch FAIL (`no task file of T-2/T-3 holds a status block`, the same two rows A213 and A214 recorded as failing intermittently on main; no lock, internal-error or unsupported-input message in the transcripts). `SMOKE_ONLY=a202`: all PASS. SECURITY ROUND 2 (environment of the platform tool): `gh`, `glab` and `az` (and the `git push` and the `git fetch` that proves a merge) no longer start with the caller's whole environment. `cleanToolEnv` (core/platform.mjs) is an allowlist: PATH, LANG, LC_*, TERM, TZ, TMPDIR, colour and CI switches, and only credential variables that cannot redirect traffic (GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT); HOME comes from the account database, not from the caller; the private-host variable of A186 is still set from the platform info; SSH_AUTH_SOCK is kept for the push only. DROPPED: GH_CONFIG_DIR, XDG_*, GH_HOST/GH_REPO/GH_*_URL from the caller, GLAB_*, AZURE_CONFIG_DIR, GIT_CONFIG_*, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_ASKPASS, every proxy variable (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, lower-case too), SSL_CERT_*, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, NODE_OPTIONS. Before, a model could point the real tool at a server of its own (a gh config with `http_unix_socket`) and fake MERGED or green CI (the shell did the same). Proved by a permanent test in `tests/core/run6-platform.test.mjs`. DECISION FOR THE OWNER (kararını bekliyor): a project behind a corporate proxy or a private CA no longer gets those variables through; if that is needed they belong in the user's own gh or git config under the account's home, or in an explicit allowlist setting. SECURITY ROUND 3: (S1) `deliver-merged` proved a merge from whatever `git remote get-url origin` said now, so a model could build a bare repository of its own, `git remote set-url origin <it>` (the hook allows it) and get an unmerged delivery recorded. Now the summary pins two lines, `origin_url` and `origin_effective` (what `git ls-remote --get-url origin` says: `url.<x>.insteadOf` applied), and `deliver-merged` refuses (`origin changed since the summary was approved ... plan the delivery again`, the run kept, nothing recorded) unless both are unchanged. A legitimate change of the remote therefore needs a new plan, as the push step already did. (S2) the `git` of the push, of the merge-proof fetch and of every call of `deliver-merged` is found once under the location rule of the platform tools (`resolveGit`: refused inside the project, the working directory or a temporary folder, by folder identity) and run by its absolute path with the allowlisted environment; the PATH given to `gh`, `glab`, `az` and `git` has every relative entry and every entry inside those folders removed (`gh` runs `git` itself). Proved by two permanent tests in `tests/core/run6-merged.test.mjs` (re-pointed origin and `insteadOf`; a fake git on the PATH). NOT FIXED HERE (kararını bekliyor, hook level): the runtime hook allows `declare -x PATH=...; sh agent.sh deliver-merged` forms and the writing of fake tools into the project; `gh` without `-R` picks the repository from the git remotes, so a model-added extra remote is unproven by this change; the other `git()` reads of the control plane (status, rev-parse, the origin url read itself) still use the PATH's git. SECURITY ROUND 4: (S1) the pins of round 3 sat in a SUMMARY.md the model could write again: `git remote set-url origin <fake>`, `deliver-plan` again (a new summary with the fake pins, MERGE_HEAD kept), `deliver-merged` recorded a merge. Now `deliver-merged` requires that the hash of SUMMARY.md is the one an approval the user ANSWERED (a `commit`, `push` or `pr` approval, not a request) is bound to; a re-planned summary has a fresh nonce and only requests, so it proves nothing until the user approves it. `deliver-plan` itself is not changed (the simplest safe rule: the proof refuses, the plan stays possible). A delivery the user pushed by hand still works, as long as the summary was approved. (S2) repository configuration applied to the merge-proof fetch (`http.proxy`, `http.sslVerify`, `http.sslCAInfo`, `core.sshCommand`, `url.<x>.insteadOf`, a hook path, ...) while the pins stayed equal. Blacklisting keys is not the fix: the fetch is now hermetic (`hermeticFetch`, core/deliver.mjs): a throwaway bare repository in a fresh temporary folder, no configuration of the project, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` off, the PINNED url read directly (not the project's remote), the project's object store as an alternate (so the delivered commit is known there; its own tracking ref seeds the negotiation), and the whole proof (ancestry, or identical paths for a squash or rebase) computed in that repository. The proven tip is then imported into the project's tracking ref with hooks off and must equal the proven commit, else nothing is recorded. The temporary repository is removed. Proved by tests in `tests/core/run6-merged.test.mjs` (re-plan; a reference-transaction hook through `core.hooksPath`; `hermeticFetch` ignoring `core.sshCommand` and writing no project ref). NOT FIXED HERE (kararını bekliyor, hook level): the hook allows `git config http.*`, `core.sshCommand` and similar keys and `git remote set-url`; they no longer change a proof, but they change what a later ordinary `git fetch` or `git push` of the user does; the push step still runs in the project repository (it only needs the approval-bound url). SECURITY ROUND 5 (the last round for the merge proof; cheap hardening only): a same-user interpreter the hook allows could still write into the throwaway repository (`refs/replace/*`, `info/grafts`, config, hooks, planted by a polling loop in the shared TMPDIR) or rewrite a loose object of the project's store that the proof reads through the alternate (git does not hash-check an object it reads). Done: the throwaway repository has an unpredictable name inside a private (0700) `~/.cache/proofline-proof` of the account (the temporary folder only when that cannot be made), is created from an empty template, every git call of the proof runs with `--no-replace-objects`, `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE` off, and `intact()` compares config, hooks, info, refs/replace, alternates and shallow with what was created, after the fetch and again before anything is recorded (fail closed). The ancestry is no longer asked of git: `reaches` walks the parents of every commit of `rb..tip` itself (git's list only narrows the walk: a lie there can hide a path, never invent one), each commit read with its hash recomputed, and refuses on a mismatch, a missing object or more than 20000 commits since the run's base; for a squash or rebase proof every commit of that range is re-hashed the same way. Cost: one `cat-file --batch` per level of the walk over the commits that landed since the run's base, so a few milliseconds on an ordinary repository. NOT COVERED: tree and blob objects of the squash and rebase proof are read by git without a hash check (the path list and the content comparison trust the object store), and a same-user process can still change anything between two checks. DECISION FOR THE OWNER (kararını bekliyor): the remaining trust boundary of the merge proof is the same-user file system. An interpreter the hook allows (node, python) can forge whatever the user could; the real fix is at the hook or sandbox level, the same class as A211. The shell proof that this replaced had the same boundary with weaker checks (a bare git on the caller's PATH, the project's own configuration, no pin of the origin).
