- **A217. Stage 4 closing decisions: three process counts accepted, and the nested headless runtime is an accepted limit (user decision; no release; refs #169, issue comments https://github.com/furkansarikaya/proofline/issues/169; follows A212 to A214 and A211; see A218).** USER DECISION (kullanıcı kararı), taken by the maintainer after stages 4 and 6: (1) The process counts that stayed slightly above the stage targets are accepted: `delivery-check` 8 (target 6), `secret-scan` 14 (target 6) and `publish-completion-report` 22 (target 20); the extra processes are the git calls that list the task's changed paths. This closes the "kararını bekliyor" items of A212 and A214 on these counts. (2) That a model can forge a user-only answer (an INTENT scope decision, the split override, an assumption acceptance) by starting a nested headless runtime in its own session (`python3 -c ... subprocess.run(['claude','-p',text,'--resume',$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID])`, a perl `system`, `find -exec claude -p`, a scratch `node` script), which the Bash guard allows because it matches the command word only, is an **accepted limit** and not a defect to fix: hooks read command text and cannot see everything, they are tripwires against honest mistakes, and the boundary against a hostile agent is the runtime's permission mode and sandbox (`.out-of-scope/small-rejected-ideas.md`, entry "Hook guards as a security boundary against a hostile agent"). The same limit already stands in A211. Why: no hook can close every spelling of "start a runtime", and the cost of chasing them is a growing list of command-text rules with no boundary behind it. Rejected: denying any exec of a runtime binary by argv anywhere in a command (a longer tripwire list, still not a boundary); requiring a user-turn marker in the hook payload (the runtime does not provide one). Not tested: nothing new; the limit was found by the security review of #196 and recorded as a comment on #169.

- **A218. Stage 6 closing decision: the merge proof trusts the same user's file system (user decision; no release; refs #171, issue comment https://github.com/furkansarikaya/proofline/issues/171; follows A215, A216, A217).** USER DECISION (kullanıcı kararı), taken by the maintainer after stage 6: the merge proof of `deliver-merged` and of the standalone `cleanup` rests on the same user's file system. An interpreter that the hook allows can write the throwaway repository of the proof, the project's `.git/objects` or `.git/config`, or put a fake tool in a folder the user can write, and so forge a merge. This is an **accepted limit**: hooks are tripwires, and the real boundary is the runtime's permission mode and sandbox (`.out-of-scope/small-rejected-ideas.md`, entry "Hook guards as a security boundary against a hostile agent"). The hardening of A215 and A216 stays (the delivery summary bound to the approval the user answered, the hermetic fetch in a private repository, the hash-verified history walk, the tool location judged by folder identity, the allowlisted environment of the platform tools) and is not to be extended further for this class; the shell proof had the same boundary with weaker checks. The hook gaps that stay open (`git config http.*`, `declare -x PATH=...` forms, writing a fake tool into a user-writable folder) are the same accepted limit. The follow-ups that came out of stage 6 (proxy and CA variables for the platform tools and the merge-proof git, the GitHub Enterprise host from `git.platform_host`) are listed in the epic #165 under "Follow-up". Rejected: more hook rules for this class (they add tripwires and no boundary); a signed record that the control plane alone can write (the control plane runs as the same user).

- **A219. `discard-stray` also removes a stray file one level inside `evidence/` (patch; #195; follows A119, A212).** What: `agent.sh discard-stray <ID> evidence/<file-name>` (lead only, run open and not sealed, as before) removes one regular file directly inside the run's `evidence/` folder. The file name follows the A119 rules (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, no leading `.` or `-`); the folder part is exactly the lowercase word `evidence`, one level, nothing else (`..`, absolute paths, `evidence/a/b`, `Evidence/x`, an empty name are refused with the existing "single top-level" or "may contain only" text). The run directory and `evidence/` must resolve (realpath) to a plain folder inside the run, never a symlink; the file is never a symlink, never a directory, and never the same inode as a protected top-level artifact (a hard-link alias of PLAN.md is refused; the inodes are read from the real directory entries whose lower-cased name is protected, `PLAN.md` and not `plan.md`, so it holds on a case-sensitive file system too). It is ledgered like today: `event=discard-stray ... path=evidence/<file> sha256=<hash>`. The "unexpected run artifact" message of `validate_control_artifacts` (Node and the shell copy), the `data.mjs` and `agent.sh` usage line and ENFORCEMENT.md name the new form. The hook's `rm` protection is unchanged. What "real evidence" means here (the decision the code could not give, taken on the safe side, Core invariant 6): the registry (`known_control_artifact`) has no `evidence/` folder at all (`EVIDENCE.md` is a top-level file; cited evidence must live in `reports/` or `worker-evidence/`, `evidence_cite_check` A107), so every file under `evidence/` is already an "unexpected run artifact" and no gate, result or approval can name one. As an extra guard the command still refuses (`cited by a run record`) when the exact run-relative path `evidence/<file>` appears as a whole token (compared case-insensitively, as the file system folds case; the project-relative `.agents/runs/<ID>/evidence/<file>` and an absolute path ending in it count too, any other prefix is a different path) in RUN.yaml, LEDGER.log (its own `discard-stray` rows are not counted), EVIDENCE.md, VERIFY.md, QA_REPORT.md, COMPLETION_REPORT.md or a file of `gates/`, `approvals/`, `waivers/`, `worker-evidence/`, `decisions/`; a record that cannot be read counts as cited. The free text of `reports/`, `results/`, `dispatch/` and `security/` is not read, because an explorer's report and its assignment name the very file that is the stray. Why: an explorer wrote a copy into `evidence/` (its assignment's write path); `discard-stray` refused subfolders and the hook denies the lead's `rm`, so the run parked (T-2 parked, T-3 skipped). Known limits and the one open question for the user: a file under `evidence/` that only a report (not a record above) calls proof can be discarded; the sha256 stays in the ledger, the file does not. Whether `evidence/` should become a registered, valid folder (and so stop being a stray at all) is a separate design decision and is not made here. Other subfolders (`reports/`, `scratch/`, `design/`) are not reachable by the command; they are registered folders, so a file there is not a stray. The check-then-delete is not atomic (as in A119). Rejected: accepting any `<folder>/<file>` (the registry depends on case and symlink resolution, A119); letting the lead `rm` in `evidence/` (reopens the writable-run-state hole the hook closes); registering `evidence/` as a known folder (makes a stray look valid and lets unreviewed files sit in a run); deleting by content hash (an explorer's copy of a real file has the real file's hash). **User decision (2026-11-07):** `evidence/` is not a registered run folder and does not become one; the list of registered run artifacts stays as it is (evidence lives in `reports/` and `worker-evidence/`). `discard-stray <ID> evidence/<file-name>` stays as the cleanup path for strays only. The open question above is closed; the source of the strays is fixed in A223.
- **A220. Corporate network and GitHub Enterprise: proxy and certificate variables reach the platform tools and the merge-proof git, and the host variable comes only from `git.platform_host` (patch; epic #165 follow-up decided by the maintainer after stages 4 and 6; follows A136, A186, A215, A216, A218; the next number after A218 is taken because another open pull request holds the one between).** WHAT. (1) `cleanToolEnv` (`core/platform.mjs`; callers `runTool`, `merge.mjs`, `deliver.mjs`, `adapters/index.mjs`) keeps `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, their lowercase forms, `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` when the value passes a narrow check, and drops it (never repairs it, says nothing) when it does not. Proxy (`proxyValue`): `http://` or `https://`, optional percent-encoded `user[:password]@`, a host name, IPv4 or bracketed IPv6 address, optional port, at most one trailing slash; no path, query, fragment, whitespace or control character, at most 2048 characters; no socks, no bare `host:port`. NO_PROXY (`noProxyValue`): comma separated plain entries (host, `.suffix`, `*.suffix`, address, `/bits`, `:port`, `*`), at most one space after a comma, at most 4096 characters; it can only make a call skip the proxy. Certificate (`caFileValue`): an absolute path of an existing regular file (a link is followed) that is neither named nor resolved into the project, the working directory or a temporary folder (`refusedLocation`, the rule the PATH entries already follow); a relative path, a missing file, a folder or a control character is dropped. Every other proxy or certificate variable stays dropped (`ALL_PROXY`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `GIT_SSL_*`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`). The same function serves `gh`, `glab`, `az` and, with `remote`, the git of the merge proof (the hermetic fetch, `ls-remote`, the push), so every tool gets the same set; a proxy without a certificate and a certificate without a proxy are both fine. WHY IT STAYS SAFE (A136, A215): the aim of the allowlist is that no model can send the tool to a server that fakes a merged pull request or a green run. A proxy carries `https` as a CONNECT tunnel and the tool still checks the server certificate, so a proxy of a model's choosing cannot forge an answer unless it is paired with a certificate the tool trusts; the certificate must be a file the model cannot write (not the project, the working directory, a temporary folder), the shape check leaves no room for a second address, a path or a shell fragment, and `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` that would loosen or replace the trust stay dropped. A model that can write a file outside those folders (the same user's file system) is the A218 accepted limit. (2) The host variable: `platformEnv` exports `GH_HOST` or `GITLAB_HOST` only when `git.platform` and `git.platform_host` of `.agents/config.yaml` decided the platform (source `config`, which needs the host to equal the origin host) and the platform is not a known public host; a platform named by the `PROOFLINE_PLATFORM` variable (source `env`) now gets no host variable (before: the origin host was exported), and `git.platform` without `platform_host` was already untrusted. The caller's `GH_HOST` was and is dropped by the allowlist. Verified in the three readers: check delivery (`pr-state`, `batch-ci`, the ci readers, the merged proof: all `runTool`), `proofline merge` (`cleanToolEnv` + `platformEnv` of `detectPlatform`) and the github adapter (`hostEnv`); no reader needed a code change beyond `platformEnv`. Tests (Node, A210): `tests/core/run6-corpnet.test.mjs` 10 (proxy, NO_PROXY and certificate tables; `cleanToolEnv` also with `remote`; gh, glab and az each against a fake tool that dumps its environment; the host only from the config; check delivery, `merge` and the github adapter with a hostile `GH_HOST`; the hook state below); `run6-platform.test.mjs` updated (the hostile list no longer holds the variables that now pass; the private host comes from a config project). Deleted: 0 shell lines (the moved behaviour had no shell code left; `tests/enforcement/platform-test.sh` keeps its black-box checks of `env`, which still pass). HOOK STATE (changed in security round 1, see below): the merge guard now denies a proxy or certificate variable named in the command that runs the merge proof or a platform tool, like `PATH=`. ACCEPTED LIMITS (tripwires, not a boundary; `.out-of-scope/small-rejected-ideas.md`, "Hook guards as a security boundary against a hostile agent"; the list of what the hook cannot see in A136 and in `docs/concepts/enforcement-layers.md` is extended): `git config http.*` (`http.proxy`, `http.sslCAInfo`, `http.<url>.*`, set in a config file the same user can write) and `declare -x PATH=...` forms (also `typeset -x`, `readonly X=v; export X`) are not caught by the hook; no test (test-free note: the hook is not widened). LIMITS OF THIS CHANGE: a dropped value gives no message, the tool then fails with its own network error (a message would need a new output on every caller; kararını bekliyor: whether `proofline doctor` should list a dropped proxy or certificate variable); a proxy that needs a certificate in a user-writable temporary folder is refused (the user keeps the bundle in their home or a system folder); `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and `AZURE_CLI_*` for `az` and `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` for git are not passed (kararını bekliyor: add them if a network cannot use `SSL_CERT_FILE`); the Node children of the `jira` and `linear` adapters are outside this change. SECURITY ROUND 1 (review FAIL, two blocking findings, both reproduced against real gh). (1) `proofline merge` has the install folder as its root, so `refusedDirs` refused only the working directory of the project: a certificate the model wrote elsewhere in the project passed, and `SSL_CERT_FILE=<project>/.agents/local/scratch/ca.pem HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:PORT proofline merge N` made a forged server answer a green pull request. Fixed in two layers. (a) `caFileValue` now also refuses the working tree of the working directory and of the root (the nearest ancestor with a `.git`, found from the file system, no git call), the main checkout of a linked worktree (the `gitdir:` line of a `.git` file) and any path with a `.agents` component, for the path and for its real path; and the file and every folder above its real path must be owned by root or by this user and not writable by a group or by everybody. (b) The hook's inline tripwire that denied `PATH=` before `proofline merge`, `agent.sh`, `gh`, `glab` or `az` (`merge.mjs`, `env`/`export`/inline prefix) now denies `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, their lowercase forms, `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` in the same way; the same variables with an unrelated command (`curl`, `npm`, `git fetch`, a bare `export`) pass, and `GH_HOST=` stays unlisted because the allowlist drops it. This reverses the first text of this entry, which said the hook accepts the inline form. (2) `merge.mjs` treated any output of `gh pr checks --required` containing "no required checks" as an empty required list; a proxy answering CONNECT with that reason phrase makes gh print `Post "https://api.github.com/graphql": no required checks`, so the required checks were skipped. Now only gh's own sentence, whole and alone (`no required checks reported on the '<branch>' branch`), counts; any other failure refuses the merge. The fakes of `run6b-merge`, `merge-guard-test.sh` and `platform-test.sh` print the genuine sentence. RESIDUAL RISK, an accepted limit (same user's file system, A218; `.out-of-scope/small-rejected-ideas.md`, "Hook guards as a security boundary against a hostile agent"): a model that writes a certificate in a folder that passes the checks (a folder of its own that is private to the user and outside the project, such as one under the home folder) and starts the merge through a wrapper script, `git config http.*` or `declare -x PATH=...`, which the hook does not see. Tests: `run6-corpnet` (the unit table with a project outside the temporary folders, the worktree, `.agents` and permission cases; `proofline merge` started with a project certificate and a loopback proxy gives gh no certificate; the hook denial table and the passing table), `run6b-merge` (the proxy-style error refuses, the genuine sentence passes), `tests/hook/merge-guard.test.mjs` (denied and allowed rows); each fails on the code before the fix. SECURITY ROUND 2 (re-review of round 1: SECURITY-2 closed, SECURITY-1 still open). (1) `proofline merge -R OWNER/REPO` runs from ANY directory, so a project found by walking up from the working directory or the root missed a project file when the directory was elsewhere (`/usr`, a library folder), and a nested repository hid the outer project (the walk stopped at the first `.git`). The structural fix decides from the FILE: `caFileValue` walks up from the path and from the real path of the certificate through EVERY ancestor to the filesystem root and refuses when any ancestor holds a `.git` entry (directory or file: a repository, a nested one, a linked worktree) or an `.agents` entry; the rules of round 1 (working tree of the directory and root, main checkout of a worktree, temporary folders, `.agents` component, owner and mode of the file and every folder above it) stay. Consequence, accepted: a certificate under a home directory that itself holds `.git` (dotfiles) or an `.agents` folder is dropped, so the user keeps the bundle in a plain folder or a system folder. (2) The hook also denies the prefix-append form `HTTPS_PROXY+=v`, `SSL_CERT_FILE+=v` (and `PATH+=v`) in the command that runs the merge proof (the scanner does not see it as an assignment, so it is read from the command text as a word of its own); `declare -x`, `typeset -x` and `readonly X=v; export X` are not seen and join the accepted limits next to `declare -x PATH=...`. (3) The test for 'does this command run the merge proof or a platform tool' was a substring match on the whole command (`merge`, `gh`); it is now by command word: a command word, or an argument whose base name is `proofline`, `agent.sh`, `proofline-core.mjs`, `gh`, `glab` or `az` (`sh agent.sh`, `xargs gh`), so `NO_PROXY=x npm run lint-merge`, `git merge-base` and `--grep=merge` pass. Tests: `run6-corpnet` (a project in the home directory with a nested repository, a linked worktree and an `.agents` folder, judged from `/usr`, `/` and a plain folder; a plain folder passes where the home allows it, with the permission cases; `proofline merge` from `/var` with `-R`; the hook rows for `+=`, the false positives and the new accepted limits) and `tests/hook/merge-guard.test.mjs`. Rejected: a boundary claim for the hook; allowing the certificate only from a fixed list of system folders (breaks a certificate in the user's home). Rejected: passing the caller's whole proxy and certificate environment as before the allowlist (any model could aim the merge proof at its own server); a fixed list of allowed proxy hosts in `config.yaml` (a new config surface and a second source of truth for what the network admin already set); refusing the whole command with an error on a bad value (it would stop a delivery over a variable the tool might not need; a drop fails closed on its own); denying the inline form in the hook (a longer tripwire list, no boundary); exporting the host from `PROOFLINE_PLATFORM` as before (the caller names the platform, so the caller would pick the server). SECURITY ROUND 3 (re-review of round 2: three tripwire regressions of the command-word test, denied again; they cannot forge the merge proof). The command-word test of round 2 missed three spellings that the first text (a substring match) had caught: (a) `env -S "HTTPS_PROXY=... proofline merge 7"` and `HTTPS_PROXY=... env -S "gh pr view 7"` (also `-S"..."` and `--split-string=...`; the scanner reports an `env -S` record and cannot split the string, so the guard reads the text: a proxy or certificate variable assigned anywhere in it plus a tool name as a word, `proofline`, `agent.sh`, `gh`, `glab` or `az`); (b) a command word that is a variable expansion (`p=gh; HTTPS_PROXY=... $p pr view 7`, `${p}`, `"$p"`, `${GH:-gh}`, a backtick) counts as running a tool, since it can be any of them; (c) an interpreter's inline program (`node -e`, `nodejs`, `bun`, `deno`, `perl -e`, `python3 -c`, `ruby -e`, `php`, `lua`) whose program text names a tool as a word counts as running it. The false-positive fixes of round 2 stay (`NO_PROXY=x npm run lint-merge`, `git merge-base`, `--grep=merge`, `node -e "console.log(1)"`, `node script.js`, `env -S "npm test"`). Cost: a variable command word in a command that also sets one of these variables is denied even if it is not a tool (`HTTPS_PROXY=x $CC ...`; the user writes the command word literally). No new process (text and record tests only; the hook budgets are unchanged). Accepted limits unchanged and extended: a tool named by a script file, by a string built at run time or by an interpreter that is not listed is not seen. Tests: `tests/hook/merge-guard.test.mjs` (denied rows for a-c, allowed rows for the false positives). USER DECISION (2026-11-07): both open questions are answered YES. (1) `proofline doctor` lists the proxy and certificate variables that were DROPPED: one WARN line, `network: these proxy or certificate variables are set here but NOT passed to gh, glab, az and the merge-proof git (values are never shown): NAME (reason); ...`. The names come from a fixed list (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and the lowercase forms, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` when their value fails the check; `ALL_PROXY`, `all_proxy`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` whenever set) or, for the rest of the family, from `GIT_SSL_[A-Z0-9_]{1,40}` (any other name is not printed); the reason is a sentence of a closed set (`caFileProblem` for a certificate: not an absolute path, not an existing regular file, inside the project, the working directory or a temporary folder, a `.git` or `.agents` entry above it, writable by a group or by everybody, owned by another user; a proxy: not an http or https address of the allowed shape; `never passed ...`) and never the value, because a proxy address may hold credentials. The helper is `proofline-core.mjs cli platform-info net-dropped` (`droppedNetVars` in `core/platform.mjs`, the same code that decides what `cleanToolEnv` keeps); `bin/lib/doctor.sh` (`doctor_netenv`) filters its lines through a plain alphabet before printing, so even a changed helper cannot print a quote, a backtick or a `$`. Nothing is printed when nothing was dropped. (2) `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` (the Python of `az`) and `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` (the git of the merge proof) are allowed through the SAME `caFileValue` check as `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` (an absolute path of an existing regular file, outside the project, the working directory and temporary folders, no `.git` or `.agents` entry above it, owner and mode of the file and of every folder above its real path, the link target checked too), for gh, glab, az and, with `remote`, the merge-proof git. Every other variable stays dropped (`ALL_PROXY`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `GIT_SSL_*` other than `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`). The merge guard (`adapters/claude/hooks/guards/merge.mjs`: `RE_NET_VAR`, `RE_NET_APPEND`, `RE_NET_ANY` and the deny texts) names the two new variables: inline, `env`, `export`, the `+=` form and `env -S` in a command that runs `gh`, `glab`, `az`, `proofline merge` or `agent.sh` are denied like the other certificate variables (tripwire, not a boundary, as before). The merge proof stays closed: a model that can steer `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` or `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` to a file only gets what `SSL_CERT_FILE` already allowed (a file it cannot write), and a replaced trust store without a proxy of its choosing cannot reach a server of its own. Tests: `tests/core/run6-netdropped.test.mjs` (the two names kept and dropped by the same matrix as `SSL_CERT_FILE`, with and without `remote`; every other variable dropped; `droppedNetVars` names, reasons, no value, a hostile variable name not printed; `proofline doctor` in an installed project with a credential in the proxy value: listed, no value anywhere in stdout or stderr, silent without a dropped variable), `tests/core/run6-corpnet.test.mjs` (updated matrix, gh/glab/az each see the new variables, hook rows), `tests/hook/merge-guard.test.mjs` (deny and allow rows for both names).
- **A221. The last status block of a merged task no longer depends on the main working tree being fast-forwarded (patch; #172 package 172-A; amends A202 item 10, follows A215 and A216).** Symptom: in the real-session smoke the hermetic batch rows "status block (T-2)/(T-3): one section, updated in place, MERGED, no local path" failed with "no task file of T-x holds a status block" although the rows "batch T-2 T-3 (both reach origin main)" and "branch name" passed (default run of 0.0.52 twice, 2 of 3 runs on #195 and #165). **Cause (Node reproduction, not a model effect):** `deliver-merged` and `deliver-step cleanup` write the MERGED block with `sbFinalPut` after the run and its worktree are gone. `sbFinalPut` put the block only when the path named by the run's `task_source.path` (after `task-source-done`: `<tasks>/done/<file>`) existed in the main working tree. That path appears there only when the merge was fast-forwarded into the main tree; when it was not (an uncommitted edit of a tracked file such as the approved-commands `.agents/config.yaml` that is not identical to origin's, a local commit origin lacks, another branch checked out), the task file is still at its old path, the guard returned silently, no note was printed, and the worktree was removed with the only copy of the block (the earlier blocks were written to the worktree copy). The merge itself, `merged.tsv` and the branch were all correct, which is why only the block rows failed. One kept fixture of a passing `SMOKE_ONLY=a202` run shows the happy path (both blocks MERGED in `done/T-2.md` and `done/T-3.md`, put by `sbFinalPut` after a clean fast-forward); the failing run could not be kept, so the trigger in the smoke (which file made the main tree not fast-forwardable) is inferred, the mechanism is reproduced: `tests/core/run6-merged.test.mjs` "A221" (a local commit origin lacks; a tracked file edited) fail without the change with the exact message of the smoke and pass with it. **Fix:** `sbFinalPut` (core/deliver.mjs) no longer asks whether the run's recorded path exists in the main tree and no longer skips when the delivery ran in the main tree itself; it hands the block to the task adapter, which finds the task file by id wherever it is now (old path or `done/`). The block is the same one as before (recorded state only, scrubbed, no local path); only a task without any file (`task_source.path` empty) puts nothing. A later fast-forward of the main tree still finds the block as a block-only edit of the task file and carries it (`sbMainPark`/`sbMainPut`, unchanged). **Not changed (stated):** the other symptom recorded in #172 (T-3 parked "awaiting merge", stage "PR OPEN") was not reproduced (the one run of this package passed) and no control-plane defect was found for it: the block says PR OPEN until the control plane is told the merge happened, which is the design of A202 and of the smoke's own comment, so it fits a lead session that ended before it ran `deliver-merged`; the control plane cannot record a merge the user did on a local origin without the lead telling it (A180, A215), so no deterministic change exists there; the smoke rows stay as they are. One passing run does not prove that variance is gone: the confirming run is in the pull request. **Observation, not fixed here:** `deliver-merged` called in the main working tree with `main` checked out (not on the delivery branch) records the merge and then stops in the cleanup with "wrong git branch"; and in that case the run's task path is `done/` before the fast-forward, so the `merged` update at the start is a logged note. Rejected: loosening the smoke rows or reading the worktree copy; writing the block into the delivered commit (it must stay uncommitted output, A202); a retry loop around the fast-forward (the cause is a tree that legitimately cannot be fast-forwarded); making the batch record merges without the lead (A180, A215: no file, flag or lock says "merged").
- **A222. Node migration, stage 7, package 172-B: the execution policy, the runtime detection and the known-issues list run in Node (patch; #172; follows A210, A202 item 27, A135, A203).** Moved: `scripts/exec-policy.sh` (302 lines) -> `core/execpolicy.mjs`, called as `proofline-core.mjs cli exec-policy resolve|explain|check-capabilities|check-lead|lead-base|runtime`; `scripts/runtime-detect.sh` (37) -> `core/runtimedetect.mjs`, `cli runtime-detect [has|bin <runtime>]`; `scripts/known-issues.sh` (194) -> `core/kirules.mjs` (canon, listable, lookup, followup-state, append, list, candidates, the approval check) and the four commands `known-issue-propose`, `known-issue-apply`, `known-issue-list`, `known-issue-candidates` -> `core/commands/kicmds.mjs` (their `agent.sh` arms and functions, and the shell copies of `finding_known_issue`, `finding_batch_accepted`, `ki_gate_facts` with their call sites in `finding_waived`, `gate_label`, the Facts block and the status block, are deleted). Deleted in the same change (A210, no bridge, no fallback): `exec-policy.sh`, `exec-policy-test.sh` (209), `runtime-detect.sh`, `known-issues.sh`, `known-issues-test.sh` (263): 1,005 lines of sh. No environment value reaches a decision: without the stub the resolver reads only `.agents/config.yaml` and `.agents/roles.conf`, and a test (`tests/core/exec-policy.test.mjs`) sets `PROOFLINE_TEST*`, `EXEC_POLICY_CONFIG`, `EXEC_POLICY_ROLES`, `STUB_ARGS` and the runtime binaries and gets the identical decision. The stub is looked for in the project's trusted scripts folder (the main tree's from a task worktree, like the other helper scripts), not the worktree's own copy. An `exec-policy.sh` that a user modified and `upgrade` therefore kept as an orphan is still run as a stub: this is the rule as written, and `upgrade` lists the file as an orphan. **Behaviour and file formats are unchanged**; what differs, on purpose: (1) the resolver's `EXEC_POLICY_CONFIG` and `EXEC_POLICY_ROLES` environment values are gone (an environment seam); `cli exec-policy --config <file> [--roles <file>]` names another pair for a check outside a project (the end-to-end harness, `capabilities-test.sh`), roles default to `roles.conf` beside the config; `decide` never passes them. (2) `check-capabilities` reads the Codex model cache itself and no longer needs `jq`. (3) The usage text of an unknown operation, and `decide`'s refusal text (`decision refused by the execution policy (exit N)`), no longer name `exec-policy.sh`. (4) Known issues: the shell read rows with `IFS=<tab> read`, which collapses empty fields and shifts the others (an empty place made the text the place); the Node code splits strictly, and `canon` refuses a finding with an empty gate, place or text (it can only make an invalid record); a place must match the whole string (`grep` matched any line of a place with a newline); `candidates` lists one line per (gate, place, text) and takes the first run in folder order, where the shell kept an arbitrary one (awk hash order); the next record number counts the list and `CLOSED.tsv` whether or not the second exists (on awks that stop at a missing file the shell numbered 1 again). (5) `runtime-detect` finds `claude.exe` and the like on Windows. (6) The `KI_*` environment values of `known-issues.sh` are gone with the script. **Parity kept (review round 1):** `--context-bytes` (and the class and hard-limit budgets) follow the shell's 64-bit integer range: a number beyond 9223372036854775807 is `INVALID_OVERRIDE` (rc 3) as in the shell, where `[ -gt ]` failed on it, and the digits are echoed as written (`007` stays `context_bytes=007`, a cap echoes the config's own digits); the golden corpus holds these edges. Other integers (`--escalations-used`, tiers) are read with JavaScript numbers, so a value beyond 2^53 differs from the shell only where the shell itself would have failed or compared a value no config holds. Approvals stay exactly as they were: a known-issue record exists only after the user's own `approve known issue`, bound to the sha256 of `gate TAB place TAB text TAB follow-up LF` (Core invariant 3); `approvalOk` accepts and refuses the same files for the same bytes (known answers and one-byte-changed cases in `tests/core/legacy-known-issues.test.mjs`). **Tests, written with the area:** `tests/core/exec-policy.test.mjs` (742 calls (722 and the edges of `--context-bytes`) recorded once from the shell resolver of 0.0.52 against ten config variants, `tests/core/golden/exec-policy/`, recorder `golden/exec-policy-record.mjs`; the rules `exec-policy-test.sh` stated as named assertions; the shipped `config.yaml` and `roles.conf`; the stub and the environment; runtime detection), `tests/core/legacy-known-issues.test.mjs` (every scenario of `known-issues-test.sh` against the real control plane, plus the data rules as units), `tests/bench/exec-budgets.test.mjs`; `tests/legacy-port-map.tsv` has the rows. **Performance** (`tests/bench/exec-procs.mjs`, external processes started through the PATH, the measured command included, median of 3; before = the shell form of 0.0.52 on the same fixture, wall time in ms): resolver 18 -> 1 (210 -> 104), `decide --dry` 152 -> 133 (1.76 s -> 1.9 s; the rest of `decide` is shell until 172-D), runtime detection `has` 2 -> 1 (25 -> 89: a Node start costs more than a shell start; the lists 5 -> 2), `known-issue-propose` 112 -> 3 (1010 -> 168), `known-issue-apply` 71 -> 3 (677 -> 155), `known-issue-list` 39 -> 2 (293 -> 123), `known-issue-candidates` 78 -> 3 (535 -> 141), `approve - known-issue` 2 -> 2 (already Node). Budgets: `tests/bench/exec-budgets.tsv` (measured plus max(2, 25 percent); `decide --dry` plus 10 percent); `known-issue-list` stays within 96 bytes on the fixture and the resolver within 389. **Budget scope, stated plainly:** `tests/bench/output-budgets.tsv` (and `process-budgets.tsv`) were added on main in db8c911a (stage 2) and deleted in b96e5553 (A210, with the shell-engine bench tooling); at the base commit of this package neither exists (only `tests/bench/hook-budgets.tsv` does), so these budgets are new: `tests/bench/exec-budgets.tsv` covers only `known-issue-list` (96 bytes) and the resolver (389 bytes), plus process counts for the nine paths above. The other read commands the issue names (`batch-status`, `batch-next`, `batch-answers`) are batch.sh's: their output and process budgets are set in the package that moves batch.sh (172-C), not here. Rejected: leaving `exec-policy.sh` as a launcher of the core (A210: no bridges); keeping the `EXEC_POLICY_*` environment values for the tests (D14: no environment seam; the stub file and the explicit `--config` do the same); porting `decide` here (it is the dispatch package's, 172-D). Not changed: `dispatch.sh`, `batch.sh`, `worktree-prep.sh` (172-C, 172-D).

- **A224. An attribution instruction never parks a delivery; the approved commit line is delivered as written (patch; #172 package 172-A2; follows A136, A151, A200).** What: a kept fixture of the real-session smoke (hermetic batch, `SMOKE_ONLY=a202`) showed both batch tasks ending `PARKED (by the lead)` at the delivery step with the reason "Delivery held: the approved commit message is one line, but the attribution rule asks for a Co-Authored-By trailer in commit messages. The message cannot carry a trailer through deliver-plan (one-line rule) and must not be edited by hand. Question: deliver T-2 without the trailer, or allow the trailer (a proofline change)?". CAUSE (two parts, both read in the transcript): (1) the Claude Code harness adds a system instruction "end git commit messages with Co-Authored-By ..." to a default session (and a user's rule files such as a commit-trailer rule do the same); nothing in the lead texts said that a delivery commit is outside it. (2) A real contradiction in the product: after `deliver-plan` the lead grepped `deliver.mjs` and found the two refusal hints "add a trailer through agent.sh deliver-plan <ID> --message <text with the trailer lines> before the approval" (since A200, item 18), while `deliver-plan` itself refuses a message with a newline ("the commit message is one line"). A trailer therefore had no path, and a haiku-class lead concluded it had to ask. Both hints are older than the Node port (they come from the shell engine) and were never exercised. Fix (text and hint only, no behaviour change): (a) `skills/proofline-lead/SKILL.md` rule 8, `references/DELIVERY.md` section 5 and `control-plane/agents/GIT.md` state that the commit message of a delivery is the one approved line, committed as written (`git commit -F COMMIT_MSG`); a trailer or attribution instruction from the harness or the user's rules does not change it and is never a reason to park, ask, edit `COMMIT_MSG` or commit by hand (invariant 6: in doubt the safe side, do not alter approved text); (b) the two refusal hints of `deliver-step` no longer point at a trailer path that cannot work, they say to run `deliver-plan` again and that the approved line is never edited by hand; the one-line refusal of `deliver-plan` says a trailer is not part of it and no reason to ask. The lead SKILL.md budget line (`role.lead.skill`) grows with it (total in the second cause below). Tests: `tests/core/run6-plan.test.mjs` (an attribution setting in the home folder changes nothing: `COMMIT_MSG` is exactly the given line, a multi-line message with a trailer is refused and leaves no file, a hand-edited `COMMIT_MSG` with a trailer is refused with the corrected hint), `tests/skills/proofline-lead.test.mjs` (known good texts, known bad hint). DECISION WAS OPEN until 2026-11-07 (it is decided and implemented in the USER DECISION (2026-11-07) paragraph at the end of this entry; at the time: kararını bekliyor, a user decision, not implemented, a behaviour change = "a proofline change", `.out-of-scope/README.md` read: no entry matches): should the control plane itself append the configured attribution trailer to the delivery commit? Alternatives: (1) keep as now (the delivery commit never carries a trailer; the user's attribution preference is not honoured on proofline commits); (2) a config key `git.commit_trailer` (empty by default) that `deliver-plan` appends as a second paragraph of `COMMIT_MSG`, shown verbatim in the summary and covered by `message_sha256`, so the approval binds the trailer, the user sets it once and it needs no lead decision (adds a config surface and relaxes the "one line" rule of `deliver-plan`; the PR title/`%s` checks of `deliver-step` stay on the first line; a trailer line must be validated like the message: no `"`, backtick, `$`, `\`, one `Co-Authored-By: Name <email>` shape); (3) read the harness attribution setting (`attribution`/`includeCoAuthoredBy` of `~/.claude/settings.json` or the project) automatically (rejected as default: it makes the commit depend on files outside the project and a second runtime (Codex) has none; an agent-readable setting also lets repository text steer the message). Trade-off: (2) honours attribution and removes the whole class, at the cost of one config key and a multi-line `COMMIT_MSG`; (1) is the safest and what is shipped. Rejected for this patch: letting the lead append a trailer or edit `COMMIT_MSG` (breaks the approved-text binding of A151); making the pre-commit hook rewrite the message (a hook that edits approved text); telling the smoke to turn attribution off with a project setting (it would hide the real-user case that failed). SECOND CAUSE, same package (kept fixture of the confirming `a202` run on the first commit: the attribution park did not recur, T-2 was delivered, T-3 stayed `RUNNING`): the lead ran `dispatch.sh T-3 implementer` in the foreground under its own tool timeout (exit 124, "Terminated: 15"). `dispatch.sh` traps TERM with `exit 143` and `finish` stops the worker, but the implementer's write window is closed only inline after the worker returns (`window-close`), so a dispatch killed from outside leaves partial edits in the task paths that no worker window recorded. The next `D` is refused (`window-open refused`; the core says the tree is not the last attested one and names `tree-inspect` / `tree-accept`), and the lead put a prose question to the user in a loop until the reply cap. Fix (guidance and wording only): `DISPATCH.md` and `SKILL.md` rule 4 say a worker `D` takes minutes and is started in the background (`run_in_background`), the lead waits for the completion notice and never runs it in the foreground under a tool timeout or a `timeout` of its own; `FAILOVER.md` (interrupted implementer) and the `window-open refused` line of `dispatch.sh` give the recovery: `tree-inspect`, ONE question with both answers (keep the tree with `tree-accept`, or discard the listed files and dispatch again), no re-dispatch, discard or hand edit before the answer, and in a batch `batch-park` that task. No safe automatic recovery exists without weakening `tree-accept` (invariant 3 and 6: the user approves an unattested tree; deleting task files is destructive and no batch approval covers it), so the question stays. The `role.lead.skill` budget line is 45400 in total (45150 before A224; about 250 bytes of text); the pull request description carries the `Context-budget-change:` line. DECISION WAS OPEN until 2026-11-07 (it is decided and implemented in the USER DECISION (2026-11-07) paragraph at the end of this entry; at the time: kararını bekliyor, a user decision, not implemented, a behaviour change in `dispatch.sh`): should a dispatch killed from outside (TERM, HUP, INT) close the implementer's write window itself, as the 124 timeout path already does (stop the worker first, then `window-close` with the signal status, so the partial edits are attested as the implementer's own and the next `D` simply continues the step)? For: it removes the whole class (a killed dispatch behaves like a timed-out one; GIT.md already says the control plane "records attested history even for a failed run"); no user question. Against: the close runs in a trap while the worker may still hold files open, a kill that comes from an attacker-controlled parent would attest a tree the worker did not finish, and it changes a path that invariants 4 and 5 depend on, so it needs its own review and tests (it belongs with the `dispatch.sh` port, package 172-D, where the trap can be tested properly). Alternatives: (1) keep as shipped (guidance plus one question); (2) close the window in the trap; (3) `dispatch.sh` refuses to start in a foreground process group of a tool with a timeout (not detectable reliably). Rejected: a lead-side `tree-accept` without the user's reply; discarding the files by the lead. USER DECISION (2026-11-07): the open question is answered YES, alternative (2): the control plane itself appends the attribution trailer to the delivery commit. WHAT "today's rule" is: the Claude Code harness instruction "end git commit messages with Co-Authored-By: <model> <noreply@anthropic.com>" (and a user's rule files that say the same); the default line is therefore `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` without a model name (the control plane does not know which model wrote the change). DESIGN. Config key `git.commit_trailer` (`control-plane/agents/config.yaml`, documented there; the shipped file carries the default line): a scalar or a block list of `Key: value` lines; absent or empty = the default; `off` = none (alone); the standard line written out counts as the default. `core/committrailer.mjs` validates every line: `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,39}: [^\x00-\x20\x7f"`$\\][^\x00-\x1f\x7f"`$\\]*$` (the characters proofline keeps out of every commit line), at most 200 bytes, at most 5 lines, no duplicate, no trailing blank, valid UTF-8, no format or line-separating code point (the NEL, the U+2028 and U+2029 separators, the bidirectional overrides, zero-width characters), and the keys `Signed-off-by`, `Reviewed-by`, `Acked-by`, `Tested-by` and `Approved-by` are REFUSED whatever the value (they certify what a person did or decided: a sign-off is a person's statement and an approval is invariant 3; a project that needs a DCO sign-off uses its own tooling). A refused configuration stops `deliver-plan` before any file is written, naming the key and the line number, never the whole file; `config-check` applies the same rules. `deliver-plan` composes `COMMIT_MSG` = the approved one line, a blank line, the trailer lines; the summary adds `trailers: default|config|off (N lines ...)` and a block `commit message, exactly as committed:` that shows every line (`  | ` prefixed, so no trailer text can pass for a summary field); `message_sha256` is the hash of the whole file and the approval hash covers the summary, so the user's `approve delivery` binds the trailer; the ledger records `commit-trailer source=... lines=N message_sha256=... trailer=...`. TAMPER CHECK: every step already compared `COMMIT_MSG` with `message_sha256`; now a step after the commit also compares the WHOLE message of the commit (`%B`, git's whitespace cleanup ignored) with `COMMIT_MSG` (`commitMessageIsApproved`, in `deliver-step` and `ciChainOk`), where before only the subject was compared: a trailer changed, added or dropped by a hand-made commit stops the chain. A trailer in `--message` is still refused (a newline, and now any control character, so `\r` cannot hide a second line); the lead never edits `COMMIT_MSG`. The CI-fix commits keep their own printed one-line message (this decision is about the delivery commit). WHO MAY CHANGE IT: `.agents/config.yaml` is a protected control file of the lead (the pretool hook refuses its edits, `nr_path_ok`, A169; during a run the lead writes no product or control file, D2); a worker can edit it only when the frozen plan scope names it, and then it is a configuration change that the REVIEW `config` focus and the SECURITY gate judge (invariant 2); and `deliver-plan` reads the key from the MAIN working tree's config (`ctx.sharedMain()`), not from the run worktree's tracked copy, so a task branch cannot steer the text at all. What is left is the user (or an agent of the same account with file access, the A218 accepted limit), and whatever it writes is bounded by the validation above and shown whole in the summary before the approval. REJECTED: reading the harness attribution setting (`~/.claude/settings.json` `attribution`, `includeCoAuthoredBy`, the project settings) for the default: the commit would depend on files outside the project, a Codex lead has none, and repository text could steer a setting an agent can read; the documented standard line is the default and the user changes it in config. A user-level attribution setting therefore does not change a delivery commit (the test sets one in a home folder and shows the config decides). DOCS: `SKILL.md` rule 8, `DELIVERY.md` section 5, `GIT.md`, `docs/concepts/workflow.md`, the `deliver-step` hints. The `role.lead.skill` budget line is 45450 (45434 measured; the pull request description carries the `Context-budget-change:` line). TESTS (Node): `tests/core/committrailer.test.mjs` (composition, default, off, override, the refusals incl. newline, NUL, a long line, a bad key, `Signed-off-by`, hidden characters, count, duplicates; `config-check`), `tests/core/run6-plan.test.mjs` (the whole chain with the default trailer: summary, hash, ledger, real commit and push; a changed, added or dropped trailer in the commit and in `COMMIT_MSG` stops the chain; off and override; a refused configuration or message writes nothing; an attribution setting in the home folder changes nothing), `tests/core/run6-merged.test.mjs` (a run worktree reads the main tree's config). KNOWN LIMIT: the whole-message check (`commitMessageIsApproved`, in `deliver-step` and `ciChainOk`) stops the chain at the step after the commit when a project's `commit-msg` or `prepare-commit-msg` hook rewrites the message (a Gerrit Change-Id, a DCO sign-off): the commit then differs from `COMMIT_MSG` and the refusal reads "the message of the delivery commit is not the approved COMMIT_MSG (the whole message counts, trailers included; commit with git commit -F, never by hand)". `git.commit_trailer: off` does NOT lift this: the check compares the commit with the approved file whatever the trailer says, so a hook that rewrites anyway still stops the chain. The real remedies are to change the hook so that the message stays byte-identical to `COMMIT_MSG` (for example to skip the delivery commit), or to accept the stop; the lead never edits the commit, `COMMIT_MSG` or the hook to get past it. Tested (`run6-plan.test.mjs`, a commit-msg hook that appends a Change-Id, with the default trailer and with `off`, the exact refusal). UPGRADE: a delivery planned before this change (its `COMMIT_MSG` and summary have no trailer) is not re-planned by the upgrade; `deliver-step` checks the existing file against its own `message_sha256`, so the commit step is not refused and `git commit -F` records that exact message without a trailer (tested: the config says `off` at the plan and the default afterwards). Only a new `deliver-plan` adds the trailer. Not tested: a trailer through the CI-fix commit (unchanged).
- **A225. Night mode and the run worktrees move to the Node core; the leftover worktree of an interrupted delivery is found by `doctor`; the refusal at `start` inside a batch names the task's own worktree (issue #172, package 172-C; Part of #172, which stays open for 172-D).** A210 migration, no redesign. Moved to `core/batch.mjs`, `core/batchplan.mjs` and `core/worktree.mjs` (handlers registered in `core/commands/moved.mjs`): `batch-plan`, `batch-cover`, `batch-next`, `batch-status`, `batch-answer`, `batch-answers`, `batch-awake`, `batch-park` and `worktree-add`, `worktree-path`, `worktree-remove`, plus the preparation of a run worktree. Deleted in the same change (no bridge, no fallback): `scripts/batch.sh` (694 lines), `scripts/worktree-prep.sh` (114), `scripts/batch-test.sh` (1080), their `agent.sh` arms and functions (`batch_plan`, `batch_record`, `batch_cover`, `batch_check`, the `worktree_*` and `rw_*` functions except `rw_shared`, which `safe_state_file` still reads), the `worktree-root` and `batch-check` shell arms, the preamble names, the shell lock rule's batch names and the worktree redirect exceptions (the core dispatcher excludes `worktree-add|path|remove` and `batch-*` from the redirect into a task's worktree, as the shell did). `core/next.mjs` no longer hands a batch member back to the shell: `batch_member`, `batch_continue_note` and the DONE-state line "agent.sh batch-next (the delivery of <ID> is covered by the batch approval ...)" are native. `build-record.sh` copies the dependency folders of its throwaway export with `proofline-core.mjs cli worktree-deps` (the former `worktree-prep.sh --deps`). `cleanup` of a run whose worktree was left behind calls `worktreeRemove` in process (it started a shell child before). Behaviour and file formats are unchanged (SUMMARY.md, order.tsv, state.tsv, merged.tsv, ci.tsv, answers.tsv, lint.tsv, paths.tsv, accept.tsv, owner, awake, awake.pid; the approvals `batch-cover` writes); the batch approval, the answers and the parks keep requiring the user's message and the existing gates (invariants 3, 5, 6; `sh tests/invariants/invariants-test.sh` passes). The texts the lead and the user read were recorded ONCE from the old shell code on deterministic fixtures (`tests/core/golden/batch/*.txt`, `tests/core/batch-golden.test.mjs`; masked: nonce, batch id, times, folder, pid) and the Node code reproduces them byte for byte except the one deliberate difference below; every scenario of `batch-test.sh` that proves behaviour is a Node test (`batch-plan`, `batch-state`, `batch-cover`, `batch-answers`, `worktree` test files; `tests/legacy-port-map.tsv` rows `batch-test` and `worktree-prep`); the one scenario part that went with its script is `batch.sh run|start|stop` (a script that no longer exists). Differences from the shell, each a clear benefit: (1) the morning table of `batch-status` put a merged task's pull request in the "park reason" column and the raw epoch in the "pending question" column (the shell's `read` collapsed the empty tab-separated fields); it now shows PR, merge time and dashes as the header says. (2) An answer "Q1 option b" / "Q1: answer a" is read on every platform (the sed alternation that strips the word was GNU-only, so on macOS it was never an answer). (3) `batch-park` with a missing argument prints `usage: agent.sh batch-park <ID> <reason>|--clear` instead of the shell's `line N: 3: usage` text. (4) Local-file copying of a worktree no longer needs `ecosystems.sh`; the ecosystem data is read from `ecosystems.tsv` directly (the prune list falls back to `.git .agents` as before). (5) Dependency folders are cloned with the file system's copy-on-write where it has one (`fs.cpSync`), no `cp` process. (6a) `batch-cover` with a missing argument exits 1 with `usage: agent.sh batch-cover <ID> <plan|delivery|mutation_budget|rationale:PATTERN>` (the shell printed its own `line N: 2: usage` text; same status). (6b) The core dispatcher no longer redirects `batch-ci` and `batch-check` into a task's worktree: the shell excluded `start`, `worktree-add|path|remove` and every `batch-*` command from that redirect (agent.sh, A169), but the Node entry of 0.0.56 excluded only `start`, so `batch-ci <ID>` and `batch-check` typed in the main tree for a task whose run lived in a worktree ran there and failed (`worktree-add` and friends were still shell). The entry now excludes `worktree-add|path|remove` and `batch-*`, as the shell did. (6c) Security review: `doctor` takes the task id of a leftover from a worktree FOLDER name, which a task could have chosen; it proposes a command only for a name `worktree-remove` itself accepts (letters, digits, `_`, `-`; first character not `-`), shell-quotes the id anyway, reads `git worktree list -z` (a name may hold a newline) and prints the folder as `.agents/local/worktrees/<id>`, never the absolute path (`x;touch${IFS}PWNED;#`, `$(id)`, a quote, a space, a newline, a leading dash and non-ASCII names are skipped; tests with hostile names). (6) The session process of `batch-next`'s one-session guard is read from `/proc` on Linux and one `ps` table elsewhere (the shell started up to 24 `ps` and `sed`). Process count (PATH shim, `sh agent.sh <command>` counted as one, median of 3, `tests/bench/batch-procs.mjs`, before = 0.0.56 shell): batch-next 112 -> 3 (sh, node, one `ps` on macOS; 2 on Linux), batch-next --tsv 78 -> 2, batch-status 52 -> 5 (`friction.sh show` stays shell until its package), batch-answers 9 -> 2; budgets in `tests/bench/exec-budgets.tsv` (rows `batch-*`: max = measured + max(2, 25 percent); max output bytes = the measured bytes), `tests/bench/batch-budgets.test.mjs` runs in CI. The issue's "batch-next at most 1" counts the Node engine alone: the launcher `sh agent.sh` and its `exec node` are 2 of the 3; DECISION PENDING (maintainer): count the launcher or not, and whether the macOS `ps` is acceptable. Two additions from the acceptance list: (a) `proofline doctor` WARNs, per worktree, "the worktree of <ID> is a leftover: its run is DONE and <why>, but <folder> is still present" and PROPOSES `sh .agents/scripts/agent.sh worktree-remove <ID> --force` (the run records are archived first); it never removes anything. A worktree counts when its run's handoff is DONE and the merge is on record: a `merged.tsv` row, a consumed cleanup approval of the run (the process died after it, A215), or the delivered commit (the `head:` of the delivery summary) reachable from the local canonical branch; a DONE run with none of these is a delivery in progress and is not reported (`core/leftover.mjs`, `proofline-core.mjs cli leftover-worktrees`, `doctor_worktrees` in `bin/lib/doctor.sh`). (b) The refusal at `core/runstart.mjs` ("another open run exists in this worktree") adds, only when the task belongs to the approved batch, "<ID> belongs to the approved batch: run this command from the task's own worktree, .agents/local/worktrees/<ID> (agent.sh worktree-add <ID> makes it; agent.sh batch-next names it), not from this folder." (a hint; no behaviour change; the intermittent smoke failure of #172 came from `start` run in the main tree while another run was open there). Rejected: a doctor action that removes the leftover (the user runs the command; a DONE run may be waiting for a merge nobody proved); counting a DONE run as a leftover without merge evidence; keeping `batch.sh` as a launcher (A210); porting the shell test line by line (A210: the scenarios are Node tests and the recorded texts are the specification); a `ps`-free session guard on macOS (no other way to read the parent chain there). Not-tested: the real `caffeinate` and `systemd-inhibit` (fakes record their arguments), the real `claude` session ancestry (`PROOFLINE_SESSION_PID` under `PROOFLINE_TEST=1` stands in), a platform tool other than the fake `gh`; the real-session smoke steps a200 and a202 run before the release. USER DECISION (2026-11-07): the batch-next target of the issue is 2 processes, the launcher `sh` and `node`; the macOS `ps` that reads the one-session guard's process is counted separately (Linux reads `/proc`, so it measures 2, macOS 3). The measurement and the rows of `tests/bench/batch-budgets.tsv` are unchanged (margin kept); `tests/bench/batch-budgets.test.mjs` now fails when batch-next starts more than 2 processes besides a `ps` (`batch-procs.mjs` returns the per-program counts), and the header of the tsv states the target.
- **A226. Node migration, stage 7, package 172-D: the dispatcher and the execution decision run in Node (patch; #172; follows A210, A222, A171, A199, A200, A203, A224).** Moved: `scripts/dispatch.sh` (620 lines, 616 of them deleted: the launcher keeps 6) -> `core/dispatcher.mjs` (the flow, the watchdog, failover, network retry, the window bracket, the resume notes), `core/dispatchtext.mjs` (the pure text rules: failure classes, token totals, claude's result, the `--agents` JSON, the template quoting), `core/gitstate.mjs` (`.git/config` and HEAD as one string), `proc.startLeader` (the child as the leader of its own process group), run as `proofline-core.mjs dispatch <ID> <role> ...`; `dispatch.sh` is a launcher of one line (`exec node "$(dirname "$0")/proofline-core.mjs" dispatch "$@"`) until stage 9. `agent.sh decide`, `ledger-note` and `metrics-dispatch` -> `core/decide.mjs` (their arms and functions, and the helpers only they used, `explorer_slot_check`, `ui_surface_signal`, `role_results_count`, `latest_decision`, `metrics_json`, `diff_stats`, are deleted from `agent.sh`; the three join the fixture prologue of `test-lib.sh`). Deleted in the same change (A210, no bridge): 616 lines of `dispatch.sh`, `dispatch-test.sh` (412) and 200 lines of `agent.sh`: 1,228 lines of sh. WHY `decide` moved: it was 123 of the 251 processes of a dispatch (172-B table) and the dispatcher calls it, `window-open`, `window-close`, `fingerprint`, `ledger-note`, `metrics-dispatch`, `ask` and `run-language` IN PROCESS now (`run()` with an io the dispatcher built); only `build-record` (a reviewer's or verifier's first dispatch on a tree) is still started as shell. PERFORMANCE (fake runtime, PATH shim, median of 3, the same file `tests/bench/dispatch-procs.mjs` run on 0.0.57 and here; the fake restores the real PATH, so only the dispatcher's own processes count): `decide --dry` as a command 123 -> 4 (the launcher, node and two git calls; in the dispatcher it is the two git calls), a codex implementer dispatch 251 -> 8 (the launcher's `sh`, `dirname`, `node`, the worker's guardian (a second `node`), four git calls), a claude reviewer dispatch 348 -> 16 (8 git calls, 3 sh and 2 awk of `build-record.sh`, the guardian); wall time 1.3 s -> 0.13 s, 2.7 s -> 0.24 s, 3.9 s -> 0.38 s. The issue's estimate was 3 for `decide` (4 here: the changed paths need `git diff` and `git status`; merging them would change `taskChangedPaths`, shared by the fingerprint and the tier, so it stays) and 10 for the dispatcher's own overhead (met: 8, the guardian included). Budgets: the new file `tests/bench/dispatch-budgets.tsv` (decide-dry 6, implementer 10, reviewer 20) with `tests/bench/dispatch-budgets.test.mjs` and its CI step; the `decide-dry` row left `exec-budgets.tsv` (it measured the shell `decide`). WATCHDOG (issue #172): the runtime runs in a process group of its own, led by a GUARDIAN (`core/guardian.mjs`, `proc.runGuardian`: a small node process that starts the real worker in that group with the same descriptors, working folder and environment, ignores HUP, INT and TERM itself, ends with the worker's status, and every 200 ms checks that the dispatcher is still its parent); at the timeout the group gets TERM, and what is still there after the grace (5 s) gets KILL (a grandchild that ignores TERM included); a runtime that ends by itself leaves its group alone; on a stop the descendants found by one `ps` listing (a grandchild that started a session of its own is not in the group) get the signal and the KILL too, as the old `ps` walk did; on Windows the tree is stopped with `taskkill /T` (`/F` at the grace; not exercised by CI, which runs Linux and macOS). The grace and the shortest step time are options of `startDispatch()` (`graceMs`, `minTimeoutSeconds`), not environment values: `PROOFLINE_DISPATCH_MIN_TIMEOUT` and `PROOFLINE_DISPATCH_NET_BACKOFF` are GONE (the backoff is `dispatch.network_backoff_seconds`, tests set it). THE NONCE (A171): the dispatcher no longer writes a nonce file; it holds a capability the command line cannot make (an io object registered in a module-private WeakSet by `dispatcherIo()`), so `decide` accepts a recording call from it on every platform. The `decide` command keeps the rule for any other process: `PROOFLINE_DISPATCH` names `.agents/local/dispatch/nonce-<hex>` (16 or more hex digits) whose pid is alive and an ancestor of the caller (Linux `/proc/<pid>/stat`, macOS and the BSDs `ps -o ppid=`, at most 12 hops, never pid 1), and the file is removed on acceptance except for `--dry` and `--agent-path`; on Windows no ancestor can be proven, so it fails closed. The sweep of nonce files older than a minute is gone with the writer. THE CODEX PROFILE (A199, A203 item 1) and the `claude -p` argument list, the prompt and the variables of the runtime are BYTE-IDENTICAL to 0.0.57: `tests/core/golden/dispatch/cases.json` was recorded from the OLD `dispatch.sh` (`tests/core/golden/dispatch-record.mjs`, 15 cases and the profile of a main tree and of a worktree run) and `tests/core/dispatch-golden.test.mjs` holds the Node dispatcher to it. Behaviour, exit codes (0/1/2/5/6/124) and file formats are otherwise unchanged. DIFFERENCES, every one: (1) the runtime's own process group and a stop that reaches the whole group and the descendants of a `ps` walk (before: the child pid and the walk, KILL scheduled in a background subshell that the dispatcher did not wait for); the guardian is one more node process per dispatch (counted above); a worker started in the dispatcher's own group used to die with it when the caller killed that group with SIGKILL (the lead's own tool timeout, A224), and in its own group it would have survived: the guardian sees the dispatcher gone within about 200 ms and kills the worker's group and every grandchild in it (tested with a real `kill -9` of the dispatcher's group); the worker has no controlling terminal any more (it is a session of its own), so Ctrl-C reaches it only through the forwarding of INT; known gaps: a grandchild that started a session of its own survives a SIGKILL of the dispatcher (the walk runs on a stop only), the guardian killed alone leaves its worker, and Windows has no guardian (`taskkill /T` on a stop only); (2) a dispatch stopped by HUP, INT or TERM forwards THAT signal to the worker's group, WAITS for the worker (grace, then KILL), ledgers `dispatch interrupted signal=<SIG> role=... runtime=... attempt=N`, writes `dispatch/RESUME-<role>[-focus].md` (`interrupted_at: ... (<SIG> to the dispatch after attempt N, runtime R: stopped from outside; no timeout)`, which the next dispatch of the step carries in its prompt) and exits 143 (as before; the metrics result stays `failed`); before it ledgered nothing and left no note; a signal during a network-retry wait ends the wait; (3) the `--agents` JSON escapes every control character (the awk program escaped backslash, quote, tab and CR only and wrote the others raw, which is invalid JSON); (4) `.git/config` and HEAD are compared from the git folder's files (config bytes by sha1 instead of `cksum`, the chain of symbolic refs HEAD follows (a branch file holding `ref: refs/heads/other` included, at most 8 hops, cycle-safe) and the commit at its end, through the loose files and `packed-refs`), with git itself for the reftable format: no git process in the normal case; a cycle, too many hops or a ref file that is no commit keep their raw bytes in the state, so the check fails closed (any change of them is a change of the state); (5) the usage line names `dispatch.sh`; the check "agent.sh not found next to dispatch.sh" is gone (nothing here runs `agent.sh` except `build-record`); (6) `decide`'s `${2:?usage}` shell message is the core's usual "a mandatory argument is missing or empty" (status 1, was a shell error text with status 2); (7) `ui_surface_signal` did not read `design/ui.json` in 0.0.57 either (its `sed` removed the whole match, so the branch printed an empty line and never matched); the port reads the `--ui-mode` flag and the `visitor_mode:` line of PLAN.md `## UI` and nothing else, as the shell effectively did; making `design/ui.json` count (A170 says it does) changes which model an implementer gets, so it is a separate decision (observation, not fixed here). A dispatcher started from a task worktree runs that worktree's own `proofline-core.mjs` (the launcher is one `exec` line, as stage 15 requires), as `dispatch.sh` in a worktree always ran its own file; the decisions it records are the same code. THE KILLED-DISPATCH CASE (A224, 'kararını bekliyor', user decision still open): with the signal path testable, the question was whether a dispatch killed from outside should close the implementer's write window as the timeout (124) path does. What the 124 path does today: after the worker is stopped by the dispatcher's OWN watchdog, `window-close <ID> <before> 124 implementer` attests everything the tree changed in the window (`WINDOW-<n>.yaml`, `exit_status: "124"`), then the resume note and exit 124; that is the user's configured limit, accepted behaviour. A signal comes from outside: whoever sends it chooses WHEN the window is closed and so which half-finished tree is attributed to the implementer (A224's 'against': a parent killing at a chosen moment), `tree-accept` exists for exactly a tree nobody attested, and no user message has accepted that a signal does what a timeout does. So the SAFEST behaviour is implemented: the dispatcher forwards the signal, waits for the worker, ledgers and notes the interruption (above), and does NOT close the window; the edits stay unattested, the next `D` is refused with `window-open refused` and the A224 recovery (`tree-inspect`, ONE question, keep with `tree-accept` or discard) applies unchanged, and the RESUME note is there for the dispatch that follows the answer. Nothing is attested that the user has not accepted, `tree-accept` and invariants 3 to 6 are untouched. DECISION WAS OPEN until 2026-11-07 (it is decided and implemented in the USER DECISION (2026-11-07) paragraph at the end of this entry; at the time: kararını bekliyor, a user decision, not implemented): should a dispatch stopped by HUP, INT or TERM close the implementer's window itself (after the worker has exited, with the status 128 plus the signal number), as the timeout path does? The code for it exists behind the option `closeWindowOnSignal` of `startDispatch()` (default false, covered by a test that shows the window recorded with `exit_status: "143"`); adopting the decision is changing that default and the guidance of A224 (`DISPATCH.md`, `FAILOVER.md`, `window-open refused` text). For: no stuck run after a tool timeout, no user question; against: the signal's sender picks the instant (see above), invariants 4 and 5 depend on window records. Alternatives: (1) keep as shipped here (forward, wait, ledger, note, window open, one question); (2) close the window after the worker exited (the option); (3) refuse to start a worker dispatch from a foreground process group (not detectable reliably). TESTS (Node, `tests/core`): `dispatch.test.mjs` (the scenarios of `dispatch-test.sh`: window bracket, permission mode and hook wiring, no spawn tool, the designer's window, `.git/config`/HEAD/tree checks, failover ask/off/floor, network retry, resubmit, metrics, parallel claims, marker, time limit, class limit, scale, explorer notes; `tests/legacy-port-map.tsv` rows), `dispatch-watchdog.test.mjs` (a runtime that ignores TERM is killed after the grace, one that hangs, one that exits early, one that spawns grandchildren (one ignoring TERM; none survives), the runtime leads its own group, HUP/INT/TERM forwarded and waited for, a stopped dispatch's window stays open, the option, a signal in a retry wait, a stopped failover worker, a grandchild of a session of its own, a real `kill -9` of the dispatcher's whole group (the worker, a grandchild and one that ignores TERM are gone within seconds), and the launcher as a process with a real TERM), `dispatch-golden.test.mjs`, `dispatch-text.test.mjs` (pure rules, `cksum` against the system's), `decide.test.mjs` (who may record, the nonce rules, the Agent path, signals, explorer slots, `ledger-note`, `metrics-dispatch`), `gitstate.test.mjs`; `gates-test.sh` `sc_decide` and the other shell suites keep running against the Node commands through the fixture prologue. Not tested: the Windows `taskkill /T` path (no Windows leg runs the dispatcher). `tests/real-session/codex-sandbox.sh` copies `core4a` into a worktree fixture and the fixture's three-line core stub awaits `main()` (it returns a promise for `dispatch`). Rejected: a second Node process per worktree run that re-executes the project's core (the launcher form of stage 15 is one `exec` line; the trust level is that of 0.0.57); keeping `PROOFLINE_DISPATCH_MIN_TIMEOUT` for the test suite (an environment seam in a production path); merging `git diff` and `git status` in `decide` to reach 3 processes (changes a shared rule). SMOKE FIX (same package, `tests/real-session/smoke.sh`, shell; found by the default smoke run on the rebased branch): the row 'hermetic batch: a Codex implementer in a worktree, submit included' reported 'no Codex dispatch seen' and the diagnosis showed it had been a FALSE POSITIVE on main. (1) `codex_config_commit` committed `implementer: codex` onto the CURRENT HEAD, which after T-1's delivery was the task branch `proofline/T-1-...`, not main; the T-2 and T-3 run worktrees branch from main, never got the Codex config and their implementers ran on Claude (`dispatch: T-2 implementer runtime=claude`). It first checked main out, which the default run refused: the kept fixture of the next default run had the task branch checked out with a dirty working tree (the status blocks of `T-2.md`, `T-3.md` and `done/T-1.md`, files that differ on main), so the lead's cleanup of T-1 never returned to main, the checkout failed, the done-command of the `-merged` drive never returned 0 and the config never reached the origin's main. It now commits the config in a clone of the origin of its own and pushes it to the origin's main, whatever the project is in, then fast-forwards the project's `main` ref without a checkout (`fetch origin main:main`, or `merge --ff-only` when main is checked out); it is idempotent and non-zero when the origin's main lacks the config afterwards. The `-merged` drive now ends when the project is back on main (`p_closed_t1`, or at once without Codex), and in every mode `codex_config_commit` runs once more after it and before the batch is planned, with a setup row that FAILS when the config did not reach the origin's main. (2) The check was `grep -rqs 'implementer-codex\|implementer.*codex' "$P/.agents/local" <batch transcript>`, a text match that also hits `roles.conf` and the `*-test.sh` files every run worktree carries (`implementer ... codex`); it passed only while the worktrees of a finished batch were still on disk, and 172-C removes them after the merge. It is now `codex_dispatch_seen`: a dispatch line `implementer runtime=codex` in the transcript, or an implementer record with runtime codex in the shared `metrics/records.jsonl`, or a `dispatch/*-implementer-codex.*` file in a run folder (the lock-failure part is unchanged). `tests/ci/smoke-fixture-test.sh` holds both: on a claude-only transcript with a worktree `roles.conf` that says 'implementer ... codex' the old grep passes and `codex_dispatch_seen` fails; each real signal passes; `codex_config_commit` puts the config on main and the origin's main from a task branch and is idempotent. `tests/real-session/codex-sandbox.sh` (real Codex sandbox, no model) passes with the launcher and the guardian. USER DECISION (2026-11-07): the open question is answered YES: a dispatch killed from outside closes the implementer's write window (the safe side). SIGNAL PATH (HUP, INT, TERM): the dispatcher forwards the signal, WAITS until the worker's group has exited (or was killed after the grace), ledgers `dispatch interrupted`, writes the RESUME note, THEN runs `window-close <ID> <before> <128+signal> implementer` (129, 130, 143), says so on stderr and exits 143; only a window this dispatcher opened and has not closed is closed (`windowOpen` is tracked, so a stop during a network-retry wait, after the attempt's window closed, closes nothing twice); if the close fails the old recovery text (`tree-inspect`, ONE question) is printed. The option `closeWindowOnSignal` is deleted (no test needs it). SIGKILL OF THE DISPATCHER'S GROUP (the lead's tool timeout): the dispatcher cannot run code. The guardian (`core/guardian.mjs`, `proc.runGuardian`) received an orphan spec from the dispatcher (working folder, the variables the dispatcher changed for the worker to put back or take away, the `window-close` command with status 137 and the `ledger-note` command, all run through `node proofline-core.mjs --pl-argv0 <agent.sh>`, never `sh` of a worktree's scripts; no secret travels in it, only the differences between the worker's and the dispatcher's environment); when it finds the dispatcher gone it starts a CLOSER (`node guardian.mjs --closer <pgid> <spec>`, a detached process of its own session that the group kill does not reach) and then kills the group. The closer waits until no live process is left in the group (a zombie does not count; `ps` unreadable counts as alive), kills the group again after 10 s and waits 3 s more; only then it runs `window-close` once and ledgers `dispatch killed from outside role=... the dispatcher got SIGKILL (no handler ran); the worker group is dead and the write window was closed by the guardian`; if the group will not die the window is NOT closed (a note says so; the A224 recovery applies). A dispatch without a window (every role but the implementer and the designer at IMPLEMENTING) gets no spec, so the guardian starts no closer; a guardian that exited with its worker never does. WHAT CLOSING MEANS (read in `window-close`, `verifyMutationOwnership`, A124, A171, A224): a `WINDOW-<n>.yaml` (`role: implementer`, `before_sha256`, `after_sha256`, `exit_status`) ATTRIBUTES the tree change of the window to the implementer so that the chain of windows has no gap (an edit outside every window is an `unattributed mutation` and the next window-open refuses); it records no acceptance by the user and passes no gate. Everything that judges the content still applies to those edits: `handoff IMPLEMENTED` runs the scope check (a path outside the frozen scope is refused) and the worker-evidence (RED/GREEN) checks, the REVIEW, QA, VERIFY and SECURITY gates bind the content fingerprint of the final tree, and a user's `tree-accept` (role `user`, bound in the ledger) is still the only way to accept a tree nobody attributed. The close happens only after the group is dead, so nothing can still write, which also answers the objection of this entry (the close in a trap while the worker holds files open); the remaining objection (the signal's sender picks the instant) changes only which half-finished edit is attributed to the implementer, never who may write: the worker is confined to its scope by the hook and the content is judged afterwards. REMAINING GAPS: the guardian killed too (an out-of-memory kill of it: nobody closes the window and the `tree-inspect` recovery stays), the dispatcher killed after its worker exited and before it closed the window (the guardian is gone with the worker, so no closer exists; the same recovery), a grandchild that started a session of its own (it can outlive the group kill and write after the close, as before), no RESUME note after a SIGKILL (the ledger note and the log are there), and Windows (no guardian). TESTS (Node, `tests/core/dispatch-watchdog.test.mjs`): HUP, INT and TERM with a fake implementer: the worker is gone, `WINDOW-1.yaml` has `exit_status` 129, 130, 143, the edit stays, the ledger and RESUME are written, the next dispatch is not refused and records `WINDOW-2`; a real `kill -9` of the dispatch's group (through the launcher) with four fake workers (a grandchild, one that ignores TERM, a hanging one, one with a grandchild that keeps writing): every process is gone when the window record appears, `exit_status` 137, the tree on disk is the recorded tree and does not change afterwards, closed exactly once, one ledger note; a reviewer dispatch killed the same way and one stopped by TERM have no window; a finished step's window is not closed again; the handoff to IMPLEMENTED is still refused after a close. `tests/skills/proofline-lead.test.mjs` holds the new lead texts (`DISPATCH.md`, `FAILOVER.md`, `SKILL.md`). USER DECISION (kullanıcı kararı, 2026-11-08): the `dispatch-watchdog` timing test must stop depending on elapsed time and pass stably under load. Changed (tests only, no production code): `tests/core/dispatch-watchdog.test.mjs` no longer asserts a duration or sleeps for a window; the step limit and the grace between TERM and KILL are timers the test holds and fires itself once the event they are about is true (the worker is up with its traps set; the TERM has reached it), so the order TERM, then KILL, then 124/143/137 and no orphan is asserted, and every other wait is for a pid, a marker file or a process that has gone (the fake runtimes in `tests/core/dispatch-lib.mjs` write the markers). The same change also fixed `tests/shared/fixture-lib.sh` (a nested template directory, and the stale-lock takeover, now an atomic rename), made the `legacy-lib` recipes run with `set -e`, and corrected the `scaffold standalone yes no STANDARD manual` recipe in `run4a-records.test.mjs`.

Tests: `tests/skills/proofline-lead.test.mjs` (known good: the three texts; known bad: no text lets the lead wait for a notice after ending its turn) and `tests/lifecycle` unchanged (the `next=wait: ... in flight (pid` prefix is kept).
