THE CONTEXT BUDGET measures the same bytes: all 25 items of the repository (name, bytes, tokens) equal the numbers of the shell script before the change, the report is byte-equal, and `tests/context/budget.tsv` is unchanged except for the header comment that named the shell script. The SessionStart text no longer comes from a `sed` over the hook source: the template moved into `adapters/claude/hooks/lib/session-head.txt` (213 bytes, placeholders unexpanded, exactly the old literal), the hook fills it, and `contextsize.mjs` measures the file; a test grows the hook source by 4,000 bytes and sees no change. BEHAVIOUR IS THE SAME (arguments, output text, exit codes, file formats of PROPOSAL.tsv and the config) except: (1) a README or CI line that carries a secret (a token shape of the secret scanner, a credential in a URL, a flag named token, secret, password, api-key or credential with a value) is never a candidate command: candidates are printed by `init` and written to the config, so the Core invariant for secrets (no secret value is printed) now also covers discovery; before such a line was a candidate when it began with a known tool; (2) the trial runs and `run-timeout` kill the whole group with SIGKILL at the limit, and also when the command ends normally (a command's background children no longer outlive it) (the shell sent TERM, waited up to three seconds, then KILL), because `spawnSync` cannot wait for a grace and a leader that ignores TERM would hold the run; an expired limit is 124 whatever status the command reports; (3) `doctor` and `insights` pass `PL_HOME` to the context measurement (it was a shell variable that was never exported, so the documented fallback to the checkout for a file the project lacks never worked there); the numbers differ only for a file the project lacks; (4) the machine measurement of `doctor --scale` starts the project's real `sh .agents/scripts/agent.sh` (launcher and Node) and the reference times 500 and 250 ms (measured on the shell engine) are NOT retuned, so a machine is proposed a scale less often than before; (5) the ecosystem definition is read from `ecosystems.json` (the sh readers of `ecosystems.tsv` stay for the other shell code), and discovery needs Node: `init` says so when `node` is missing (the CLI already needed it for `next-line`); (6) files are walked with `readdir` (a symbolic link is not followed, as `find` did) and sorted in byte order; (7) the report of a trial run is written as it happens, not at the end. TESTS (Node, `tests/core`, absolute expectations, no shell engine; written with the area and run RED once, with the new modules taken away, before they were green): `discover.test.mjs` (95: the whole ecosystem table of the deleted `discover-eco-test.sh` and the discovery cases of `cli-test.sh`, the pruned folders, the sources in order, a hung tree closed whole, a leader that ignores TERM, a command that traps TERM and exits 0 reported as 124, the secret rule, the CLI forms), `commandsprop.test.mjs` (7: empty keys, nothing found, a failed trial, the one question, the user's own reply, single use, a list written as a block list, and `cfgSet` known answers), `scale.test.mjs` (7: the rounding of the scale, a machine that is not slow, a slow one (a start of `agent.sh` that sleeps), the reply and the settings files, a proposal with no valid scale, the hook limits), `contextsize.test.mjs` (14: the budget of the repository, every mapped rule, a project counts the block only, growth of each item breaks the check, an unbudgeted or unmeasured item fails, the hook is measured through its template), `tests/hook/session-head.test.mjs` (2: a missing or empty template file gives the same SessionStart message, because the text is also embedded in the hook, and the two are equal); `tests/legacy-port-map.tsv` rows for every scenario of the three deleted suites and the discovery part of `cli-test.sh`; the CI node leg `discovery` and a Node step for the budget in the invariants job (with `actions/setup-node` 22.13.0). Rejected: keeping the process-group methods (`setsid`, perl, python3) as a fallback (A210: no fallback; `detached` plus a group kill is one call on POSIX); measuring the hook by importing it (the CLI is synchronous and the import would run project code at measure time); changing the placeholders to `{skill}` (the measured size would change by 24 bytes); a TERM-then-KILL grace through `runAsync` (it would make discovery and the whole `init` path asynchronous); a committed process budget for discovery (the numbers above are the record). Not-tested: Windows (no process group, no `/bin/sh`: the trial runs are POSIX only, like the build record); a real `claude plugin list`; a trial run of a real `npm`; `doctor --scale` on a machine that is genuinely slow (a slow `agent.sh` stands in); a project whose installed hook tree is older than this change (its hook still holds the literal and has no `session-head.txt`; `doctor` then measures the checkout's template file, which is the same text).
- **A231. 0.0.65, shellcheck regression of A230 on main (Refs #173; follows A230, A210).** What: `bin/lib/doctor.sh` built its CI hint with `dc_rows=$(mktemp ...) && pl_core ... || :`, which `shellcheck` reports as SC2015; `cli-test [sc_static]` failed on main. It is an explicit `if` now (a failed `mktemp` or `discover` leaves the rows empty and does not stop `doctor`). WHY it reached main: while `tests/ci/fast-mode.txt` exists a pull request skips the legacy self-test shards, and `sc_static` lives in one of them, so a shellcheck regression in a changed shell file is seen only on main. RULE for the next packages (173-C, 173-D): before pushing, run the `sc_static` shellcheck over ALL shell files it covers (`shellcheck -s sh -x bin/proofline bin/lib/*.sh adapters/codex/install.sh tests/cli/cli-test.sh`, and `SELFTEST_ONLY=cli sh tests/selftest.sh`), not only over the changed files. Not-tested: the local shellcheck version did not report SC2015 for the old line; the CI version did.
- **A232. Node migration, stage 7, package 173-C1: `doctor`, `insights`, the config helpers and the launcher of `merge` run in Node (patch, 0.0.66; Part of #173; follows A210, A230, A231, A202, A220).** Moved: `bin/lib/doctor.sh` (468 lines; every check and the live probes) -> `core/doctor.mjs`, `bin/lib/insights.sh` (33; argument checks, `--run` scope, the context-size and rules tail) -> `core/insightsfront.mjs` (the report itself was `core/insights.mjs` since A89), `bin/lib/config.sh` (134; `cfg_lines`, `cfg_get`, `cfg_cmds`, `cfg_val`, `cfg_set`, `cfg_merge_new`) -> `core/cfgcli.mjs` (the merge of the keys a new default config has; reading and writing were `core/config.mjs` and `core/configset.mjs`), `bin/lib/merge.sh` (13; it only started `cli merge`) -> `pl_core cli merge` in `bin/proofline`. Their entries left `tests/ci/shell-allowlist.txt` and `tests/selftest-weights.txt`; `tests/legacy-port-map.tsv` has the rows. TESTS (Node, absolute expectations, written with the area and run RED once with the new modules taken away): `doctor-fresh.test.mjs` 7, `doctor-faults.test.mjs` 11, `insights-front.test.mjs` 6, `cfgcli.test.mjs` 9 (the merge texts are what the shell `cfg_merge_new` printed for the same inputs, recorded once), `merge-front.test.mjs` 2 (`sh bin/proofline merge 7` against a fake gh: `is green at <sha> (1 checks); merging (--squash)`, a red check merges nothing, `--admin` and `--auto` refused). The doctor tests run the real `proofline init` and the real `proofline doctor` against fake `claude` and `codex` binaries, so every printed line, the exit status and the count of WARN lines are compared with the text the shell printed; on a real installed project the output of 0.0.65 and of this change is identical line by line except the approval-path milliseconds. PERFORMANCE (a PATH shim counts every external process, median of 3, the same script on the 0.0.65 tree and on this one): `proofline doctor` in an installed project with Claude and Codex 1,599 -> 315 processes (12,759 -> 4,120 ms; what is left are the live probes' git and hook runs, the approval-path measurement and the runtime version calls), `proofline insights` 8 -> 5 (337 -> 202 ms). `init` is not faster: its config calls are one Node start each now (`init --yes --runtimes claude,codex`, 16.6 s before and 18.3 s after on a loaded machine; 173-C2 ports `install.sh`). BEHAVIOUR IS THE SAME (text, exit codes, file formats) except: (1) foreign context hooks are listed also without `jq` (the old code skipped them without it) and a command that is not text still drops the whole file as the `jq` program did; (2) `hook_has` has one reader (JSON) instead of three (`jq`, `node`, `grep`): an unparsable settings file is `not wired`, also where only `grep` was left; (3) the machine load is read in process (`os.loadavg`, `availableParallelism`) instead of `/proc`, `sysctl`, `uptime` and `nproc`; `PROOFLINE_DOCTOR_LOAD` and `PROOFLINE_DOCTOR_CORES` still override; (4) the read-only lines of `doctor` (platform, CI, time limits, project rules, context size, the Codex lead model) are computed by the plugin core in process, where they started the project's `agent.sh`; what still starts the project's own engine is `config-check`, the approval-path measurement (`fingerprint`, `approve-pending`), the ecosystem check, the hook runs of the probes and the runtime versions; (5) `insights` and `doctor --commands|--apply-commands|--scale|--apply-scale` run in the plugin's core, not the project's; (6) `proofline` commands that only print an instruction (`task`, `run`, `design`, ...) read the config through Node now, so they need Node 22.13 like the rest. Rejected: keeping `config.sh` as a shell library until 173-C2 (a second copy of the parser, A210: no bridge); porting `install.sh` here (it is 173-C2); a process budget file for `doctor` (the probes start git and the hook on purpose, so the count is not a budget but a measurement, recorded above). Not-tested: a `doctor` run on Windows and on a machine without `ps` while it is overloaded (`load:` then names no executable); the `claude plugin list` branch with a real Claude Code (the fake prints nothing, so the FAIL branch is tested and the plugin-provided PASS branch is not). FIX ROUND 1 (review and security review of the pull request): (S1) the `cli` names of `bin/proofline` were reachable through `sh .agents/scripts/agent.sh cli ...`, and `cli config set` wrote any file (a `commands.*` key without its approval, A169/A200). DESIGN: agent.sh always starts the core with a leading `--pl-argv0` and a model reaches the core only through agent.sh (the Bash guard denies starting the core directly), so `main()` marks the call (`io.viaAgent`) and `runCli` refuses, with status 2, the closed list `LAUNCHER_ONLY` = `config`, `doctor`, `insights-front`, `hookspath-message`, `discover` (`--out` writes), `run-timeout` (runs any program; it was reachable since A230), `hook-timeouts-apply` (writes a settings file; reachable since A230); `doctor-commands` and `doctor-scale` keep their own approval gates, `merge` its green-check gate, the rest are read-only. (R1) every command except help, version and init stops with `proofline: node is not on PATH; proofline needs Node 22.13 or newer` and a non-zero status when `node` is not on the PATH (the config reads would otherwise be empty), and `nu_line` prints nothing without node (no second message); (R3) `doctor` without node prints `FAIL node: ...` and `doctor: 1 FAIL, 0 WARN` and exits 1; with a flag it stops like the others; (R2) a hook command that is not a string is not wired (as `jq`'s `test` failed on it); (R4) `doctor <flag> <extra>` ignores the extra argument; (R5) `cli config get` of a list key prints an empty value and a missing file is status 1, as the shell reader. Tests: `cli-agent-path`, `frontend-nonode`, and cases in `doctor-faults` and `cfgcli`. USER DECISION (kullanıcı kararı, 2026-11-08): `doctor` FAILs (not WARN or PASS) when `.claude/settings.json` is broken: not parseable as JSON, or the proofline hooks are missing, read strictly: for each of the 7 events a hook command (a string naming `proofline-hook.mjs`) under a group whose matcher is not narrower than the shipped fragment's, and `disableAllHooks: true` in the project or local settings is a FAIL too (the two strict cases come from the security finding recorded on issue #173: a matcher changed to a tool name that never fires, or `disableAllHooks`, printed PASS). Implemented in A238.

WARN <path> (named by the manifest) is not a plain path inside the project; not touched`; with a matching hash a hostile manifest could delete a file outside the project); `clean` counts and deletes under `.agents/local` with `find -P ... -delete` (an argument array, no shell; Node on win32 keeps a Dirent walk): it never follows a link in place of the folder or inside it and decides per entry as it deletes. The maintainer's three decisions of 2026-11-08: the checkout after a proven merge (A228), an existing `core.hooksPath` (A233), a broken `.claude/settings.json` (A232) (patch, 0.0.72; Part of #176, Refs #165; follows A215, A218, A221, A226).** (1) DELIVERY (`core/deliver.mjs`, `deliver-merged`): after the merge is proven, the main working tree is looked at once. On the base and clean: fast-forwarded as before. Clean and on the merged task branch (a standalone project ends there, A226): when the local base is absent or an ancestor of the fetched `refs/remotes/origin/<base>` the checkout is switched to the base (`git switch`, hooks off, `--track -c` when the local base does not exist) and `merge --ff-only` follows; the switch waits until `cleanupRun` is done, because the cleanup verifies the run on its task branch. A diverged local base is never switched to: the checkout stays on the task branch. Any other state is left as it is with ONE line: `the main working tree was left as it is: it has uncommitted changes (it is on branch X)`, `... it is on branch X, not on the merged task branch Y`, `... left on Y: local <base> has commits origin lacks (no fast-forward)`, `... git could not switch to <base>`. The old `note: the main working tree is not on a clean <base>` is gone. The names are compared as strings and handed to git as refs (`refs/heads/...`, `--is-ancestor`), the base is checked with `check-ref-format --branch` (an option-looking name is refused) and the git calls use the delivery's allowlisted environment (`cleanToolEnv`: no global or system git configuration, A215/A218) and, on the user's checkout, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `core.fsmonitor=false` (what is neutralised: hooks and a file system monitor program named in the repository config; nothing else of the repository config is, which is why a configured filter driver stops the switch, see fix round 1); "clean" means no modified or staged TRACKED file (`status --untracked-files=no`), and a colliding untracked file is refused by git itself; nothing is stashed and no file is checked out. (2) HOOKS PATH (`core/doctor.mjs` `hooksPathState`, `core/install.mjs` `doGithooksPath`): the value is read with `git config --show-scope --show-origin --get core.hooksPath`, so the scope git resolves decides (local, worktree, global, system); relative, `~/`, trailing-slash and symlinked spellings are compared by resolved path (`realish`). Unset: set locally. Same folder: no change, no message. Another folder: not overwritten (a global value is also no longer overridden by a local one, which the A233 text did), and the message names the path, the scope and file, and the remedy (`git config --local core.hooksPath .agents/githooks`); `doctor` keeps its FAIL for the inactive locks (a fact, exit status 1 as before) and adds the WARN with the path and origin. (3) SETTINGS (`doctorClaudeSettings`, `matcherCovers`, `hooksMerge`): `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` are parsed; a file that is not a JSON object is `FAIL ... is not a valid JSON object (<reason>)`, `disableAllHooks: true` is `FAIL ... in <file>`; per event the groups of both files are searched for a string command naming `proofline-hook.mjs` (none: `lacks proofline hooks for: <events>`; none under a wide enough matcher: `narrower matcher ... for: <events>`); the shipped matcher is read from `adapters/claude/settings.fragment.json`, a wildcard (absent, `""`, `*`, `.*`) needs a wildcard, a tool list needs a wildcard or a list or expression that matches every shipped name. The plugin-provided PASS still replaces the missing and narrowed FAILs (the plugin hooks are not narrowed), never the broken-file and `disableAllHooks` FAILs. `init`/`upgrade` keep refusing to rewrite an unparsable file (`not merged (invalid JSON)`); a group that names the shipped command under a narrower matcher no longer counts as the shipped one: proofline's group is added beside it and the line says so; a second run adds nothing. Rejected: switching the checkout when the tree is dirty or the branch is another (it moves the user's work); a stash (the decision says no); a merge commit or `pull` (the proof fetched the exact tip; `--ff-only` of it is the whole update); turning the hooksPath FAIL into a WARN (the locks are off, exit status stays); comparing hooksPath strings (`./.agents/githooks`, a link and an absolute path are the same folder). TESTS (RED first, run against the old code once: all 11 new cases that touch the changed code failed): `run6-merged.test.mjs` four cases (switch and fast-forward with the fresh-clone semantic of a local bare origin and no merge commit; dirty tree; another branch; diverged local base) and the three changed expectations of the old wording; `user-decisions-1108.test.mjs` ten cases (unset, local, global, same folder in five spellings, a symlink, a non-git directory and `--dry-run`; valid, unparsable, array/null/empty, missing event, narrowed, wider, disableAllHooks in both files, a command that is not text, a broken local file, hooks wired in the local file) and the changed texts of `doctor-faults` and `install-init`. Not-tested: Windows; the system-scope `core.hooksPath` (`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` in the sandbox; it takes the same path as the global one). FIX ROUND 1 (review and security review of the pull request; each case has a test that failed first): (B1) `matcherCovers`: Claude Code reads a matcher as a REGULAR EXPRESSION, so only the plain form `^[a-zA-Z0-9_|]+$` is read as a list of names; any other matcher counts only when it is a wildcard (absent, empty, `*`, `.*`) or exactly the shipped string, else it is narrower or unknown (`(?!)(|Edit|...|)` never matches yet looked like a list of every tool); a SessionStart matcher that is a plain list of all four sources (`startup|resume|clear|compact`) is as wide as the shipped group without a matcher and is not a false FAIL. A hook command counts only when its shape equals the shipped command's (`node`, the hook script under `.agents/hooks/`, its arguments, in any spelling of the directory: `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, an absolute or a relative path), so `echo "proofline-hook.mjs"` is not a wired hook. `disableAllHooks` anything but absent or `false` (the string "true", `1`, `{}`, `null`) is a FAIL. (B2) `hooksPathState` reads the value EXPANDED BY GIT (`git config --type=path -z --show-scope --show-origin --get core.hooksPath`: `~`, `~user`, `%(prefix)/`) and compares real paths; the origin `command line:` is printed as the git command line. (B3) the parked status blocks are put back whatever the cleanup does (`try`/`finally`), the switch follows only a cleanup that worked, and a failed cleanup prints the one line `left as it is: the cleanup of the run failed first`. (B4) a configured `filter.*.smudge|process|clean` driver in the repository config stops the switch (repository-controlled code that git would run for every changed file; config rather than attributes, because a driver without configuration is not run; only drivers of the local, worktree or command-line scope count, because a system or global driver (git-lfs on the CI image) is the administrator's or the user's own and the first version, which counted every scope, stopped the switch on Linux CI); `core.fsmonitor=false` is passed to the git calls on the user's checkout. (B5) a file git IGNORES in the working tree but the local base or origin's tip TRACKS is never overwritten (the switch and the fast-forward overwrite ignored files silently): no switch, one line naming the file; an unreadable file list counts as a clash. (B6) tests for a base checked out in another worktree (`could not switch to <base>`) and for a task branch named `-x` (a string, never an option). FIX ROUND 2 (re-review and the Linux CI; each case has a test that failed first): (CI) the filter-driver check counts only the local, worktree and command-line scopes (`config --show-scope`): the Linux CI image has a SYSTEM git-lfs filter configuration, which stopped every switch there; a system or global driver is the administrator's or the user's own. (R1) the filter-driver and ignored-file checks and `--no-overwrite-ignore` apply to BOTH update paths, the checkout that is already on the base and the switch. (R2) `--no-overwrite-ignore` is passed to `git switch` and `git merge --ff-only`, so git itself refuses an ignored file that the target tracks also when the shapes differ (an ignored file where the target has a directory, an ignored file below what the target has as a file, a different case on a case-insensitive file system); the path list stays only to name the file in the one line; when the fast-forward is refused after the switch the checkout goes back to the task branch. (R3) `core.fsmonitor=false` is part of every git call of `deliver-merged` on the checkout (the call wrapper, the park step, the import fetch and the shared `git()` helper the cleanup uses), and the filter-driver check runs BEFORE the park step: with a driver the checkout is not touched at all (no park, no A200 drop, no update). (R4) the hook command shape: the directory part has no white space or shell metacharacter and the script path is quoted on both ends or on neither, so a newline cannot hide a different command before the script name. (R5) a `core.hooksPath` value and origin are printed with control characters replaced by `?`. Fix round 3: (a) the filter check also counts ANY local-scope `includeIf.<condition>.path` (not only onbranch: the others cannot change between the check and the fast-forward, but one rule is safer than a judgement per condition type), because `git config` evaluates `onbranch` against the branch checked out when it runs: during the check the checkout is on the task branch, the driver is invisible, `switch` moves to the base, and the next process (`merge --ff-only`) sees it and runs the smudge driver. Global/system includes and drivers still do not block (the user's own program). (b) The cleanup keeps reading the main checkout (`diff`, `status` through the shared `git()` helper), so when a local driver exists those calls carry `-c filter.<n>.clean= -c filter.<n>.smudge= -c filter.<n>.process=` for every driver name found in local/worktree/command scope (`ctx.gitBlank`; blanking was chosen over skipping the reads because the cleanup needs them); the earlier comment that the checkout is 'not touched at all' is corrected to say what is skipped. Rejected: skipping the cleanup's tree reads (the cleanup verifies the run from them). Known limits (not fixed here; follow-up on epic #165): (1) the driver-name parse in `deliver.mjs` (~line 680) is a greedy regexp that also reads the value, so a value like `echo c >> CNT; cat #.smudge x` makes the name wrong and that driver is not blanked in the cleanup (fix: `git config --show-scope --name-only -z --get-regexp`, split on NUL, match `^(local|worktree|command)\tfilter\.(.+)\.(smudge|process|clean)$`); (2) a driver named `a=b` is not blanked by `-c filter.a=b.clean=` (fix: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n in the environment instead of `-c`); (3) `runend.mjs` ~226 (cleanupWorktree `status --porcelain --ignored`), `runend.mjs` ~183 (sbBlockOnly) and `deliver.mjs` ~555 (sbMainPark) spawn git without `ctx.gitBlank` and `core.fsmonitor=false`; (4) the filter query reads the config with `-C main` only, but the cleanup runs git in `ctx.root` (a run worktree), where an `includeIf onbranch:proofline/**` include applies. Why none stops the merge: each needs a write to the user's own repository config (same-user write, accepted limit A218), they sit in calls that existed before this change, the new switch and fast-forward path refuses to run when any local driver or includeIf exists (F1 tests), and default usage is unaffected.

- **A247. The prompt-history readers read one message at a time; the harness template cache cleanup is checked, not assumed (patch, 0.0.81; Part of #165; follows A246, A171, A172).** (1) HISTORY NEWLINE. `capture.mjs` writes each per-session history file without a trailing line end (the bytes are pinned by `tests/golden/capture/*`, the writer is NOT changed), so concatenating the files joined the end of one message to the start of the next. Two tripwire readers did exactly that: `language.mjs` (`languageScanFiles`, `languageCheck`) built one string and used its lines as the set of quotable user lines and its whitespace-squeezed text as the corpus for quoted pieces, and `freeze.mjs` `verifyIntentProvenance` searched an INTENT.md "user" answer in one squeezed string. Both now keep one entry per history file: `scanLine`/`languageHit` take the messages as `string[]` (the quotable lines are the lines of each message; a quoted piece must lie in the task text or inside ONE message, `corpora.some(inCorpus)`), and the provenance check is `messages.some((m) => m.includes(answer))`. Approvals and answers are unchanged (they use only the current event's capture, session-bound, with sha256 and time checks). Accepted limits: a message may itself hold several lines (a multi-line message keeps them, as before); the history stays a tripwire, not a boundary (A211, A217); a user who really wrote the same words in two messages is still matched per message. Evidence (RED on main, GREEN here): `tests/core/legacy-language.test.mjs` "the history files carry no line end ..." (two files with no line end: each message alone is accepted as a quote line, the two joined with and without a space, and an inline piece that crosses the boundary, are refused) and `tests/core/gates-s4.test.mjs` `sc_intent_provenance` second test (an answer split over two files, the first ending on a blank, is refused with "in no captured user prompt"; the same words in one message are accepted). Mutation checks: the two readers reverted to the concatenation (patch of `control-plane` reversed): both new tests red, every older language and provenance test stays green; the first draft of the provenance test (split without a blank at the join) did NOT go red on the old code, because the unspaced join is not a match either: the test now ends the first message on a blank. (2) TEMPLATE CACHE. The CI failure of run 42875098480 (`build-race-*` next to the final template after 8 contenders, every contender exit 0) is the one A246 round 1 already addressed (`discard` after a lost rename, the winner's template checked); A247 re-examined the root cause. Every path of `cached()` either renames the private directory to the final path or removes it, and with every contender exiting 0 the only way the old code leaves a `build-*` is a removal that returned without removing it. A246's `discard` already retried `rmSync` (5 loops with `maxRetries`) and failed loudly when the directory was still there; A247 adds an entry-by-entry fallback before it fails. Likely mechanism, unverified: that run used Node 26.13 (`lts/*`), where `fs.rmSync` is implemented over the C++ library's `remove_all`, so what it leaves behind may depend on the platform library. Not reproduced: the loser path ran 0 of 150 times red on the host (Node 24) and the docker runs on Node 22 and 26 did not finish on this machine (the container clock stalled under load); the primitives behave as documented (rename onto a non-empty directory is ENOTEMPTY, `rmSync` of the loser's tree removes it). So the fix is not tied to one proven interleaving: `discard(dir)` (now exported) tries `rmSync`, then checks, then removes entry by entry (`lstat`, links never followed, a read-only directory made writable first, `unlink`, `rmdir`), then checks again and throws if the directory is still there, so a leftover can neither pass for a clean cache nor go unnoticed; a failing build reports the build error even when its cleanup fails. The race test already asserts that the cache folder holds only the final directory after 4 and 8 contenders and a late arrival (A246); a new unit test makes the first removal a no-op (a removal that reports success and removes nothing) and a tree with a read-only file, a read-only directory, a nested `.git` and a link to a folder outside: the directory is gone, the outside file is untouched. Mutation: the entry-by-entry fallback removed: that test red (1 of 10); the `chmod` of a read-only directory removed (fix round 1: such a directory made `unlink` fail with EACCES): that test red (1 of 10). The nightly shell race (`fixture-test`, builds=2) is gone with the shell test; the Node cache keeps the documented property: at most one build per caller and ONE complete template at the final path, whoever built it (a second build is wasted work, not a wrong result), and it is asserted for 4 and 8 contenders. Said plainly: the interleaving of the CI failure was not reproduced, the claim is the mechanism-independent one above. Test durations: new language test 0.5 to 1.1 s, new provenance test 0.7 s, new cache unit test 3 to 4 ms; two runs on the same commit, same result.
- **A248. One hermetic git for every call on a checkout (patch, 0.0.82; Part of #165; hardens A238, follows A215, A218).** What: the four residual cases of the 2026-11-08 follow-up comment on #165, where a hostile LOCAL repository config (a `filter.<n>.clean|smudge|process` driver, a same-user write, accepted limit A218) could still run in deliver-merged's cleanup and status calls. (1) The driver name was read with a greedy regexp over `--get-regexp` lines that also hold the value, so a value containing `.clean ` made the name wrong; (2) `-c filter.a=b.clean=` cannot blank a driver whose name has `=`; (3) `runend` (`cleanupWorktree` status, `sbBlockOnly`) and `sbMainPark` spawned git without `ctx.gitBlank`/`core.fsmonitor=false`; (4) the query ran in the main tree only, while the cleanup runs in the run's worktree where an `includeIf onbranch:` include applies. Now: `core/hgit.mjs` holds `repoDrivers` (`git config --show-scope --name-only -z --get-regexp`, NUL split, the sub-section is what lies between the first and the last dot, only local/worktree/command scope counts, run in the main tree and in the tree the command runs in, names unioned), `hermeticEnv` (core.fsmonitor=false and every driver's clean, smudge, process set empty through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n, appended after a count the environment already has) and `hgit` (the one helper); `git.mjs`, the delivery's `g`, `sbMainPark`, `sbBlockOnly` and the cleanup status use it. The existing guarantees are kept: any local driver or `includeIf` still stops the switch, fast-forward and parking (A238), the `filters` decision is the union over both trees (it can only become true more often), system and global drivers stay the administrator's own. Rejected: keeping `-c` with a quoting scheme (git's `-c` text cannot carry `=` in a name); one query only in the worktree (the main tree's include must still count). Accepted limits: a driver reachable only through an include evaluated on a branch no tree has checked out is still caught only by the includeIf refusal, not by blanking; `sbMainPark` runs only when no driver exists, so its blanking is defence in depth (its fsmonitor and env now come from the helper). Evidence (first round): four end-to-end tests, all red with the control-plane files back at main. FIX ROUND 1 (independent security review and review of PR #239; each case has a test): (S1) `hgit` also sets `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` in the hermetic environment, so no hook (post-checkout of the parking checkout, the `.agents/config.yaml` checkout) runs; (S2) `git status` starts a git in each checked out submodule and that reads the submodule's own configuration, so `hgit status` always adds `--ignore-submodules=all`, and, because that would hide a modified submodule, a checked out submodule (`populatedGitlinks`) keeps the run's worktree (`runend`) and counts like a driver for the user's checkout (no switch, no parking, one note naming the submodule); (S3) the import of the proven tip no longer calls `git fetch` in the project (the project's `url.<x>.insteadOf`, `core.sshCommand` or an `ext::` transport could run a program): `importProvenTip` has the proof repository pack what the project lacks (`pack-objects --revs --stdout`), the project index it (`index-pack --stdin`) and `update-ref` move the tracking ref, no transport, both project calls through `hgit`; (S4) `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` on every diff and show that reads content or paths for a decision (`git.mjs`, `gates`, `diffdigest`, `knownissues`, `lifecycle`, `deliver`, `runend`), so `diff.external` and a textconv cannot replace the diff the risk scan reads; also `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` is dropped from the hermetic environment (git applies it after `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, so a caller's `core.fsmonitor` could undo the blanking), the existing count is parsed with `/^\d+$/`, and `worktree remove/prune` of the cleanup go through `hgit`. Tests: the end-to-end cases were slow (each built a delivery chain, 4.7 to 5.6 s) and are replaced by `tests/core/hgit.test.mjs` (11 unit tests on tiny repositories, 1 to 900 ms each, 1.7 s for the import test: `parseDrivers`, `repoDrivers` with `=`, dotted and crafted names and an includeIf in a worktree, `hermeticEnv` with an existing count, `hgit` with drivers, monitor, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, hook, `sbMainPark` direct, submodule, diff programs, the import with ssh and ext:: configuration); ONE end-to-end wiring test stays in `run6-merged.test.mjs` (includeIf in the run's worktree through the whole delivery). Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards, the named test goes red): no hooksPath (hermeticEnv, S1, sbMainPark); GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS kept (hermeticEnv, monitor); count ignored and count via Number() (hermeticEnv); no ignore-submodules (S2); query with values (crafted value, includeIf, planted driver); only the first tree (includeIf); diff without the flags (S4); sbMainPark on raw git (sbMainPark); import by fetch (S3); gitlinks never found (S2). Accepted limits stay: an include evaluated on a branch no tree has checked out is caught by the includeIf refusal, not by blanking; a checked out submodule is not inspected by the cleanup (the worktree is kept, the user's checkout is left alone). FIX ROUND 2 (security re-review, reproduced through deliver-merged): (B1) the calls through `git.mjs` `git()` (the cleanup's `trackedPaths`, the status lists, `addedLines`, `numstat`, `diffNames`, `runend`'s owned-path status, run BEFORE the submodule guard) still started a git in each checked out submodule and so ran its filter drivers; with `diff.submodule=diff` a child diff ran without `--no-ext-diff`. Fixed at the root, once, in `hermeticEnv` (so every `hgit` and `git()` call, whatever its first argument): `diff.ignoreSubmodules=dirty`, `status.ignoreSubmodules=dirty`, `diff.submodule=short`, `submodule.recurse=false`. `dirty` rather than `all` on purpose: a moved submodule COMMIT is still a changed path (a test pins it), only the submodule's work tree is not read. The explicit `--ignore-submodules=all` of the status calls and the `status` rewrite of `hgit` stay. Narrowed claims: this is a change of what `git()` reports (before, uncommitted content inside a checked out submodule showed the gitlink as modified in the task-path lists; it no longer does), which is the price of not running a submodule's configuration; the delivery paths keep their guard (a checked out submodule keeps the run's worktree and the user's checkout). The earlier sentence that `status` "never enters a submodule" holds for every call through the helper and `git()`, not for a git started by something else. (B2) `populatedGitlinks` decoded the NUL list as latin1, so a non-ASCII gitlink path (`süb`) was not found (the guard failed open); it now keeps the bytes (a `Buffer` path to the file system). `submodule.recurse=true` made `switch` write a submodule through its smudge driver; `submodule.recurse=false` in the environment covers it (the delivery's `switch` goes through `hgit`). (R5) `hermeticFetch` takes the folder whose `.cache` holds the proof repositories as an optional last argument (default: the account's home), and the S3 test uses its own temporary folder, so no test writes outside it. Tests (`tests/core/hgit.test.mjs`, 16 unit tests, two runs 5.6 s and 5.0 s, the same result, 0.001 to 0.85 s each): `hermeticEnv` pins all entries; B1 drivers (trackedPaths with and without a base, addedLines, numstat, diffNames, status with leading options); B1 `diff.submodule=diff`; a moved submodule commit is reported; B2 non-ASCII gitlink; B2 recursive switch. FIX ROUND 3 (a new implementer; the previous rounds each added one flag and the next review found another path, so this round changes the design; both findings were reproduced through deliver-merged): (R3-1) `submodule.<name>.ignore=none` (in the config, or in a committed or untracked `.gitmodules`) overrides `diff.ignoreSubmodules` and `status.ignoreSubmodules`, so `git()` (trackedPaths, diffNames, addedLines, numstat, the status lists, the `status --porcelain` of the delivery and of the cleanup, `diff HEAD`, stash) started `git status --porcelain=2` inside a populated submodule and ran its clean filter; `git add` (the content fingerprint) enters a submodule whatever the ignore keys say. Design: no ignore key is relied on and the two are REMOVED from `hermeticEnv`. `repoDrivers` now also visits every populated submodule of each tree it is given, recursively (depth 8, each folder once), with the same NUL split `git config --show-scope --name-only -z --get-regexp` run by `-C <submodule>` (its includes count like the others) plus `ls-files --stage -z` (index only), and returns the folders (`submodules`); the submodule drivers are blanked by name through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, which the child git inherits, together with `core.fsmonitor=false` and `core.hooksPath` (the hook and the monitor of a submodule are blanked by the same inherited entries). Discovery only reads configuration and the index, so it cannot run a filter itself. Where it runs (round 3 chose call sites, round 4 replaced that by construction, see FIX ROUND 4): `discoverBlank` (deliver.mjs) sets `ctx.gitBlank` for both trees at the start of `deliver-merged` (it also decides the user's checkout). The kept entries `diff.submodule=short` (a child DIFF in a submodule would run its `diff.external`, which is not a driver we can blank) and `submodule.recurse=false` stay and are now mutation-proven (below). (R3-2) `merge --ff-only` of the cleanup (`ffNow`) ran `gpg.program`, `gpg.ssh.program` or `gpg.x509.program` when the tip is signed (GitHub signs its merge commits) and the repository has `merge.verifySignatures=true`; the hermetic environment now sets `merge.verifySignatures=false`, `log.showSignature=false`, `commit.gpgSign=false`, `tag.gpgSign=false` and empties `gpg.program`, `gpg.openpgp.program`, `gpg.ssh.program`, `gpg.x509.program`, `gpg.ssh.defaultKeyCommand`. An empty program is a program called "" that git cannot start, so a check that is asked for explicitly (`log --show-signature`, `verify-commit`) fails closed and never starts the config's program; nothing in the control plane asks for a signature, and the signed tip is still fast-forwarded (tests, three `gpg.format`s). (R3-3) the behavioural status test is in the R3-1 tests: `trackedPaths` with an empty base (the `status --porcelain=v1 -z` path of `git()`) with a same-size content change and the unblanked control that proves the driver fires; `diff.submodule=short` is proven by its own test (below) and the claim that the old `dirty` mode was mutation-proven is withdrawn (the round 2 sentence "the entry is a second line" is the truth: it was never proven until now). (R3-4) decided on evidence: the ignore keys are gone, so `git()` sees uncommitted content inside a checked out submodule again (the gitlink is a changed path: `githooks.mjs` has a `git()` of its own and was never affected, the decisions of `runend.mjs`'s owned-path status, `deliver.mjs`'s delivery-plan `status --porcelain` and `git.mjs` `statusLists` are the ones that changed back); the destructive decisions stay guarded by `populatedGitlinks` (a checked out submodule keeps the run's worktree and the user's checkout is left alone). Tests (`tests/core/hgit.test.mjs`, 23 tests, all in one file, 0.001 to 1.1 s each): the env shape (no ignore key, the 18 entries), R3-1 with `ignore=none` in the config and in an untracked `.gitmodules` (trackedPaths with and without a base, addedLines, numstat, diffNames, status, `git()` status, `hgit diff HEAD`, `git add -A`, each after an unblanked control that proves the driver fires), `git add -A` with every ignore key set, a nested submodule, the submodule's `core.fsmonitor`, R3-2 for `openpgp`, `ssh` and `x509` (premise: the plain ff-only merge and the plain log run the program; then the hermetic merge succeeds and moves HEAD, `git()` log, an explicit `--show-signature` and `verify-commit` run nothing). Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards, the named tests go red): no recursion into submodules (the three R3-1 tests and the nested one); no `merge.verifySignatures=false` (env shape and the three R3-2 tests); no gpg program entries (env shape and the three R3-2 tests); only `gpg.program` emptied (env shape, the `ssh` and `x509` R3-2 tests); no `diff.submodule=short` (env shape and the `diff.submodule=diff` test); (`ensureBlank` of round 3 is gone: round 4 does it inside `git()`); the ignore keys put back (env shape, the config variant of R3-1 and the nested test: `dirty` hides the control's premise, which is why the ignore keys are not used). `log.showSignature=false` is caught by the env shape only: with the programs emptied it is a second line of defence that no behavioural test can tell apart. Systematic hunt of every git spawn that touches a checkout (control-plane/agents/scripts/core), and the mechanism that covers it: (a) the helper `hgit`: deliver.mjs (`g`, `importProvenTip`, `sbMainPark`), runend.mjs (`cleanupWorktree`, `sbBlockOnly`), `populatedGitlinks`: drivers of both trees and all their submodules, monitor, hooks, signature programs, submodule child diffs; (c) calls that read refs, objects or configuration only and never a work tree file (CORRECTED in round 7: the list below named `ls-files --error-unmatch` and `check-ignore`, which read the index and can start `core.fsmonitor`; see FIX ROUND 7 for the class and the guard; CORRECTED again in round 8: "never a signature" was wrong too, a raw `log` runs gpg when the repository configuration sets `log.showSignature`, and `cat-file --textconv|--filters` and `rev-parse :path` apply a filter or read the index, so FIX ROUND 8 narrows the class once more): `rev-parse`, `cat-file`, `merge-base`, `worktree list`, `config`, `diff-tree`, `symbolic-ref`, `var`, `remote` (worktree.mjs, leftover.mjs, paths.mjs, gitstate.mjs, dispatcher.mjs:387 and :609, kirules.mjs `ls-files --error-unmatch`, batch.mjs, approvals.mjs, hookcmds.mjs, friction.mjs, platform.mjs, doctor.mjs, install.mjs, proflinecli.mjs, lessons.mjs `show`, merge.mjs `gitOut`: `rev-parse`, `branch --show-current`, `symbolic-ref`; Accepted limits of the entry (all rounds): a driver reachable only through an include evaluated on a branch no tree has checked out is caught by the includeIf refusal and not by blanking; a checked out submodule is not inspected by the cleanup (the run's worktree is kept, the user's checkout is left alone); the submodule search follows a `gitdir:` redirect or a symlinked folder (git reads that configuration too) and is bounded only by depth 8, one visit per real folder and 256 folders in all (round 4); a submodule that is checked out AFTER the discovery of a context and tree (the cache is dropped by `ctx.forget('')` and `discoverBlank`, not by every write) is not blanked until then (the destructive decisions are guarded by `populatedGitlinks` at the point of use); `diff.external` and a textconv of a submodule are not blanked by name (every diff that feeds a decision passes `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv`, and `diff.submodule=short` stops the child diff); the merge proof trusts the user's file system (A218). FIX ROUND 4 (by construction; independent re-review of round 3, three findings reproduced): round 3 made the safety depend on `discoverBlank`/`ensureBlank` having run EARLIER in the same command, and with no ignore key left any `git()` or `hgit()` call before it ran a submodule's clean filter (`deliver-plan`: `deliveryCheck` before the discovery, `statusLists`; the standalone `cleanup`: `verifyHandoff`, `trackedPaths`, the status in `runend`). A command that changes the set of checked out submodules drops it with `ctx.forget('')` or `ctx.forget('git:blank')` (`discoverBlank` and `inProcessCleanup` do); `discoverBlank` stays because `deliver-merged` also needs the includes and the submodule list for the decision about the user's checkout, and `ensureBlank` and the extra calls before `deliverPlan`'s status are removed. Every entry command reaches git through one of three doors, all of which now blank by construction: (1) `git.mjs` `git()` (`runcmds` start, status, next, resume, freeze, handoff, gates and every `verify-*`, `freshness`, `delivery-check`, `report`, the fingerprint and its `git add -A`, `lifecmds` terminate and cleanup, `deliver-plan`, `deliver-step`, `deliver-merged`, `approve`, `signals`, `probes`, `knownissues`, `diffdigest`, `statusblock`, `platform`); (2) `hgit` (`deliver-merged`, its import and the cleanup of `runend`, `sbMainPark`, `sbBlockOnly`, `populatedGitlinks`); (3) calls that read refs, objects or configuration only (see (c) above). F2 (denial of service, reproduced): the search was keyed by the path string and bounded by depth only, so gitlinks that are symlinks to `.` gave B^8 visits (B=2: 1,022 visits, 19.9 s; B=3 did not finish); it now dedupes by `realpathSync`, visits at most 256 folders and 8 levels, and when a bound is hit sets `includes` (fail closed: the user's checkout is left alone) and `capped` (deliver-merged prints a note). Cost: a first version spent two spawns per tree and context and pushed `dispatch-implementer-codex` (10 to 14) and `dispatch-reviewer-claude` (20 to 22) over their budgets in `tests/bench`; `indexHasGitlinks` now reads the index file itself (versions 2 and 3, no split index; anything it does not understand asks git) and a tree whose index holds no gitlink starts NO process, so the budgets are unchanged. A repository with N populated submodules costs 2(N+1) extra spawns the first time a git call on it is made (`config`, `ls-files` for each folder visited), per context and tree. (CORRECTED in round 5: this round skipped the tree's OWN drivers when the index holds no gitlink, which left the cleanup, `deliver-plan` and the fingerprint without blanking for them; round 5 searches the tree's own drivers always, see FIX ROUND 5.) F3: the search DOES follow a `gitdir:` redirect or a symlinked folder out of the repository (git reads that configuration too); only the three bounds stop it (the earlier sentence is corrected above). F4: the new unit tests keep their repositories small and the stand-in-context variant runs once. Tests: (a) `R4` in `hgit.test.mjs`: a context with `gitBlank: []` and no discovery, `ignore=none` in the config and in an untracked `.gitmodules`, `git()` status and `add -A`, `hgit` diff and status, `trackedPaths` (with and without a base), `untrackedPaths`, `addedLines`, `numstat`, `diffNames`, after the plain-git control that proves the filter fires; a context without `once`; the cache (`blankNames` once, forgotten, merged with `gitBlank`); `F2` with three symlink-to-dot gitlinks (3 visits, not capped) and the folder bound (capped, includes). (b) two end-to-end wiring tests in `run6-merged.test.mjs`: the standalone `cleanup` of a finished run and `deliver-plan`, each in a worktree with a populated submodule and a clean-filter marker, `ignore=none` in an untracked `.gitmodules`, after the control that proves the marker fires. (c) every earlier test is kept (the premise controls of R3-1 now use plain git, because `git()` itself no longer needs the caller to discover). Mutation checks: `blankNames` returns only `ctx.gitBlank` (the four `R4` tests, the cache test, the `git add -A` test and both wiring tests go red); `git()` reads `ctx.gitBlank` only (the `R4` tests and `git add -A`); no real-path dedupe (`F2`: the capped flag turns on, since the visits would otherwise not end); no folder bound (`F2` bound); the bound not failing closed (`F2`); the index reader's padding changed from 8 to 4 bytes (the `indexHasGitlinks` test); the no-gitlink shortcut removed (no unit test goes red: it is the process budget of `tests/bench/dispatch-budgets` that does). FIX ROUND 5 (the LAST round; independent review and security verification of round 4, every finding reproduced): (S1, blocking) the tree's OWN drivers were not blanked in `deliver-step <ID> cleanup`, the standalone `cleanup`, `deliver-plan` and the fingerprint's `git add -A`: round 4 removed `discoverBlankNow`/`ensureBlank` and `blankNames` returned `[]` for a tree with no gitlink, so `ctx.gitBlank` (set only by `deliver-merged`) stayed `[]` and a local `filter.<n>.clean` ran on every file git read. Now `blankNames` ALWAYS finds the tree's own drivers (the raw `git config --show-scope --name-only -z --get-regexp` of `repoDrivers`; when `tree` is the command's root, also in `sharedMain()`, so an `includeIf onbranch:` include is judged in both trees) and adds the submodule search (`ls-files --stage`, recursion) only when `indexHasGitlinks` is not `false`. Process budget kept by a text pre-check, not by a spawn: `ownConfigMayHaveDrivers` reads `<common dir>/config` and `config.worktree` and answers false only when no `[filter` or `[include` section exists in the text, no `config.worktree` exists, `.git` is understood, and the call carries no `GIT_CONFIG_*`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` in its environment (command scope); anything else asks git. - **A249. `init` sets `core.hooksPath` only when all the code git will run is proofline's shipped code; `doctor` compares it with the shipped sha256 and runs none that differs (patch, 0.0.83; Part of #165; the item is in the 2026-11-08 comment on #173, https://github.com/furkansarikaya/proofline/issues/173#issuecomment-6716526633, tracked under the epic; follows A233, A238, A218, A211).** FINDING (independent security review of 173-C2, both points present unchanged in the shell installer of 0.0.66): (1) `init` set `core.hooksPath` to `.agents/githooks` also when a committed `.agents/githooks/pre-commit` differed from proofline's and was kept as the user's own file; in a cloned hostile repository `init --yes` followed by `git commit` then ran that committed file. (2) a hostile `.claude/settings.json` (matchers changed to a tool that never fires, or `disableAllHooks`) made `doctor` print PASS. ROUND 1 (reviews of PR #240) found that the first version trusted too little and too late: `doctor`'s probes copied the project's `.agents` (hooks and scripts) into a temp repository and RAN them as the user with the full environment, so the hostile hook ran from `doctor` itself; the trust decision looked at the working-tree bytes only, so a committed manifest row naming the hostile hash (route a) or a hostile blob behind a clean working copy (route b) passed; and the check stopped at the hook folder while the shipped hooks start the project's own `proofline-core.mjs` (R1, reproduced: a commit wrote a marker file). POSIX answers are those of `grep -E -e PATTERN` (the file holds the bytes plus one line end, so a pattern with a line end is several patterns, and with `grep -f` an empty line in the pattern file matches every line; `git grep -f -` with an empty line matches nothing, which no caller can reach because `confirmPattern` never returns an empty pattern). Node migration stage 15, package 180-A: the strict no-shell-logic check is the only mode, the launchers are pinned by template, no shell or awk is started from Node outside `core/proc.mjs`, shellcheck leaves CI, the final before/after table (patch, 0.0.85; Part of #180; follows A250, A246, A245, A218, A217, A211, A210, A207).** WHAT. (1) `tests/ci/no-shell-logic.mjs` has one mode. The ratchet (`shell-allowlist.txt`, `inline-shell-snapshot.txt`, `--base`, `--print-*`, their tests) is deleted. Rules: a shell file is only one of the four launchers and no `.awk` file exists; each launcher is BYTE-EQUAL to its section of the new `tests/ci/launcher-templates.txt` (`agent.sh` included); the three plain launchers must also pass `launcherOk` (a shebang and one `exec node` line), so a template cannot give them logic; every hook command equals a template of `hook-templates.txt`; every `run:` step is one command line; no `sh`, `bash`, `awk` or `sed` is started from Node outside `core/proc.mjs`. DECISION (the open question 1 of the issue comment 'Input for this stage from the 176-E2 reviews'): the launcher text with the A207/A245 redirect stays as it is and is pinned by template, no guard is loosened. The redirect cannot move into Node because it chooses WHICH core file runs: that choice must not be made by code a run worktree's task could have rewritten (A207). Rejected: redefining `agent.sh` as the ADR one-liner (the redirect would move into the core it is meant to select); a pattern that 'accepts the redirect' (a regex is a looser guard than equality); loosening `launcherOk` (it would let a plain launcher grow logic). Accepted limit: the template and the launcher change together in one pull request, so review and the A entry are the gate for a launcher change, as for the Core invariant tests. Process notes (round 2): CODEOWNERS names one owner, so on the owner's own pull requests the Code Owner gate is a self-review; branch protection (Code Owner review required, no direct push, no admin bypass) cannot be verified from the repository and is a process setting; the `Launcher-change:` line is read live from the pull request body when the job runs, and the `pull_request:` trigger has no `types:`, so editing the body after a push needs a re-run of the job; the line is written by the author, it is a reason on record and not an approval. (2) THE TIGHTENING (item 2 of the comment): after the redirect step `agent.sh` runs `case $(cd "$root" && pwd -P) in */.agents/local/worktrees/*) ... exit 127`, i.e. when the launcher still sits in a run worktree (main tree unconfirmed: a failing `git worktree list`, an odd path, or a deleted or rewritten untracked `.git` file) it prints `proofline: <$0> is in a run worktree and the main tree could not be confirmed ...` and exits 127; it never runs the worktree's own core and never one chosen from the caller's directory. The check is outside the `[ -f "$root/.git" ]` block on purpose: deleting the `.git` file is the attack. Tests (`tests/hook/worktree-flow.test.mjs`): a failing-git shim with a decoy core in the caller's directory and a rewritten core in the worktree: neither runs, exit 127 (extends the A250 test); a worktree whose `.git` file is deleted, and one rewritten to a bad gitdir, exit 127 with the marker unwritten; the normal redirect is unchanged (the existing tests, plus a status call from the worktree and from the main tree). Mutation: the `case` line removed turns both tests red, and the strict check red (the launcher no longer equals its template). Finding (before this package, not changed): on Windows a launcher started as `sh C:\x\agent.sh` (backslashes in `$0`) finds no `/` in `$0`, takes `.` as its folder and fails closed with 'no control-plane core beside'; the two new tests spell the path with `/`, as the shell of a user does. Accepted limit: a project that itself lives under a path with `/.agents/local/worktrees/` in it (a repository cloned inside a run worktree) fails closed with the same message; it has no redirect to make. A second accepted limit (review round 1): the worktree test is textual and case-sensitive on `pwd -P`, so a path spelled `/.AGENTS/local/worktrees/` on a case-insensitive file system, or a symlinked `.agents/local`, passes both the redirect and the exit-127 line; no normal flow produces either (a miscased MAIN path alone still fails closed through the exit-127 line). Item 3 of the comment, confirmed: the core sets what the launcher no longer exports for every child it starts (`context.mjs childEnv`: `LC_ALL=C`, `RTK_DISABLED=1`, `PROOFLINE_SHARED_ROOT`; `platform.mjs` sets the first two), and the launcher has no `set -eu` because every line of it is guarded (`||`, `[ -n ]`, `2>/dev/null`) or ends in `exit` or `exec`; `set -e` would turn the guarded `git` failure into an exit and defeat the fail-closed branch. 'Rewriting the worktree's `agent.sh` itself' (the part the comment left open): DECIDED, an accepted limit, same class as A211, A217 and A218. A launcher cannot verify itself: `sh <file>` reads the file before any check can run. What is covered: everything proofline's own code starts from a run worktree (the hook, the bridge, every `proc.run` of a script under `<main>/.agents/local/worktrees/<id>/.agents/scripts/`) is refused with status 126 unless the worktree's whole `.agents/scripts` equals the project's (`tree.mjs`, `refuseUntrustedScript`); and the committed text is pinned by this check. What remains: a person or lead typing `sh <worktree>/.agents/scripts/agent.sh` after a task rewrote that file runs the rewritten text. Why accepted: the hook guards are tripwires against honest mistakes and the boundary against a hostile agent is the runtime's permission mode and sandbox (`.out-of-scope/small-rejected-ideas.md`); and rewriting the file needs a task to get past the path guards of the hooks first. CORRECTION of the first text of this entry (review round 1): it said 'no normal flow executes the worktree copy'. The limit is accepted for the other reasons only: the same class as A211, A217 and A218, the path guards a rewrite has to pass, the 126 refusal of every script start by proofline's own code from a run worktree whose `.agents/scripts` differs from the project's, and the review gate on the committed text. Rejected: copying a vetted launcher over the worktree's before each use (a window between check and use, and a write into a tree the task owns); a hash check inside the launcher (it would be the file a task rewrites). (3) The two multi-line CI steps are one-line steps: `skill tests` (static job) is `node tests/ci/ci-steps.mjs skill-tests` (tests/skills/ when it holds test files, else the SKIPPED line, then the benchmark tests; the first failing status ends it) and the `checks` gate is `node tests/ci/ci-steps.mjs gate` with `NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}` (a failed or cancelled job, or an unreadable context, fails; the job now checks out the repository and sets up Node first). Behaviour unchanged. Tests: `tests/ci/ci-steps.test.mjs` (new; injected exec and list, no process). (4) NO SHELL OR AWK STARTED FROM NODE. The rule found real cases, all fixed: `core/signals.mjs` ran an `awk` program for a risk pattern the JS translator does not cover (now `grep -E` selects the lines, `grepTextLines` in `grepfile.mjs`, and the same JS word test decides; macOS awk could not parse `\\<` while grep does); `config-check` validated the risk patterns that have words with `awk` (now `grep -E` for all, the dialect of the signal without words); `queue.mjs` listed a folder with an `sh` `for` loop in non-C locales (now `readdirSync` sorted by `Intl.Collator`; accepted limit: names outside ASCII ids may sort differently from the C library's); `batch.mjs` held the sleep inhibitor with `sh -c` with a polling loop (now a Node watcher, `INHIBIT_WATCH`); `resultutil.mjs` re-ran recorded commands through `sh -c` plus a `command -v timeout` probe (now `runUserCommand` with the Node timer, 124 on expiry, standard error merged by a file, the process group stopped whole); `secretscan.mjs` ran the configured scanner as `/bin/sh -c 'cmd "$@"'` (now `runUserCommand` with quoted path words); `proflinecli.mjs` merged stderr with `sh -c 'exec sh "$@" 2>&1'` (now `proc.runMerged`, moved from `doctor.mjs`); `/bin/sh -c` strings of the build record, discovery and the dispatcher template go through `proc.userShellArgv`. Node starts a `.cmd`/`.bat` only through `cmd.exe /d /s /c`, which re-parses the command line (`& | ^ % " <` act again; CVE-2024-27980 is the reason Node refuses a bare spawn of a `.cmd`), and a pull-request title or branch name reaches the arguments; no escaping rule is verifiable here without a Windows host, so the safe choice is the real `.exe`. `core/wintool.mjs` (pure, the file system passed in) resolves the tool through `PATHEXT` on the `;`-separated `PATH`: only drive-absolute entries (empty, relative, UNC and rooted entries are never searched), a plain tool name (no separator, colon, metacharacter, `..`), a `.exe`/`.com`, the real path again drive-absolute and still an `.exe`/`.com`, and not inside the project, the working directory or a temporary folder (a refusal list, NOT an ACL check: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps` or `%USERPROFILE%\\bin` pass; compared case-insensitively, with `\\` and `/` alike, on the as-spelled and the `realpathSync.native` form of both sides, so an 8.3 short TEMP such as `RUNNER~1` meets a long PATH entry); the first folder that holds the tool decides, as Windows resolves it, so a shim there is reported and an `.exe` further on is not used. A shim answers `unreadable (gh is only a .cmd/.bat shim at <path>; proofline does not run a shim through cmd.exe: install the real gh.exe and put its folder on PATH ahead of the shim ...)`; for `az` (the Azure CLI ships only `az.cmd`) the text says to merge in Azure DevOps (merge: manual). `platform.mjs` `resolveTool` uses it on win32 only; POSIX resolution is unchanged. `tests/core/wintool.test.mjs` (fake file system, any host): the `.exe` path, `.cmd`/`.bat` never returned, the first folder decides, PATHEXT order and filtering, relative/empty/UNC/rooted PATH entries, shadowing also through a link, unsure cases (UNC or shim real path, throwing file system), sixteen hostile tool names (`& | ^ % " < >`, space, separators, drive colon, `..`, newline) that never reach the file system, quoted PATH entries. The line `process.kill(cpid, 0)` right after the start remains a synchronous check of a process the test just waited for, not a wait. (c) `startLeader` WIRING: `startLeader` takes `options.platform` (default `process.platform`) and `options.warn` (default stderr); on a refusal it returns `refusedLeader(reason)`, which now also writes the reason to the worker log (`stdio[2]`, the dispatcher's `logFd`), where before only stderr showed it and the run log stayed empty. `wintool.test.mjs` R2 simulates a win32 refusal and reads the log. - **A253. The Node test harness no longer grows without bound: the template cache prunes itself, `node tests/lib/clean-temp.mjs` removes what killed runs leave, and the helpers clean up on SIGINT/SIGTERM (patch, 0.0.87; Part of #165; follows A247, A246, A244, A236).** MEASURED (the maintainer's machine, one afternoon): the template cache `$TMPDIR/proofline-harness-501` was 13.4 GB in 5108 entries (kinds `sc-*`, `rcp-*`, `ctl-*`, `lcs3-*-failed-*`, `l2b-failed-*`, `build-*`) because every template is keyed by a content hash and nothing ever removed one; 1343 `proofline-*` test folders (14 GB) lay under `$TMPDIR` (killed runs, tests that did not clean up: `proofline-h-*`, `proofline-fp.*`, `proofline-approve.*`, `hf5-*`, `br-*`, `bt-fake-*`); free disk fell to 44 GB; a CI-like local run regrew about 15 GB per 3 hours; the lead cleaned by hand twice. (1) PRUNING (`tests/lib/prune.mjs`, called by `cached()` of `tests/lib/harness.mjs`): the clock and the file system are arguments (`now` in milliseconds; the harness is the only place that reads the wall clock, once per `cached()`/`copyOf()`), so the rules are tested on a fake file system at a fixed instant. An entry's last use is the mtime of its `.built` marker, touched by every `cached()` hit and every `copyOf`. Rules, in order: a folder `build-*`, an `evict-<time>-*` tombstone, or an entry without a marker older than 1 hour goes (a tombstone is as old as the time in its name, not the mtime of what it holds); an entry idle for more than 6 hours goes; when what is left is over 2 GB the least recently used go, oldest first, until it is under; NEVER an entry used within 30 minutes and never the key being asked for (so the cap is soft: a live run is worth more than the bytes). Only direct children that are real directories of this user are looked at (`lstat`; links, files and other users' folders are skipped, nothing is followed). It runs from `cached()` on the default cache only (another root, as the cache tests use, is left as built), at most once per 5 minutes per cache folder (a stamp file; a failure of the pruning never fails a test). (2) CONCURRENCY with live runs: an entry is not deleted in place: it is renamed to `evict-<time>-<pid>-<n>-<key>` (atomic; the rename moves a link as a link), the marker is read again, and when it was touched since the listing the entry is renamed back; only then is the tombstone removed (entry by entry, links never followed). A reader that is copying that very template at that instant gets an error and `copyOf` copies again (up to 3 tries) after building the template anew through the builder it remembers from `cached()`. Round 1: this verification and the rebuild apply only to a folder that has a `.built` marker or a remembered builder; any other folder (`copyOf` of a project directory, as `risk-s2` does) is copied as it is. This needed one more change found by the multi-process test: `copyOf` no longer uses `cpSync`, because node's `cpSync` runs in C++ and ABORTS the whole process (`filesystem_error` from `directory_iterator`) when the source folder disappears under it instead of throwing, which no retry can catch; `copyTree` copies with plain file system calls (modes kept; links kept as links with their target text, where `cpSync` rewrote relative targets to absolute paths into the cache; about the same time: 31 ms against 29 ms for a template of 190 files). (3) `node tests/lib/clean-temp.mjs [--dry-run] [--hours N (at least 1)] [--tmpdir DIR]`: prints each folder it removes (or would) with its size and the reason, and a total. It touches only direct children of the temp folder (and of `/tmp`, which a run without `TMPDIR` uses) whose name is on an explicit list (`PREFIXES`, round 1: mkdtemp-shaped names, a fixed prefix and exactly the six characters mkdtemp adds): `proofline-t-*` (the family of the test helpers), `proofline-h-`, `proofline-{recipe,bt-fake,bt-origin,guards,fixtures,trees}-`, the product's own scratch folders `proofline-{rerun,dm,pl,install,grep,rt,ver}-` and `proofline-{fp,approve,doctor,submit,lint}.`, and the names tests used before A253 (the `LEGACY` list: `pl-lib-`, `pl-t2s-`, `adp-`, `rv-bin-`, ...). A folder named `proofline-<anything else>` is NOT on the list (the cache folder, `proofline-e2e` and `proofline-smoke.*` kept on purpose, a person's `proofline-review-9`). A folder that holds a `.git` (file or folder) is skipped unless it is `proofline-t-`/`proofline-h-` (made only by the helpers, which build repositories in them). The folder must be a real directory of this user older than the threshold (default 2 hours, never less than 1), and a harness base whose recorded process (`.pid`) is alive stays. `--tmpdir` refuses `/`, the home folder, the checkout, an empty value and the folders directly above those. Stale `<pid>` and `batch-<pid>` folders under `tests/core/.fake-tools/` (A180; a killed run leaves them; the `ln-`/`cx-` folders of the platform tests live inside a `<pid>` folder) are pruned too (pid not alive, older than the threshold); that root is judged like the cache root (`lstat`: a link, which a branch can commit, a file or another user's folder is never entered). Round 2: the refusal of dangerous folders applies to the effective folder however it was given (`--tmpdir`, `TMPDIR`, or the defaults) and compares device and inode, so the letter case of a case-insensitive file system makes no difference. The cache folders get the pruning rules above; a cache folder that is a link or another user's is never entered. (4) CLEANUP AT EXIT: `base()` registers its removal at exit and on SIGINT/SIGTERM (`removeAtExit`: removes synchronously and sends the signal to itself again with the default action back, so the exit status is the signal's); and the helpers that left folders now use one family: `proofline-recipe-*` (recipes), `proofline-bt-fake-*` and `proofline-bt-origin-*` (batch tests), and `hf-`, `hf5-`, `hf5b-`, `br-out-`, `br-timeout-` folders of tests that never removed them are made with `tmp()` and so go with their process. (4b) ONE FAMILY FOR EVERY TEST (round 1; the independent review measured the real regrowth: `pl-lib-*` 591 folders 7.2 GB from `makeFixture()`, `pl-t2s-*` 1387 folders 6.2 GB, `pl-core-*`, `adp-*`, `rv-bin-*`, `rv-proj-*`, ...): `tests/lib/tempdir.mjs` `tempDir(prefix)` makes `proofline-t-<prefix>XXXXXX` and removes it at exit and on SIGINT/SIGTERM (one handler for all folders of a process); about 215 `mkdtemp*(tmpdir(), ...)` calls in 135 test files were moved to it, and `tests/lib/census.test.mjs` fails on any `mkdtemp*` call in a test file that is not in its list (each with the reason it is safe: inside a base that is removed, under the fake-tool root that clean-temp prunes, ...). A run of `port-t2*`, `run6b-adapters`, `runtime-versions`, `worktree` and the fixture tests with a scratch `TMPDIR` left 0 folders (before: 14 adp-, 36 rv-bin-, 32 rv-proj-, 3 pl-lib- from three files). Folders made by `fixtures/*/selfcheck.mjs` (standalone scripts) are not covered. (5) CARRY-OVER from the review of #243 in `tests/core/batch-state.test.mjs`: (a) `finally` now stops and awaits the stand-in sessions before it removes `session.fifo` (the `3>"$1"` redirect of a session that had not reached it yet created a regular 0-byte file after the unlink; shown directly: that command in a folder without the file makes `-rw-r--r-- 0 session.fifo`); (b) the `awaitPipe` regression test writes through a read-write descriptor (opening a pipe `r+` never blocks), so a `head` that fails to start cannot hang the run; (c) the stale comment about the fake ending by itself is corrected. EVIDENCE: `tests/lib/prune.test.mjs` (rules on a fake file system, the claim-and-give-back instant through a seam between the rename and the second look, links and other users, dry run, throttle, `cached()` with an injected clock, `copyOf` retry, `copyTree`, and 4 pruners plus 4 copiers as real processes released together by a line on stdin, 80 consecutive runs without a failure) and `tests/lib/clean-temp.test.mjs` (names, links, other users, age, live pid, dry run, the whole command, SIGINT and SIGTERM of a real child); both run in the existing `tests/lib` leg. MUTATIONS (each restored; every one turned a test red, 38 of 38 after tests were added for the four that first survived: `removeTree` following a link, and the default cache not being pruned): the second look at the marker, `keep`, the 30-minute protection, the directory test, the user test, the tombstone age, the size cap, the size order, the throttle, the copy verification, the rebuild before the retry, the retry, the use recorded on a hit and on a copy, the default/explicit cache choice, the live-pid test, the age test, the dry run, the name list, the cache-link test, the signal handler, the swallowed signal, the `.pid` file; round 1: the copy verification of a plain folder, the `.git` skip and its exemption, the narrow name list, the `--tmpdir` refusal, `--hours` below 1, the fake-tool pid test and pruning, the census limit, the exit removal of `tempDir()`. ACCEPTED LIMITS: (i) a template idle for more than 30 minutes that is read at the same microsecond it is evicted costs that reader a rebuild (never a wrong copy, never a crash); (ii) the cap is soft, 2 GB is exceeded while more than that is in use within 30 minutes; (iii) `removeTree` works on paths: between its `lstat` and its `readdir` a folder of this user could be swapped for a link by another process of the same user (the temp folder is world-writable and sticky, so another user cannot rename ours); (iv) a prune that is killed between the rename and the removal leaves an `evict-*` folder that the next prune removes after an hour; (v) a build longer than an hour is treated as killed; (vi) `fixtures/*/selfcheck.mjs` make their own folders and are not covered; (vii) a `proofline-t-*` folder of a process that runs for more than the threshold without ever touching it carries no `.pid` and can be removed by a `clean-temp` run meanwhile (only `proofline-h-` bases record their process): use `--hours` of 6 or more while long runs are going, or run it between runs; the liveness test of a base is `kill(pid, 0)`: a reused pid keeps a dead run's folder until that pid is gone; (viii) the SIGTERM handler runs after the current synchronous code: a process busy in a long synchronous call dies later (the dispatcher kills with SIGKILL after 2 s); (ix) `--tmpdir` takes any folder not refused above, including a world-writable one without the sticky bit: the name list, the owner test and `lstat` still apply, but a name that matches in such a folder is removed. Constraint: no Windows host here; the prefix list and the pid test use only `lstat`, `process.kill(pid, 0)` and paths. Rejected: a timer or a background process for the pruning (a clock read and a process to leak); deleting by `du` of the whole temp folder (unsafe: not ours); a lease file taken before each copy with a claim of the marker by the pruner (written and dropped: renaming the marker inside the entry disturbs a copy that is already running, and a lease with check-then-act is not atomic with a folder rename). Confidence: medium-high. Scope-risk: low (test infrastructure only; the product reads none of it). Round 3 (independent review): `tests/core/scale.test.mjs` asserted on measured wall-clock time (a real `agent.sh` timed with `Date.now()`, a `sleep 0.6` stub, a regex on `1[0-9]{3} ms`), so it flipped under load; `measureMachine(ctx, { now, run })` and `proposeScale(ctx, { measure })` now take the clock, the runner and the measurement (defaults: the wall clock, a real start of `agent.sh`, the real measurement, so `proofline doctor --scale` behaves as before), the tests give `[400,200]`, `[500,250]` and `[500,251]` (the boundary of the reference sum), `[1200,600]` and `[1000,500]`, a fake clock proves the best-of-two choice, and exactly one test runs the real command and checks only the shape `\d+ ms`; no `sleep` is left. `tempDir()` removes with `removeTree` of `prune.mjs` (a folder a test made read-only with `chmod 0o500` no longer survives; before, it did every time), and `tests/lib/tempdir.test.mjs` (3 tests, real child processes released by a printed line) pins the read-only case and the SIGTERM and SIGINT exit status (`signal === sig`, folder gone). The census also flags `mkdtemp`/`mkdtempSync` used as a value (an alias) and a `mkdirSync` of a name built by hand under `tmpdir()`; imports, re-exports, destructured dynamic imports and comments are not flagged, the exception list stays explicit. `clean-temp` knows `dispatch.XXXXXX` (core/dispatcher.mjs) and `agent-status-block.XXXXXX` (core/statusblock.mjs), exactly six random characters, with the usual guards; the comment above `PREFIXES` is back where it belongs and says that the generic legacy words (origin, wiki, ui, qa, tp, up) are guarded by age, owner and the `.git` skip. MUTATIONS round 3 (each restored; each turned a test red): the reference of the start time, best-of-two taken as the larger, the injected clock ignored, the injected measurement ignored, `rmSync` instead of `removeTree` in `tempDir()`, the signal re-sent by `process.kill` removed (the child then keeps running: the test ends by its 20 s hang guard, which is a safety net and not a wait), the alias check, the hand-named-folder check, each new `clean-temp` name and the exact six characters. ACCEPTED LIMITS round 3: (x) a template folder with no `.built` marker and no builder in the copying process is copied without verification; it can only arise if a pruner removed the marker first, and the 20-run multi-process test never produced it.
