- **A255. Tool-call economy, second half (items 4 and 5): `proofline insights` reads `tools.jsonl`, and the Codex log reader (patch, 0.0.88; Part of #181; follows A235, A210, A211, A253).** What: (1) `proofline insights` has a TOOL CALLS section (and `tools` in `--json`): per role, per run and overall, the jobs, calls and result bytes per job, hook refusals and the top tools; the role table is the table the A235 measurement produced. Jobs without a readable log are counted apart (`unreadable`/`no-log`, `malformed`) and their counts are `n/a`, `12 (2/3)` when only some jobs had a log, never zero; rows are in byte order and the report does not depend on the order of the file. It reads only what the control plane wrote (`core/toolsinsights.mjs`): 64 KiB chunks, at most 200000 lines, a line over 64 KiB or not JSON is counted as corrupt and skipped, a record of another schema is counted, an unfinished last line is ignored, identifiers are reduced again, numbers must be safe non-negative integers, tool names are keys of a `Map` (`__proto__` is a name), at most 50 tools per record and 100 per row. No new option or command name: the help line and `docs/guides/daily-use.md` name the section in one phrase. (2) `readCodexToolStats` in `core/toolstats.mjs` returns the same `ToolStats` for a Codex rollout log and `submit` writes the record for a Codex worker. WHERE THE LOG IS (checked on this machine, codex-cli 0.167, 163 logs from 0.163 to 0.167): `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<local time>-<session id>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line `{timestamp, ordinal, type, payload}`; a tool call is a `response_item` with `payload.type` `custom_tool_call` (or `function_call`), `call_id` and `name`, its result a `*_output` item with the same `call_id` and `output` (a list of `input_text` blocks or a string). The dispatcher does not record the path and no Codex hook writes a `.started` file (that is the Claude subagent hook), but a command the model runs has `CODEX_THREAD_ID` = the session id (A211), so `submit` looks for the file by that id: a UUID (so no path can come from it), an exact name match in a listing of the day folders of the last 4 days (local and UTC day), no symlink, `$CODEX_HOME` else `$HOME/.codex` (the dispatcher sets both for a Codex worker). A log that is not found gives `log: unreadable` and a new last key `reason` (`no-session-id`, `no-codex-home`, `no-rollout`; read failures `read-error`, `too-large`, `not-a-file`, `line-too-long`, `bad-line`, `no-events`; the Claude reader gives reasons too); `schema` stays `proofline.tools/1` (A210: no compatibility layer). Counted as for Claude: calls once per id, result bytes = UTF-8 length of the output text, a refusal = `blocked by PreToolUse hook` in the first 300 characters of a result (the Codex hook message; 228 of 4093 results on this machine), reductions to `[A-Za-z0-9._+:-]` and 64 characters, 40 tools then `other`, an unfinished last line ignored, 128 MiB cap (read in chunks, a line over 32 MiB is `unreadable`). (3) Carry-over of the #244 review: the duplicated clean-temp test is gone; the tempdir test helper rejects when the child exits before its first line (and the test has a timeout) instead of hanging; the census catches `mkdirSync` of any path that starts at `tmpdir()`, also through a variable (`const t = tmpdir(); mkdirSync(t + '/x')`) and with a fixed name. MEASURED (deterministic: a loop of `readCodexToolStats` (the command is in the pull request) over every `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` of the maintainer's machine, 0.6 s): 163 logs, all `ok`, 4094 calls, 17,912,697 result bytes, 228 refused calls; tools `exec` 4059, `wait` 33, `js` 2. An independent line scan of the same files (a script that counts `function_call`/`custom_tool_call` items and results whose text holds the hook phrase) gives the same 4094 calls and 228 refusals. Why: the A235 measurement existed only as a one-off table; the maintainer reads the per-role tool cost where the other costs are. Accepted limits: Codex names almost every command `exec`, so `by_tool` for Codex says little about the commands (the bytes and the count are the signal); a call without a `call_id` (web search) is not counted; a session older than 3 days at `submit`, a Codex lead without `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (started other than by Codex) or a `CODEX_HOME` that the model's shell does not inherit gives `unreadable` with a reason, never a count; the record is written while the session runs, so the `submit` call itself has no result yet (0 bytes); the lead's own session log is still not recorded (item 3 of #181); the old tools.jsonl lines have no `reason` key (insights does not read it). No hook, guard, gate or Core invariant was touched. EVIDENCE (deterministic; `node orient.mjs origin/main`, below; no model run): per role, bytes of what the old text sent an agent to open (the linked schema file plus the validator script) against what the new commands print: reviewer 29,699 to 2,896 (-90.2%), security reviewer 20,815 to 3,091 (-85.2%), verifier 11,593 to 1,139 (-90.2%), QA 20,049 to 841 (-95.8%); total 82,156 to 7,967 (-90.3%). The command: a 20-line script that sums `git show <ref>:<path>` for the four schema-plus-script pairs and the length of `node <script> --schema` and `--help`; it is in the pull request text. READ THE NUMBER AS AN UPPER BOUND OF THE SAVING PER JOB THAT OPENED BOTH FILES, not a measured saving: whether a job opens the schema or the source is the agent's habit (A235 counted the bytes of skill-file reads, not which file); the saving per run is unknown until `proofline insights` (A255) shows the tool-result bytes per role of a run made with 0.0.89, and one run is noise (A235). TESTS (`tests/skills/orientation-help.test.mjs`, 18 tests, 0.80 s, twice 0.818 and 0.798 s, slowest test 153 ms): per script `--help` equals the header read by a second method, every `--option` the script reads is named in the help and every option the help names is read, a usage error points at `--help`; QA help names every category of `CATEGORIES`; `--schema` equals the projection of the schema file and is under a third of the file and a quarter of the script; a known-answer test of the renderer (`$ref`, allOf of refs, oneOf, enum, const, pattern, conditionals, open objects, minLength); PINNED AGAINST THE REAL VALIDATOR: a valid document is walked along the schema, for every object `--schema` prints each key in order with `*` exactly when the schema requires it and the enum values joined, the validator refuses the document when that required key is deleted, refuses a value outside each enum, and for EVERY closed object of the schema the test asserts what the legend says: proof-review refuses an injected unknown key in each of them, exploit-proof in exactly five (the walk runs over a traced and a reproduced document with a suspicion, so `reproduction` and the suspicions are exercised) and accepts it in the others; a test on the real schemas pins that the `target` head rule (a node-level `if/then/else`, `else` branch included) and the `min1` of `path` are printed; the known-answer test also covers `format`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, array `minItems` and a node-level `if/then/else` (in the real schemas `format` occurs only in proof-review's `generated_at`, `maximum` and `exclusiveMinimum` in neither, so those two are pinned by the synthetic schema only); the skill texts name the commands. REVIEW ROUND 1 (the renderer printed conditionals only from `allOf`, so the `else` branch of exploit-proof's `target` head rule was missing; array `minItems` was never printed; the legends were inexact): fixed, and the new pins turned red under (failing tests): node-level `if` not printed (2), `else` not printed (2), `$ref` in a conditional left unresolved (2), `format` not printed (3), `maximum` not printed (2), `exclusiveMinimum` not printed (1), array `minItems` not printed inline (2) or on a `see` line (1), exploit-proof validator no longer refusing unknown keys in `reproduction` (1) or in suspicions (2), the validator starting to refuse them in `target` so the legend would lie (2), either legend reworded (1 each). The lead's combined step command and the lead's own session log, item 3 of #181 (patch, 0.0.91; Part of #181; follows A235, A255, A256, A257, A210).** MEASUREMENT FIRST: the lead is 31% of the calls of a STANDARD run (A235). The real sequences, read from the lead skill's Flow table and from a STANDARD e2e transcript on the maintainer's machine (45 lead calls; the model already chained some with `;`): `classify`, `branch`, `baseline`, then `next` (4); `freeze`, `freshness`, `next` (3); `handoff IMPLEMENTING`, `next` (2); `handoff IMPLEMENTED`, `tier`, `pipeline`, `next` (4); each a separate process whatever the tool call. It stops, with the `next` output as its last block, at the first `next=` that is anything else, at several `next=` lines, at a repeated command, after 8 steps; and at the first command that fails: that command's output and exit status, nothing after it runs. Both reached class COMPLEX, tier `full`, the eight gates, a `plan` stop answered by the harness (one reply before; two after, the plan was re-asked at a refreeze). PROTOCOL (A235's, with the deviations below): the numbers are read from the Claude Code transcripts of the run, with the CURRENT reader `core/toolstats.mjs` (`readToolStats`) applied to BOTH versions, so the two columns use one counting rule (a call is a `tool_use` counted once by id; result bytes are the UTF-8 text of the matching `tool_result`; a call whose result starts `PreToolUse:<Tool> hook error` is a refusal); the lead is the run's session transcript, a specialist job is one subagent transcript, its role from the `agentType` of its `.meta.json`. For AFTER the same run was cross-checked with `proofline insights` (TOOL CALLS section, from `.agents/local/metrics/tools.jsonl`): 27 jobs, 561 calls, 2,128,209 result bytes, 48 refused (the transcript reading: 26 transcripts, 545 calls, 2,030 KiB, 47 refused; the two differ because `tools.jsonl` is a snapshot at each `submit`, the verifier has three step records for two transcripts, and the lead record is taken when the run ends). BEFORE has no `tools.jsonl`, so only the transcript reading exists for it. RESULT (n = 1 each; calls / result KiB / refused by a hook): TOTAL 583 / 1,925 / 68 before, 545 / 2,030 / 47 after (KiB = bytes/1024 throughout; ratio calls 0.93, bytes 1.05, refusals 0.69). SPECIALISTS ONLY 486 / 1,706 / 63 before, 437 / 1,730 / 45 after (0.90, 1.01, 0.71). PER ROLE (jobs; calls; result KiB; refused), before then after: reviewer 11; 253; 941; 34 then 11; 224; 979; 24. lead 1; 97; 218; 5 then 1; 108; 300; 2. implementer 2; 90; 192; 8 then 2; 54; 179; 4. qa 3; 44; 199; 6 then 4; 54; 184; 8. security reviewer 1; 27; 79; 6 then 1; 21; 74; 1. verifier 2; 25; 84; 4 then 2; 26; 71; 1. data architect 1; 15; 61; 1 then 1; 11; 57; 1. architect 1; 13; 55; 1 then 1; 18; 81; 1. designer 1; 10; 54; 2 then 1; 15; 59; 3. explorer 2; 9; 43; 1 then 2; 14; 47; 2. WALL-CLOCK (the harness's own `summary.txt`, lead calls): before 3,480 s in all (leads 869 + 2,592 s, one reply), after 2,636 s (867 + 709 + 1,053 s, two plan replies: the plan was approved twice, a refreeze); 0.76 of before. SAME FINAL STATE? NO, and that matters for every number above. BEFORE stopped with the run in `IMPLEMENTED`, `fix_round=2` of 2, `escalation=yes`, gate `REVIEW_TESTS` `stale` (all other gates `pass`), and the lead asked the user to decide: it had used both fix rounds. AFTER reached `handoff=DONE` (`CODE_DONE`), `fix_round=1`, `escalation=no`, every gate `pass` (`REVIEW_RULES:contract` and `REVIEW_DATA:migration` reported unsupported in the report, not as a full proof). Both ran 11 reviewer jobs and 2 implementer jobs, both left `db_unchanged=yes`. So the runs did not do the same work: BEFORE spent a second fix round and did not finish, AFTER did finish; this is the model's path, not necessarily the versions'. WHICH ITEMS PLAUSIBLY CONTRIBUTED (counted from the same transcripts, not proof): the refusals fell from 68 to 47 and the specialist refusals from 63 to 45 (item 1, A257 refusal texts, and the `plan-section`/`config-get` hook fix of A235; the refusals of the workers are what those two changes aim at); `diff-digest` (A235) was run 17 times (reviewer 13, verifier 3, security reviewer 1; two further `Write` calls only mention the word and are not counted), never before it existed, and the verifier made 15 `agent.sh` calls before against 11 after; the `--help`/`--schema` of the validators (item 2, A256) were used 7 times (reviewer 4, QA 1, security reviewer 1, other 1) against 2 before (QA 1, other 1), yet commands that open `.agents/skills/` were not fewer (reviewer 65 before, 73 after; all roles 138 before, 166 after (counted as tool calls whose Bash command, or for another tool the JSON of its input, contains the text `.agents/skills/`, once per `tool_use` id; a count over Bash commands only gives 135 and 165, reviewer 63 and 72)), so item 2 shows no saving of bytes in this run, the result bytes are 5% higher after (the lead's own bytes are 218 KiB before and 300 KiB after); `agent.sh advance` (item 3, A258) was run 4 times by the lead (4 distinct `advance` commands, some chained with other commands; a count of tool calls that contain it gives 3), whose calls rose from 97 to 108 (its `agent.sh next` calls 16 before, 18 after; the lead ran in three sessions after two plan replies): no lead saving is visible in n = 1; items 4 and 5 (`insights`, the Codex reader) are measurement tools and cannot lower a count. READING: the total calls fell 7% and the specialists' 10%, the refusals fell by almost a third, the result bytes did not fall, the wall-clock fell 24%, and the AFTER run finished where the BEFORE run escalated. Nothing here is a proven saving: the 7% is far inside the run-to-run spread A235 measured (342-435 calls, mean 385, in five smoke runs of ONE version), the two runs took different paths (a second fix round in one only), and one run each cannot separate the versions from the model. ACCEPTED LIMITS: (1) n = 1 per version, no distribution, no confidence interval; (2) model variance is large and the paths differ (see the final state), so the ratios are an observation, not an effect; (3) model, host and time differ from A235's corpus (the lead here is Opus under the balanced profile, the smoke used haiku; the Claude Code build and the model snapshot are whatever the machine had on 2026-11-12; the machine runs other work); (4) BEFORE uses the shell harness of its own commit and AFTER the Node harness, the task, replies and profile are the same files in both; (5) the reader is the current `toolstats.mjs` for both, so a difference of counting rule is excluded, but a worker that is resumed is one transcript and the `tools.jsonl` figures (561 calls) differ from the transcript figures (545) by the snapshot rule above; (6) Codex workers were not measured (the `claude` configuration), as in A235; (7) wall-clock includes model latency and the machine's load and is not a property of the version. DEVIATIONS FROM A235's PROTOCOL: A235 measured earlier fixtures' transcripts (the corpus) and five smoke runs on haiku before and two after; this is the e2e COMPLEX task, once each, on the lead model the harness prescribes, and it reports the lead beside the specialists; A235 read the BEFORE transcripts with the reader introduced by the same change, and so does this (the reader of 0.0.91 on the 0.0.68 transcripts). No infrastructure retry was needed: both runs were valid on the first attempt. NO transcript, task text or secret is copied into the repository: only the aggregate numbers above. Rejected: repeating each run until the numbers looked better, or averaging a re-run (a second sample would be a distribution of two; the lead asked for one run each, and a re-run only for infrastructure failure); counting the BEFORE run with the A235 corpus script (not kept; the reader in the repository is the reproducible one). Confidence: high that the numbers are what the transcripts hold; low that any of the differences is caused by the versions. Not-tested: a second run of either version, the `mixed` and `codex` configurations, STANDARD and CRITICAL classes. WHAT THE LEAD SHOULD DO WITH IT: close the acceptance wish of #181 item 6 only as "measured once, with the caveats above"; the repeatable thing to read after any release is `proofline insights` on a real run. Reproduce: `E2E_ROOT=<scratch> node tests/e2e/run.mjs COMPLEX claude --keep` on a checkout of each sha (the BEFORE sha uses `sh tests/e2e/run.sh COMPLEX claude --keep`), then run `readToolStats` of `control-plane/agents/scripts/core/toolstats.mjs` over the lead transcript and the `subagents/*.jsonl` beside it.
- **A260. Windows port W1: the probe takes a `tests` input, and one Windows-aware path helper removes the largest failure cluster (patch, 0.0.93; Part of #165; follows A254, A252, A251, A250, A242, A210).** WHAT: package W1 of the Windows port, the last package set of epic #165 (user decision of 2026-11-11: native Windows is not deferred; target: windows-latest runs the core's Node tests and the Node invariant suite and passes, then the Windows hook and core jobs become gates of the nightly run; later packages do the rest). TWO PARTS. (A) PROBE INPUT: `workflow_dispatch` input `tests` of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (space-separated test files, globs or folders under `tests/`; empty = every leg in full, as before). The `windows-core-probe` step is now `node tests/ci/windows-probe.mjs` (matrix and job names unchanged; the logic is a Node script, the step is one line, A242). The input reaches the script only as `$PROBE_TESTS` (an `env:` of the step; `inputs.tests` appears once in the workflow, nowhere inside a command), is checked by the pure function `selectTests` (only letters, digits, `_ . - / *` and spaces; every entry starts with `tests/`, has no `.` or `..` or empty segment and no leading `-`, ends in `.mjs` or is a folder meaning its `*.test.mjs`; at most 64 entries of 200 characters; one bad entry refuses the whole input, exit 2) and goes to `node --test` as separate arguments with no shell. The selected files are shared by the four core legs with `--test-shard=k/4`; files under `tests/invariants-node` go to the `invariants` leg; a leg without a file prints SKIPPED. Every leg prints `PROBE-RESULT leg=... pass=... fail=... duration_s=...` (the counts and `duration_ms` of the runner's own closing summary, so no clock is read) and adds a row to the job summary; read a round with `gh run view <id> --job <job> --log`. It stays manual (`workflow_dispatch` only) and `continue-on-error`. (B) CLUSTER 1, "ARTIFACT path must be inside the run" (about 80 direct and 90 chained failures of the first probe, A251). CAUSE: the containment checks of `record` (ARTIFACT), `evidence_cite_check`, `unsupported_evidence_check` compared `realpathSync` results as POSIX text (`real.startsWith(`${runReal}/`)`); on Windows `realpathSync` answers `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...` with backslashes, so every file inside the run was refused; `diff-digest` (`real !== `${runReal}/reports``) and `discard-stray` (`real !== `${dir}/evidence``) had the same comparison, and an absolute ARTIFACT given as `C:\...` was not seen as absolute. FIX (one helper, `core/pathin.mjs`): `realpathPosix` (win32: `realpathSync.native`, which also expands 8.3 short names such as `RUNNER~1`, then forward slashes and an upper-case drive letter; elsewhere exactly `realpathSync`), `inside(base, child, platform)` (child strictly inside base on a whole path component; the base itself is not inside; no `..` is interpreted because real paths are already resolved; case ignored only on win32) and `isAbsoluteInput` (leading `/`; on win32 also `C:\x`, `C:/x`, UNC). `realOf` (resultutil), `record`, `diffdigest` and `runcmds` use them; symbolic-link and realpath rules are unchanged (a link that leaves the run is still refused: tested on POSIX with a real link). POSIX behaviour: byte-identical; `tests/core/pathin.test.mjs` compares `inside` with the old `startsWith(`${base}/`)` over a table (the only difference is the impossible empty remainder), checks that every refused path stays refused (sibling prefix, base itself, parent, other case, other drive, UNC share, link out of the run), `realpathPosix` equals `realpathSync` through links, and runs the Windows rules with the platform and realpath as parameters. TESTS: `tests/core/pathin.test.mjs` (6 tests, 20 ms) and `tests/ci/windows-probe.test.mjs` (10 tests incl. 45 malicious or malformed inputs, 40 ms); both run twice with `TMPDIR` unset, `/tmp` and a scratch folder: same result, 64-68 ms for both files together. MUTATION CHECKS (all red, then reverted): `inside` without the `/` boundary (5 of 5 tests of pathin red); `inside` case-insensitive everywhere (2 red); the existing record/digest/lifecycle suites (121 tests) stay green on this machine. WINDOWS EVIDENCE (windows-latest, the CI is the oracle; selection = the 36 files whose tests showed the message in the A251 logs plus `tests/invariants-node`; core counts are the sum of the four legs, durations are the slowest leg; every round is one `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref feat/165w1-probe-input-paths -f tests=...`):

  | round | head | change | core pass / fail | invariants pass / fail | duration (slowest leg / invariants) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | `48388fc0` | baseline (the selection in one leg: the input, no fix) | 150 / 284 | 1 / 7 | 728 s / 35 s |
  | 1 | `b9033936` | `pathin.mjs` in record, resultutil, diffdigest, runcmds | 338 / 96 | 8 / 0 | 704 s / 49 s |
  | 2 | `2d12ef74` | `isAbsoluteInput` for a Windows absolute ARTIFACT | 339 / 95 | 8 / 0 | 698 s / 78 s |

  "ARTIFACT path must be inside the run" occurs in no log of rounds 1 and 2. The 95 failures left in the selection are other clusters (a different cause each; listed for the following packages, none fixed here): tests that assume POSIX paths or programs (`/etc/hosts`, `/dev/null`, `sed`, `sh` recipes in `run6-*`, `run4a-records`, `run4c-gates`), the delivery/merge flow (`run6-merged`, `run6-cifix`, `run6-plan`: "delivery of LC stopped before commit/merge", `git push ... does not appear to be a git repository`), "could not archive the records of LC" (`lifecycle-s2`, `run4b-lifecycle`), `freeze verified: LC` (`lifecycle-s1`, `lifecycle-s2`, `gates-s4`), `ENOENT mkdir` (`risk-s2`), mixed-separator expectations (`run4a-records`: `...\worktrees\W-1/.agents/scripts`). FULL PROBE (empty `tests`, head `2d12ef74`, run 43142005482): core 1/4 417 pass / 260 fail (983 s), core 2/4 424 / 195 (779 s), core 3/4 393 / 186 (2,552 s: the dispatch tests wait for timeouts), core 4/4 486 / 150 (696 s), invariants 8 / 0 (53 s); core total 1,720 pass / 791 fail against 1,473 / 980 in the A251 run (counts include sub-tests), and the invariants suite is green on Windows (1 / 7 before). REMAINING CLUSTERS of the full probe (largest first; message counts, first files): path-format assertions `Expected values to be strictly equal` (96; base, cli-help, decide, doctor-fresh, install-init); `ENOENT open/lstat` (37; batch-plan, doctor-fresh, install-init, verify-fixes, batch-state); `timed out waiting` (23; dispatch, dispatch-watchdog); deep-equal path lists (20; hgit, run6-merged, toolstats, verify-fixes, dispatch); `mkdtemp '\tmp\proofline-fp.XXXXXX'` in fingerprint (22; dispatch, port-t2-fingerprint, fingerprint); `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'/'includes'/'split')` (23; risk-s1, cli-help, doctor-fresh); `init failed: NaN` and `The "string" argument must be of type string` (17; doctor-fresh, install-init, install-upgrade, cli); delivery/merge flow (run6-merged, run6-cifix, run6-plan); hgit submodule/driver premises (hgit); `git init ... unable to access '\\.\nul'` (4; insights-front); `Traceback` python in approve-tty (4); `reading 'PreToolUse'` (3; user-decisions-1108); `gh auth login` (2; friction). ACCEPTED LIMITS: the other clusters stay red; the helper covers the five sites that showed the message, not every `startsWith` in the core (the next rounds find the rest by their failures, not by reading); `realpathSync.native` on win32 is untried beyond the CI rounds above; case is ignored on win32 only and for ASCII letters only (`asciiLower`; `toLowerCase` would fold the Kelvin sign U+212A to `k`, which NTFS does not; tests with U+212A, U+0131, U+017F; mutation to `toLowerCase` goes red); remaining limit: a directory with the per-directory case-sensitive flag that holds both `Run` and `RUN` can confuse the case-insensitive compare (it needs an attacker who creates such siblings next to the run); `tests/*` or `tests/**` in the probe input puts the invariant files into the core shards, and together with `tests/invariants-node` they run twice; the probe script forces `--test-reporter=spec` (the log format differs from the old default, the counts are read from the same closing summary); 'the selection matched nothing' covers both a missing file and a file without tests; the spawn options (`shell: false`) and the failing leg for a missing file are pinned by tests; a drive-letter case difference between the run folder and a cited file is accepted on win32 only (case-insensitive file system); the 16 skill scripts' resolver and `.out-of-scope/deferred.md` are untouched (a later package). Windows stays unclaimed in the README.
- **A261. Windows port W2: path-format failures of the Windows probe (patch, 0.0.94; Part of #165; follows A260, A254, A252, A250, A210).** WHAT: package W2 of the Windows port, clusters (1) path-format assertions (`Expected values to be strictly (deep-)equal`, about 116 tests of the W1 probe) and (2) `init failed: NaN` and `The "string" argument must be of type string` (about 17). The probe is the oracle; every round is one `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref feat/165w2-path-format -f tests=...`. ROOT CAUSES AND FIXES. (2) was one cause: `bin/proofline` is a Node script with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` line, and Windows cannot start it by its path (`spawnSync` answers ENOENT, `status` null, `stdout` null, so `stdout + stderr` is NaN). `tests/lib/winpath.mjs` `launch(program, args)` starts it as `node <script>` on win32 and unchanged elsewhere (the shebang and the execute bit stay covered on POSIX); `frontend-lib` (`pl`, `plAsync`), `cli`, `install-init`, `githooks-trust`, `entry`, `run6-netdropped` and `cli-help` use it, and `sb.pl` now reports a spawn error instead of NaN. (1) was several causes, decided one by one. PRODUCT (user-visible or stored values): `core/pathin.mjs` gains `localRemote` (win32: a drive-path remote that git answers with its `..` still in it, `C:\\proj\\.agents\\local\\worktrees\\LC/../proj-lo.git`, is folded and made the real path; identity elsewhere; used by `originUrl`), `posixForm` (win32: drop the `\\?\` prefix, upper-case ASCII drive, forward slashes; identity elsewhere, where a backslash is a file name character), `samePath` (`===` off Windows; on win32 `posixForm`, no trailing slash, ASCII case folded; the rule of `inside`) and `eolText` (win32: CRLF to LF); `isAbsoluteInput` (A260) now decides what was `startsWith('/')`: the Claude and Codex home folders (`leadlog`, `toolstats`: `HOME` is `C:\Users\x` there, so every transcript lookup answered `no-claude-home`), the session-log path of `metricsStep` (two sites; the tool record said `no-log`) and a local origin in `platform` (`C:\x.git` was taken for a host); `worktree-add`, `rwMain` and a relative origin (`originUrl`) print `realpathPosix` (long names instead of `RUNNER~1`, forward slashes; `realpathSync` elsewhere); `core.hooksPath` equal to the shipped folder is recognised through `realpathPosix` and `samePath` (the same folder spelled with an 8.3 name or another case was reported as foreign); the platform-tool resolver (`resolveToolIn`, the PATH filter of `cleanToolEnv`, `caFileProblem`) tests absolute paths with `isAbsoluteInput` instead of `startsWith('/')` (on Windows every PATH entry was dropped, so the first `git ls-remote --get-url` of a delivery plan found no `git` and pinned an empty `origin_effective`, which made every later `deliver-merged` refuse with `origin changed since the summary was approved`); `originPushCmd` compares the origin with `localRemote` of the stored text; the version line of `node`, `claude`, `codex` goes through `eolText` (doctor printed `v22.13.0?`, the CR shown as `?`). TEST (only the test is POSIX-biased): `posix()` on the expected or observed side where the product joins with `/` and the test with `path.join` (leadlog, toolstats-codex, argv0, cli-help, hgit-guard keys, batch-lib `real`), `hooksPath` `NUL` for `/dev/null` (hgit), `path.basename` for a relative origin, node's own `symlinkSync` for the launcher links (the MSYS `ln -s` makes a copy), no execute-bit assertion on NTFS, the MSYS signal status (15 << 8) accepted as non-zero, `..` behind a link accepted on Windows (the OS folds `..` in the text; the project's own script is named, as its real path). NO product security check was weakened: containment, ancestor and run-relative checks are untouched; `isAbsoluteInput` only recognises more host-absolute inputs. POSIX BEHAVIOUR is byte-identical: `tests/core/pathin.test.mjs` compares the new expressions with the old (`startsWith('/')`, `/^\/.*\.jsonl$/`, the local-origin regular expression) over a table of 18 inputs, `posixForm`/`samePath`/`eolText` are the identity or `===` for linux and darwin, and the full local run (3,066 tests of `tests/ci`, `tests/enforcement`, `tests/core`, `tests/invariants-node`, `tests/lib`: 3,059 passed, 2 failed, 5 skipped) found two tests that this change broke, which the fix round repaired (`hgit-guard` listed `proc.eolText` as an unregistered spawn: the helper moved out of `proc.mjs`; `fixtures/TREES.sha256` regenerated with `node tests/fixtures/trees.mjs --update`, one digest, `insights`). TESTS: `tests/lib/winpath.test.mjs` (2 tests), `tests/core/pathin.test.mjs` (+3 tests: `posixForm`/`samePath`, the old-versus-new table, `localRemote`), `tests/core/base.test.mjs` (+1, `eolText`); run twice with `TMPDIR` unset, `/tmp/w2tmp` and a scratch folder: same results, 55-60 ms for winpath, 61 ms for pathin, 0.2 ms for the eolText test. MUTATION CHECKS (all red, then reverted): `samePath` case-folding everywhere (pathin red), `posixForm` rewriting backslashes everywhere (pathin red), `eolText` rewriting CRLF everywhere or dropping a lone CR (base red), `launch` always through node (winpath red), `localRemote` without the platform gate (pathin red). WINDOWS EVIDENCE (windows-latest; core counts are the sum of the four legs, the duration is the slowest leg; the file lists differ per round, so the counts are not comparable between rows):

| round | head | change | files | pass / fail | slowest leg |

| 1 (43153152278) | 17d7dc82 | `launch` in frontend-lib, `isAbsoluteInput` at the home, log-path and local-origin sites, `rwMain`, test expectations | 26 | 268 / 157 | 515.8 s |
| 2 (43155242886) | 1aba97f3 | `launch` in cli, install-init, githooks-trust; `eolText`; `samePath` for hooksPath | 26 | 275 / 151 | 600.1 s |
| 3 (43157584468) | 90eef4a0 | `posix` in leadlog, toolstats-codex, argv0, cli-help; `originUrl` real path | 16 | 197 / 54 | 309.9 s |

| 5 FULL (43164594702) | e609ff3a | version 0.0.94, trees | all | core 1,866 / 654 (462/220, 464/156, 439/143, 501/135), invariants 8 / 0 | 2,572.0 s (core 3/4) |

RESULT: the two clusters are gone from the probe (`init failed: NaN` 0, `must be of type string` 0; the strict-equality failures that remain are 66 messages, all of other clusters: `sh`-script programs that Windows cannot start by name (status 127 or null), signals, fake runtimes, `/tmp` in the fingerprint). The core went from 1,720 / 791 to 1,866 / 654. REMAINING (largest first, unique tests of the full probe; none belongs to this package): (a) port rigs and delivery/merge flow (`port-t3-core`, `port-t3-rig`, `tests/lib/harness.mjs`: `origin changed since the summary was approved (was 'C:\\...', now 'C:\\...'; git contacts '...', was '')`, `delivery of LC stopped before commit`, `could not archive the records` (GNU `tar` takes `C:` for a host)) about 310; (b) fingerprint `mkdtemp '\tmp\proofline-fp.XXXXXX'` about 158; (c) fake `sh` runtimes and tools (status 127 or null: dispatch, buildrecord, tree, verify-fixes, cli-agent-path, doctor-fresh, install-init, run4c-probes, exec-policy) about 75; (d) hgit premises (`test premise: a plain status runs the submodule's driver`) 25; (e) timeouts (`dispatch-watchdog`) 23; (f) `Cannot read properties of undefined` in `tests/lib/harness.mjs` 13; (g) file names Windows cannot hold (control characters, quotes, backslashes: `verify-fixes`, `githooks-trust`) and `git` path expansion (`%(prefix)`), a few; (h) the ancestor check of the dispatch nonce has no `/proc` or `ps` on Windows (`decide`: `parentPid` answers null; the check fails closed). ACCEPTED LIMITS: no Windows host to run on besides CI; `Windows stays unclaimed in the README` (not touched); a `startsWith('/')` guard that REJECTS absolute paths (`art.startsWith('/')` in `submit`, `gatecmd`, `lifecycle`, `runstart`, `markdown`) still does not see `C:\x` as absolute on Windows; the later containment checks (`inside`, A260) refuse it, but the early message is wrong; left for the package that owns those commands. The 16 skill scripts and `.out-of-scope/deferred.md` are untouched (a later package).
